Gradually, this seemed to make a difference and I sensed that she was less depressed and more hopeful – she’d made some important connections with her past that allowed her greater insight into her present and seemed to make her feel she could shape her future differently.

在接下来的几周里，我们聊起了她童年的这些经历，以及她对母亲的一些感受是如何在我身上重现的。渐渐地，这似乎产生了一些影响，我感觉到她不再那么沮丧，反而更有希望了——她与过去建立了一些重要的联系，这让她对现在有了更深刻的理解，也让她觉得她可以以不同的方式塑造自己的未来。

Making links between one thing and another is the daily work of a psychoanalytic therapist. Threading together seemingly random thoughts, behaviour and events helps to make sense of a patient’s inner world and to bring some meaning to what is confusing and fragmented. Being alive to these links is perhaps the nearest we can get to apprehending the unconscious. That part of the mind that runs like an underground river shaping all we think, all we do and how we love.

建立事物之间的联系是精神分析治疗师的日常工作。将看似随机的想法、行为和事件串联起来，有助于理解患者的内心世界，并为那些混乱和支离破碎的事物赋予意义。觉察到这些联系，或许是我们最接近理解无意识的方式。无意识就像一条地下河流，塑造着我们的一切思想、行为和爱。

Unfortunately, patients, particularly early in their treatment, can sometimes be sceptical about these links and, at times, positively scornful. The idea that their conscious self isn’t necessarily in the driving seat can feel quite alarming. However, at some point in the therapy, there’s often a shift in attitude and that’s when genuine breakthroughs become possible. Patients then bring their own insights about their dreams, their pre-occupations and their day-to-day lives.

不幸的是，患者，尤其是在治疗初期，有时会对这些联系持怀疑态度，甚至嗤之以鼻。意识到自己的意识并非总是主导一切，这种想法可能会让他们感到非常不安。然而，在治疗过程中，患者的态度往往会发生转变，而真正的突破也正是在此时发生的。患者会带着他们对梦境、执念和日常生活的深刻见解来参与治疗。

I remember one patient who was extremely anxious when her long-term partner told her, now he was retired, that he wanted to buy a flat in London so that he could visit galleries and go to the theatre – pleasures he’d missed greatly since moving to the country. The couple lived in the middle of a national park, surrounded by mountains and lakes, and though my patient’s husband had often spoken of his desire for a London pied-à-terre, he had never acted on it. She had been sleepless all week and, despite her partner’s reassurance that he wanted her company on these trips, she felt convinced it was otherwise and that he was really telling her that this was a precursor to their relationship ending.

我记得一位病人，她的伴侣退休后告诉她，他想在伦敦买一套公寓，这样他就可以去美术馆和剧院——自从搬到乡下后，他就一直很想念这些乐趣。这让她非常焦虑。这对夫妇住在国家公园的中心地带，四周群山环绕，湖泊点缀。虽然我的病人的丈夫经常说他想在伦敦拥有一套公寓，但他从未付诸行动。她整整一周都没睡好觉，尽管她的伴侣一再保证说他希望她能陪同他一起去，但她仍然觉得并非如此，她觉得他其实是在暗示他们即将分手。

I was puzzled by the strength and depth of this anxiety. I couldn’t make head or tail of it until some weeks later when she began to talk about her parents’ separation and how it had followed a heated and protracted dispute over purchasing a villa in France. Her French father desperately wanted to spend some of his retirement back in his homeland but her English mother put her foot down and resisted fiercely. Her parents fought over this for a year and then abruptly divorced. Suddenly, the connection between this memory of her parents’ separation, which she’d found deeply traumatic, and her current worries about her own relationship became clear. And this link, which had hitherto been unconscious, helped her to understand her panic at her partner’s suggestion.

我当时对她焦虑的强度和程度感到困惑。直到几周后，她开始谈起父母的分居，以及他们因在法国购买别墅而爆发的一场旷日持久的激烈争吵，我才恍然大悟。她的法国父亲迫切希望在退休后回到故乡生活，但她的英国母亲坚决反对。父母为此争吵了一年，最终突然离婚。突然间，她意识到父母分居这段令她深受创伤的记忆，与她目前对自身感情的担忧之间存在着某种联系。而这种此前她并未意识到的联系，帮助她理解了自己为何会对伴侣的提议感到恐慌。

Both Jackson and Grace seemed similarly to be in a process of development, making connections between their pasts and their present challenges. Jackson had slowly emerged from his grief and now he’d met a woman he liked called Veronica. He had been bored at work for some time and, feeling more confident again, had applied for a new job and was thrilled when he got it. It was quite a promotion and meant that, at last, he was doing what he’d always wanted to do. The only issue was his hours were less flexible and his 9.30am appointment was no longer possible. Could I see him earlier, at 8.30am, he enquired? I told him I didn’t have an earlier time free but, as the session with him progressed, I thought to myself that Grace, being freelance, might be able to come an hour later. The following week, I asked her if she’d mind changing to 9.30am and she readily agreed.

杰克逊和格蕾丝似乎都处于类似的成长阶段，努力将他们的过去与当下的挑战联系起来。杰克逊慢慢走出了悲伤，现在他遇到了一个名叫维罗妮卡的女子，他很喜欢她。他之前一直对工作感到厌倦，但随着信心的恢复，他申请了一份新工作，并在被录用后欣喜若狂。这是一次相当大的晋升，意味着他终于可以做自己一直想做的事情了。唯一的问题是他的工作时间变得不那么灵活了，他原定的上午9:30的预约也无法实现了。他问我是否可以提前到8:30。我告诉他我没有更早的时间，但随着咨询的进行，我想格蕾丝是自由职业者，或许可以晚一个小时过来。下周，我问她是否介意改到9:30，她欣然同意了。

One morning, about three weeks after the swap, she came into her session flushed with anger. ‘That guy. That guy you see before me. The guy who used to come after me.’ She laughed scornfully. ‘What’s his problem? He always gives me a really dirty look and just now he shut the door on me as I was coming in. I presume it’s cos of him you asked me to change time?’

一天早上，大约在换班三周后，她怒气冲冲地走进诊室。“就是那家伙。就是你刚才看到的那个人。以前总是在我后面来的那个人。”她轻蔑地笑了笑。“他到底有什么毛病？他总是用那种很不友好的眼神瞪我，刚才我进来的时候他还把门关上了。我猜你让我换时间就是因为他吧？”

I was rather taken aback by this and didn’t respond immediately. Grace just sat there looking cross with her arms folded, challenging me.

我当时有点吃惊，一时没反应过来。格蕾丝就那样坐在那里，双臂抱胸，一脸不悦，仿佛在挑衅我。

‘Perhaps it feels as if I’ve put his needs first, Grace, and messed you around?’

“格蕾丝，你是不是觉得我一直把他的需求放在第一位，而让你感到很困扰？”

‘Well, you kinda have, haven’t you?’ She paused. ‘You got me to change times so it was more convenient for him.’

“嗯，某种程度上来说，你已经做到了，不是吗？”她顿了顿。“你让我改了时间，这样对他来说更方便。”

‘Was it inconvenient for you?’ I asked.

“给您带来不便了吗？”我问。

‘That’s not the point,’ she responded. ‘It’s just not fair of you to have got me to inconvenience myself for him. ’

“这不是重点，”她回答说，“只是你让我为了他而给自己添麻烦，这很不公平。”

I felt surprised and wrong-footed. The reasonable and emollient Grace had disappeared and, in her stead, sat this angry, demanding child.

我感到既惊讶又措手不及。那位通情达理、温柔体贴的格蕾丝不见了，取而代之的是一个愤怒、蛮横的孩子。

It took some time for Grace to calm down and for us to explore her feelings about the swap. It was clear that I hadn’t spent enough time checking out whether it was really OK for her; her tendency to be amenable and compliant with me hadn’t been properly explored and now she felt that, once again, her own needs had been overridden in favour of someone else’s.

格蕾丝花了些时间才平静下来，我们也花了些时间探讨她对这次交换的感受。很明显，我没有花足够的时间去了解她是否真的能接受；她一贯的顺从和听话的性格也没有得到充分的探究，而现在她感觉，自己的需求又一次被别人的需求所忽略了。

‘My mum always puts herself first. My father is a massive bloody narcissist and gets his own way … and here you are, doing the same thing.’

“我妈总是把自己的利益放在第一位。我爸是个十足的自恋狂，总是随心所欲……而你，现在也一样。”

I didn’t point out that her accusation was unfair and irrational: the swap wasn’t about my needs but about Jackson’s. I understood that at this moment, she felt as if I, like her parents, had somehow made her secondary.

我没有指出她的指责不公平、不合情理：交换孩子不是为了满足我的需求，而是为了满足杰克逊的需求。我明白，在那一刻，她觉得我就像她的父母一样，把她放在了次要位置。

After that, Grace began to start each session by talking about Jackson – she didn’t know his name but called him ‘Mr Big’. She’d come early and ring my buzzer, interrupting Jackson’s session despite my having asked her, as I asked all my patients, not to come more than ten minutes before the session time.

之后，格蕾丝每次开始咨询前都会谈论杰克逊——她不知道他的名字，但叫他“大先生”。她会提前到，按响我的门铃，打断杰克逊的咨询，尽管我像要求所有病人一样，也要求她不要提前超过十分钟到达。

‘How’s Mr Big, your favourite patient?’ she’d joke in a sing-song voice.

她会用一种唱歌似的语调开玩笑说：“你最喜欢的病人，大先生，最近怎么样了？”

But when I tried to explore her rivalry with him, she’d dismiss me and say she was only joking and not everything was that serious.

但当我试图探究她与他之间的竞争关系时，她却不以为然，说她只是开玩笑，并非所有事情都那么严重。

Some weeks later, Jackson was in the middle of talking about his fears about moving in with Veronica when the buzzer went. I glanced at the clock: it was 9.15am. I looked at Jackson, who said, rather bitterly, ‘She’s keen.’ I felt furious with her. This was intolerable and couldn’t go on.

几周后，杰克逊正说着他担心搬去和维罗妮卡同住的事，这时门铃响了。我瞥了一眼钟：早上9点15分。我看向杰克逊，他有些不高兴地说：“她很积极。” 我当时气得不行。这简直无法忍受，不能再这样下去了。

In the ten-minute break between the two of them I gathered myself and thought about what I was going to say, then I opened my door and beckoned Grace in. She took off her coat with her back to me and sat down, staring defiantly.

在他们两人交谈的十分钟空隙里，我整理了一下思绪，想了想自己要说什么，然后打开门，示意格蕾丝进来。她背对着我脱下外套，坐了下来，目光挑衅地盯着我。

‘Grace,’ I said, sounding calmer than I felt. ‘I need to be clear. You’re not to come early. I’ve asked before but if you continue to ring the bell early, then we’ll need to rethink your sessions.’ She looked at me anxiously. ‘I’ll have to move you to a different time,’ I explained.

“格蕾丝，”我说道，语气比实际感觉平静一些。“我需要说清楚。你不能提前来。我之前已经说过，但如果你继续提前按铃，我们就需要重新安排你的治疗时间了。”她焦虑地看着我。“我得把你的治疗时间改到别的地方，”我解释道。

‘But that is my time. The other time.’ Then she put her head down on her knees and burst into tears.

“但那是我的时间，另一个时间。”说完，她把头埋在膝盖上，嚎啕大哭起来。

After that session, Grace stopped coming early. It took some weeks to unpick what had been going on and we gradually understood that she’d been testing me to see whether I would reject her if she behaved badly. So when I had simply ‘told her off’, she’d felt hugely relieved because she’d feared her behaviour might result in my ‘sacking’ her. Gradually, it also emerged that this hostility she felt towards Jackson was connected to a belief that her mother had always favoured her brother – she believed that I preferred Jackson to her. She was able to acknowledge how jealous she felt of her sibling and this led to her connecting to long-forgotten feelings about his birth and how this had triggered her mother leaving her to go into hospital. This ancient hostility and fear, which was deep inside her and hard to reach, had led to this irrational resentment towards Jackson, whose name she didn’t even know.

那次谈话之后，格蕾丝就不再提前来了。我们花了几个星期才弄明白到底发生了什么，逐渐意识到她是在试探我，看看如果她表现不好，我会不会拒绝她。所以，当我只是简单地“训斥”她一下时，她反而感到如释重负，因为她害怕自己的行为会导致我“解雇”她。渐渐地，我们也发现她对杰克逊的敌意源于她一直以来认为母亲偏爱弟弟的想法——她觉得我更喜欢杰克逊而不是她。她能够意识到自己对弟弟的嫉妒，这让她想起了很久以前关于杰克逊出生的感受，以及母亲当年是如何离开她去医院的。这种深藏在她内心深处、难以触及的古老敌意和恐惧，导致了她对杰克逊——一个她甚至不知道名字的孩子——的非理性怨恨。

The work continued. Grace came regularly to her sessions and soon I began to hear about Marcus, whom she had met on a work trip. Months passed and the relationship seemed to be developing. She talked about their ups and downs and many times I thought she’d break the relationship off but gradually he became a fixture in her life. Rapunzel was letting down her hair and letting Marcus into her life.

工作仍在继续。格蕾丝定期来接受咨询，不久后我开始听到她提起马库斯，她是在一次出差中认识他的。几个月过去了，他们的关系似乎正在发展。她谈起他们之间的酸甜苦辣，有好几次我都以为她会结束这段关系，但渐渐地，马库斯成了她生活中不可或缺的一部分。就像长发公主放下了头发，敞开心扉接纳了马库斯。

Some months later, I’d just got back from holiday in America and, jet-lagged, I slept through my alarm. It was 8.31am and I hurried along Welbeck Street, late for Jackson, when I saw him outside, waiting. He lifted one arm in greeting and smiled warmly as I fiddled for my key.

几个月后，我刚从美国度假回来，时差还没倒过来，睡过了头。早上8点31分，我匆匆沿着韦尔贝克街往杰克逊家赶，眼看就要迟到了，这时我看到他正站在外面等我。我手忙脚乱地摸索着钥匙，他抬起一只胳膊跟我打招呼，脸上带着温暖的笑容。

‘I’ve got some news,’ he said as he disappeared into the loo.

“我有些消息要告诉大家，”说完，他便走进了洗手间。

I walked into my consulting room, straightened the cushions and soon Jackson came in, removing his jacket as he entered.

我走进咨询室，整理了一下垫子，杰克逊很快就进来了，进门时脱掉了外套。

He smiled. ‘Veronica’s pregnant!’

他笑了。“维罗妮卡怀孕了！”

Fifty minutes later he departed and I picked up my iPhone to read a message from Grace: Running late – Had to go to doctor.

五十分钟后他离开了，我拿起我的 iPhone，读了格蕾丝发来的消息：迟到了——得去看医生。

Twenty minutes later, the buzzer sounded and Grace appeared, pink-faced and sweaty from the journey.

二十分钟后，蜂鸣器响起，格蕾丝出现了，她脸颊通红，因为旅途劳顿而满头大汗。

‘Guess what? I’m pregnant!’ she announced.

“你们猜怎么着？我怀孕了！”她宣布道。

Freud theorised that there is probably no such thing as an accident or a coincidence. Whilst we may be ignorant of something at one level, at another level, feelings, ideas, events and experiences are always being unconsciously communicated and assimilated. Perhaps we ‘know’ things at many different levels? Sometimes we’re able to know fully and consciously whilst at other times, when ‘knowing’ might be too painful or our attention is elsewhere, we find ourselves in a state of ‘not knowing’.

弗洛伊德认为，或许根本不存在所谓的意外或巧合。虽然我们可能在某个层面上对某些事物一无所知，但在另一个层面上，感觉、想法、事件和经历却总是在无意识地传递和吸收。或许我们在许多不同的层面上都“知道”着某些事物？有时我们能够完全且有意识地了解，而有时，当“知道”可能过于痛苦或我们的注意力分散时，我们便会发现自己处于一种“不知道”的状态。

Was I particularly alert during this period? Did I notice confluences and concurrences that at other times I’m blind to? Or were all these coincidences simply that? Happenstance, random events coming together that had no meaning, neither mystical nor unconscious?

我在这段时间里是否格外警觉？我是否注意到了一些平时容易忽略的巧合和同时发生的事件？或者，所有这些巧合都仅仅是巧合而已？仅仅是偶然事件，是没有任何意义的随机事件，既非神秘的，也非无意识的？

Bear Learns about Beauty and the Beast

熊了解美女与野兽

A man called Bear came to see me because he was having a difficult time in his relationship. He sat down heavily on my sofa and stared at me dolefully until I encouraged him to tell me why he’d come. He seemed reticent and talked evasively about his partner and children and his job in IT, which he found dull but paid the bills. He had a lopsided grin when he could manage one, enormous brown hands and wild curly hair. He was rather attractive apart from the smell of damp sadness that emanated from him.

一个名叫贝尔的男人来找我，因为他感情出了问题。他沉重地坐在我的沙发上，忧郁地盯着我，直到我鼓励他告诉我他来的原因。他似乎很沉默寡言，说话也闪烁其词，只谈到他的伴侣、孩子和他在IT行业的工作——他觉得这份工作很枯燥，但至少能糊口。他咧嘴一笑时，笑容有些歪斜，一双棕色的大手和一头蓬乱的卷发。除了身上散发出的潮湿悲伤的气息，他其实挺有魅力的。

Eventually, I said, ‘It seems you have some difficulty telling me what is really troubling you.’

最后，我说：“看来你很难告诉我真正困扰你的是什么。”

He looked away and out of the window and said, ‘I can’t stand the way she sighs.’

他别过脸，望着窗外说：“我受不了她叹气的样子。”

‘Sighs?’ I asked. I wasn’t sure I’d heard correctly.

“叹气？”我问。我不太确定自己是否听清楚了。

He was silent again and then, raising his head, he nodded and said, ‘Yes, she sighs.’

他又沉默了一会儿，然后抬起头，点了点头说：“是的，她叹了口气。”

Though I encouraged him several times to tell me more, he seemed reluctant to expand and I heard nothing more about the sighing in that first session. As I travelled home on the bus I wondered what it could mean. I knew how my husband’s sighs could affect me, how alert I could be to this little signal from him that might indicate he was tired or perhaps displeased about something. And I knew that I could also be given to sighing and thought about how there was sometimes a kind of lovely relief in doing so.

虽然我多次鼓励他多说一些，但他似乎不太愿意详述，第一次咨询后，我再也没听到关于叹气的事。回家的路上，我一直在琢磨这究竟意味着什么。我知道丈夫的叹气会如何影响我，我多么敏锐地察觉到他发出的这个小信号，它可能表明他累了，或者对什么事不高兴。我也知道自己有时也会叹气，想到叹气有时也能带来一种美好的解脱感。

When Bear came back to see me the following week, he said, ‘I told my partner this evening that I was going off to see you. She was in the kitchen feeding the dog. I asked her if she wanted to come. She didn’t look up. She just sighed.’ He paused. ‘I wanted to hit her. I’m afraid I might hit her if she sighs like that again.’

贝尔下周来看我的时候，他说：“我今晚跟我伴侣说我要去看你。她当时正在厨房喂狗。我问她要不要一起来。她头也没抬，只是叹了口气。”他顿了顿，又说：“我真想打她。要是她再那样叹气，我怕自己真会打她。”

A shiver of alarm went through me; I could hear the rage and spite in his voice and I could hear it more loudly than I could hear his fear. I asked him what stopped him from hitting her and if he ever had. He shook his head and stared at his shoes.

我感到一阵惊恐袭来；我能听出他语气中的愤怒和怨恨，而且这比他的恐惧更加清晰。我问他是什么阻止了他打她，以及他是否曾经打过她。他摇了摇头，盯着自己的鞋子。

‘I’ve never hit her and I don’t think I ever would but sometimes I feel as though I’m going to explode into little pieces.’ And then he apologised for what he’d just said and reassured me that he wasn’t dangerous, that I needn’t worry.

“我从来没打过她，我想我以后也不会打她，但有时我感觉自己好像要爆炸成碎片了。”然后他为刚才说的话道歉，并向我保证他没有危险，我不用担心。

For the rest of the session, he talked in a monotone about his job and I suddenly felt tired and sleepy. Feeling sleepy is an exceedingly rare thing for me – mostly, when my patients talk, I’m fully there with them, attentive to everything they say and alert to how they look and how they react to the things I might suggest to them. I’m taking them in with my whole self and stretching out to connect with them. So, when I feel sleepy in a session, it’s something to take seriously and I ask myself what it means and whether my patient is unconsciously communicating something. From my own experience and from the wisdom of others, I’ve learnt that feeling sleepy can sometimes be a sign that the patient has a great deal of repressed anger and that the consequence of this repression is a general flattening of their manner and their behaviour, suppressing the livelier part of themselves. Obviously, in my reflections, I must exclude the obvious, such as my sleepiness being due to jet lag or a particularly bad night’s sleep, but neither of those were factors on that day with Bear. Towards the end of the session, I thought about how odd it was that he had started with such violence and yet now he seemed utterly lifeless and flat.

在接下来的咨询中，他用单调的语气谈论着他的工作，我突然感到疲倦和困倦。对我来说，犯困是极其罕见的——通常情况下，当我的病人说话时，我会全神贯注地倾听，认真聆听他们说的每一句话，留意他们的表情以及他们对我的建议的反应。我会全身心地投入，努力与他们建立联系。所以，当我在咨询过程中感到困倦时，我会认真对待，并思考这意味着什么，以及我的病人是否在无意识地传递着什么信息。根据我自身的经验以及他人的智慧，我了解到，感到困倦有时可能表明病人压抑了大量的愤怒，而这种压抑会导致他们举止和行为变得平淡，压抑了他们活泼的一面。显然，在我的反思中，我必须排除一些显而易见的因素，比如时差或前一晚睡眠不好导致的困倦，但那天和熊在一起时，这些都不是原因。临近结束时，我想到很奇怪，他一开始那么暴躁，现在却显得毫无生气，毫无生气。

‘I think you’re afraid of the violent feelings your wife stirs up in you and that you work hard to damp them down rather than understand what causes them,’ I suggested.

“我认为你害怕妻子在你心中激起的强烈情绪，所以你努力压制这些情绪，而不是去了解这些情绪的起因，”我建议道。

He nodded and said that he’d been told that before by the psychologist who’d helped him with his drinking. I was surprised because he hadn’t mentioned he’d had problems with alcohol but now he told me that his drinking had spiralled out of control after his first son was born and the previous year he’d spent six weeks in rehab away from the family. He’d been dry now for 14 months.

他点点头，说之前帮他戒酒的心理医生也跟他说过类似的话。我很惊讶，因为他之前没提过自己有酗酒问题，但现在他告诉我，自从第一个儿子出生后，他的酗酒问题就彻底失控了，去年他还在戒酒中心待了六个星期，远离家人。他现在已经戒酒14个月了。

‘Did your feelings about your wife’s sighing start after you stopped drinking?’ I asked.

我问：“你戒酒之后才开始注意到妻子的叹息吗？”

He nodded. The session was coming to an end and as he slowly gathered his things and left my office, I thought about his anger and wondered if he’d used alcohol to damp down his fury. Was something now coming to the surface in his relationship with his wife that had previously been masked when he was drinking?

他点了点头。会谈即将结束，他慢慢收拾东西离开我的办公室时，我想起了他的愤怒，心想他是不是用酒精来压抑怒火。是不是他和妻子的关系中，有些问题在他喝酒时被掩盖了，现在才浮出水面？

The following week, Bear came early and sat patiently outside my room for 20 minutes but when the session started, he seemed to have nothing to say and we sat in silence for some time. After a bit, his phone buzzed and he picked it up off the sofa where it sat beside him. I watched as he read the message before looking back at me.

接下来的一周，贝尔早早地来了，耐心地在我房间外坐了二十分钟。但咨询开始后，他似乎什么也没说，我们沉默了一会儿。过了一会儿，他的手机震动了一下，他从沙发上拿起放在身旁的手机。我看着他读完信息，然后才回头看向我。

‘She’s outside. She wants to come in.’ He looked at me, panicked, and for a moment I wondered who the hell was outside; it felt like someone dangerous, someone out to get him. Then it dawned on me – it was his wife.

“她在外面。她想进来。”他惊慌地看着我，我一时之间也纳闷外面到底是谁；感觉像是有什么危险人物，好像要害他似的。然后我突然意识到——那是他妻子。

‘What shall I say?’ he asked, his eyes wide with alarm.

“我该说什么呢？”他问道，眼中充满了惊恐。

‘Do you want her to come in?’ I asked.

“你想让她进来吗？”我问。

‘Don’t tell her what I told you,’ he said fiercely, rising from the couch. ‘I’m going downstairs to see her.’ And he got up and left.

“别把我跟你说的话告诉她，”他恶狠狠地说着，从沙发上站了起来。“我要下楼去看她。”说完，他就起身离开了。

I waited in my room, wondering what would happen next. I imagined her bursting into my office, demanding to know what was going on. The way he’d reacted to the text made me feel she must be quite scary. After a while, I heard voices outside and then footsteps on the stairs. My door opened and Bear reappeared, followed by a small, slight woman with beautiful brown eyes and curly brown hair, who smiled at me nervously as she took a seat. She was wearing a long, green dress peppered with tiny white flowers and as she sat down, I noticed her dainty brown feet and the tiny gold chain she wore around her ankle.

我在房间里等着，琢磨着接下来会发生什么。我幻想着她冲进我的办公室，质问我到底发生了什么事。他回复短信的方式让我觉得她一定很可怕。过了一会儿，我听到外面有人说话，然后是楼梯上的脚步声。门开了，贝尔又出现了，后面跟着一个身材娇小的女人，她有着漂亮的棕色眼睛和棕色卷发。她坐下时，略带紧张地朝我笑了笑。她穿着一条缀满白色小花的绿色长裙。她坐下时，我注意到她纤细的棕色脚，以及脚踝上戴着的那条细细的金链子。

‘I’m really sorry for just turning up. I felt bad about not coming last week when Bear asked.’ She paused, shook her curls and looked at me questioningly. ‘But obviously if it isn’t cool, I can split now.’ She looked from me to Bear with her head angled to the side, waiting expectantly for a sign whether she was welcome. How meek she seemed; so different from what I’d expected.

“真抱歉我突然来了。上周Bear邀请我的时候我没来，感觉很愧疚。”她顿了顿，甩了甩卷发，疑惑地看着我。“不过，如果这样不好，我现在就可以走了。”她歪着头，看看我，又看看Bear，期待着得到是否欢迎她的信号。她看起来多么温顺啊，和我想象中的完全不一样。

We talked for a while about what they wanted – did they both want couple therapy and was Bear comfortable with her being in the session? I said that I thought they needed to go away and think through what was best. Then they could let me know and we could see how to proceed.

我们聊了一会儿他们的想法——他们俩都想接受伴侣治疗吗？贝尔是否愿意陪同他们一起接受治疗？我说我觉得他们需要冷静下来好好想想什么才是最好的选择。之后他们可以告诉我结果，我们再看看下一步该怎么做。

She shook my hand as they left and apologised again for turning up without warning. I wondered if I’d see her again.

他们离开时，她和我握了握手，再次为不请自来而道歉。我不知道是否还能再见到她。

Three days later, Bear emailed me to say that Saffron wasn’t coming – she thought that he should continue with me on his own.

三天后，贝尔发邮件告诉我，萨弗伦不会来了——她认为他应该独自和我继续下去。

At the next session, I was quite taken aback. Bear looked different; wearing forest-green yoga pants, he suddenly seemed much less conventional.

下一次见面时，我着实吃了一惊。贝尔看起来判若两人；他穿着森林绿的瑜伽裤，突然间显得不再那么循规蹈矩了。

‘I’m really sorry about last week,’ he began. ‘I thought I wanted her to come and then I really didn’t. She can’t know what I told you about the sighing. She’d be upset, furious, she’d go mad if she knew what I’d said to you.’

“我真的很抱歉上周的事，”他开口说道，“我以为我想让她来，但后来我又不想了。她不能知道我跟你说的关于叹气的事。如果她知道我跟你说了什么，她会很生气，会非常愤怒，会疯掉的。”

I noted how fearful his response seemed. Was he concerned that Saffron would be hurt or was he worried she’d be angry?

我注意到他的反应似乎很害怕。他是担心萨弗伦会受伤，还是担心她会生气？

‘You talk about Saffron as though you’re very scared of her or perhaps of upsetting her? It’s as though you fear she’d break or explode if you said anything at all negative or critical.’ As I spoke, I knew there was a disparity between how Bear experienced Saffron and how she seemed to me. I couldn’t quite square the person who’d come to the session the previous week – who seemed neither fragile nor fierce – with the terror Bear was expressing. Neither did it seem that Bear had told me anything about her that could justify his anxious concern. Something didn’t add up.

“你谈到萨弗伦的时候，好像很害怕她，或者害怕惹她生气？好像你担心只要说一点负面或批评的话，她就会崩溃或爆发。” 我说话的时候，意识到贝尔对萨弗伦的印象和我眼中的她截然不同。我实在无法将上周来咨询的那个人——既不脆弱也不凶狠——与贝尔表现出的恐惧联系起来。贝尔似乎也没有跟我说过任何关于萨弗伦的事情，足以解释他如此焦虑不安。总觉得哪里不对劲。

There are many moments in couple therapy when the therapist is confronted with a disparity between how one partner sees the other and how, in actuality, they really are. I remember one couple where the woman, Yolande, an elegant and accomplished person in her mid-fifties came to see me one early summer. Her husband was in the armed forces and away on tour and we agreed, rather unusually, that she would come alone until he returned to the UK in September. She had a rich and interesting life and spent a great deal of time caring for others, which she found rewarding and interesting. However, she was deeply disappointed in her marriage and over the few months we met alone, she complained bitterly about her husband. As we talked, I got a picture of a rather cold and uncaring man. She wept about his lack of real interest in her and her life and she raged angrily about his authoritarian and controlling personality. She told me how critical he was of her – her cooking, her clothes and the company she kept – painting a portrait of a man obsessed with his status and how the world saw them as a couple. By the end of the summer, I had a very vivid picture in my mind of her husband, a picture which reminded me of the character Soames in the Forsyte Saga novels. Cold, cruel, inadequate and very self-important. A beast of a man, not an attractive picture at all. So, it was with some trepidation that I arranged to meet him individually before we began the joint couple work.

在伴侣治疗中，治疗师经常会遇到这样的情况：伴侣双方对彼此的认知与实际情况存在巨大差异。我记得有一对夫妇，女方约兰德，一位五十多岁、优雅而事业有成的女性，在初夏时节来找我咨询。她的丈夫是军人，正在外地执行任务。我们达成了一个略显特殊的协议：她独自前来，直到九月丈夫返回英国。她拥有丰富多彩的生活，并投入大量时间照顾他人，她认为这既有意义又充满乐趣。然而，她对自己的婚姻深感失望。在我们单独相处的几个月里，她不断地抱怨丈夫。随着谈话的深入，我逐渐了解到他是一个冷漠无情的男人。她为丈夫对她和她的生活缺乏真正的兴趣而哭泣，也愤怒地控诉他专横跋扈、控制欲极强的性格。她告诉我他如何对她吹毛求疵——她的厨艺、她的穿着、她交往的人——描绘出一个痴迷于自身地位以及世人如何看待他们夫妻关系的男人形象。到了夏末，我脑海中浮现出她丈夫的形象，让我想起了《福尔赛世家》小说中的索姆斯。冷酷无情、能力不足，而且极其自负。简直是个禽兽，一点也不讨喜。因此，在正式开始夫妻咨询之前，我怀着忐忑的心情安排了一次单独会见。

September came and into my office walked a tall, slightly balding and very upright man. He smiled at me warmly and began his narrative by telling me how Yolande had spoken so well of me and how much he’d been looking forward to coming. I was taken aback; here was someone completely different from the man I’d pictured. Not cold and arrogant at all but instead gracious and, surprisingly, given his rank, humble. Yolande had seen her husband through a lens that was distorted by her own internal world. And yet, though Yolande’s husband wasn’t the Soames she painted him to be, over time, I came to see that there were actually aspects of him that confirmed her view. It was just a lot more complex and nuanced than the picture she held of him in her mind. Neither Beauty, nor Beast.

九月来临，一位身材高挑、略微秃顶、身姿挺拔的男士走进我的办公室。他热情地对我微笑，开始讲述他的经历：约兰德对我的评价很高，他一直很期待这次来访。我感到很意外，眼前这个人与我之前想象的截然不同。他一点也不冷漠傲慢，反而彬彬有礼，而且令人惊讶的是，考虑到他的身份，他竟然如此谦逊。约兰德看待丈夫的方式，显然受到了她内心世界的扭曲。然而，尽管约兰德的丈夫并非她笔下描绘的索姆斯那样，但随着时间的推移，我逐渐意识到，他身上确实有一些特质印证了她的看法。只不过，他远比她想象的要复杂得多，也微妙得多。他既非美女，也非野兽。

It seemed this distortion was going on inside Bear as he continued to experience Saffron as both fragile and frightening. We would discuss how he might talk more directly to her about his feelings but, when it came to it, he was never able to do so and so nothing seemed to change. The weeks passed and though he persisted in talking about her sighs, we seemed unable to make much sense of it. Why, I wondered, did the sighing get to him so badly? I could see that often he was silently irritable with her and we regularly discussed this anger he had. Gradually, he was able to acknowledge his own unhappy feelings but he still felt murderous when she sighed.

似乎这种扭曲的认知一直存在于贝尔的内心，他始终觉得萨弗伦既脆弱又可怕。我们讨论过他该如何更直接地和萨弗伦谈谈自己的感受，但真到那一步，他却始终无法做到，所以一切似乎都没有改变。几周过去了，尽管他一直念叨着萨弗伦的叹息，我们却始终无法理解。我不禁纳闷，为什么萨弗伦的叹息会让他如此痛苦？我看得出他常常默默地对萨弗伦感到恼火，我们也经常讨论他这种愤怒。渐渐地，他开始正视自己不快的情绪，但每当萨弗伦叹息时，他仍然恨不得杀了她。

One Tuesday morning, Bear came in looking exhausted; his normal springy mop of hair looked as depressed and flattened as he did. He told me he’d been up all night worrying because Saffron had snapped at him and he hadn’t slept a wink.

一个星期二的早晨，贝尔进来时看起来筋疲力尽；他那平时蓬松有弹性的头发，此刻也像他本人一样，显得萎靡不振、扁塌塌的。他告诉我，他整晚都没睡，因为萨弗伦冲他发脾气了，他担心得彻夜未眠。

‘It started cos I forgot to buy bread on the way home from work. She said that I didn’t listen to her and that I was thoughtless. In front of the children, too.’ He paused briefly and looked at me, hoping, I think, for sympathy, and then continued with his tale of woe. Saffron was unfair on him; Saffron was unkind to him; Saffron never said thank you; Saffron never seemed to look out for his welfare. As I listened, I thought to myself that her comments had sounded really quite mild.

“事情起因是我下班回家路上忘了买面包。她说我不听她的话，说我粗心大意。而且还当着孩子的面。”他顿了顿，看了我一眼，我想他是想博取同情，然后继续诉说他的悲惨遭遇。萨弗伦对他不公平；萨弗伦对他冷酷无情；萨弗伦从来不说谢谢；萨弗伦似乎从来不关心他。我听着，心想她的话听起来其实还算温和的。

‘You often feel that Saffron is raging at you, Bear. I wonder why?’

“你经常觉得萨弗伦在对你发火，贝尔。我想知道为什么？”

‘She hasn’t forgiven me.’

“她还没有原谅我。”

‘Forgiven you?’

“原谅你了吗？”

‘For missing Arlo’s birth.’

“因为错过了阿洛的出生。”

He then told me with great shame that when his second son was born, he’d been in the pub, drinking after work. Saffron called him to say she thought she was going into labour but, somehow, he didn’t leave the pub and when he eventually got home, she’d already gone to the hospital without him. When he arrived at the labour ward, the midwife had sent him back home because he was too drunk. After he told me, we sat in silence and I waited for him to say more.

他羞愧地告诉我，第二个儿子出生那天，他下班后在酒吧喝酒。萨弗伦打电话告诉他，她觉得自己要生了，但他不知怎么的没离开酒吧。等他终于回到家时，萨弗伦已经去了医院。他赶到产房时，助产士因为他醉得太厉害，让他回家了。他告诉我这些后，我们沉默地坐着，我等着他继续说下去。

‘Saffron didn’t speak to me when she came back with the baby. She wouldn’t even let me hold him. Wouldn’t have anything to do with me at all,’ Bear recounted, his voice breaking. ‘When Arlo was a week old, I went and talked to the GP and she arranged for me to go to rehab. Her mother moved in whilst I was in treatment.’

“萨弗伦带着孩子回来后，一句话也没跟我说。她甚至不让我抱孩子。她根本不理我，”贝尔哽咽着回忆道。“阿洛出生一周后，我去看了家庭医生，她安排我去戒毒所。我接受治疗期间，她妈妈搬来和我一起住。”

‘I wonder how it was when you came home?’

“我想知道你回家的时候是什么感觉？”

Bear shrugged. ‘We never really talked about it.’

贝尔耸了耸肩。“我们从来没真正谈论过这件事。”

This confession gave me a much stronger insight into their situation and I felt in my own bones the let-down and betrayal Saffron must have felt. To be so careless, to not make it to your own son’s birth, that must have stirred up feelings hard to recover from.

这段坦白让我对他们的处境有了更深刻的了解，我感同身受地体会到了萨弗伦当时的失望和背叛。如此粗心大意，竟然没能亲眼见证自己儿子的出生，这想必会让她难以释怀。

‘Perhaps her sighing is her way of expressing how upset she still feels, Bear?’ I suggested. ‘Every time she sighs, I think you hear her berating you for what you did. She sighs and it makes you feel so guilty and bad, and you hate her for it.’ Bear looked miserable and nodded. ‘It seems you both have difficulties in facing your feelings, perhaps even knowing what they are. And neither of you have felt able to talk things through with each other. You’ve previously dealt with your emotional pain by anaesthetising yourself with alcohol and perhaps Saffron can only express her feelings by sighing?’

“或许她叹气是在表达她仍然很伤心，贝尔？”我建议道。“我觉得她每次叹气，你都感觉她在责备你。她叹气让你感到内疚和难过，你因此恨她。”贝尔看起来很沮丧，点了点头。“看来你们俩都难以面对自己的感受，甚至可能根本不知道它们是什么。而且你们俩都没办法好好沟通。你以前都是用酒精麻痹自己来应对痛苦，或许萨弗伦只能通过叹气来表达她的感受？”

‘I just wish she’d be happy. That I could make her happy. I used to. If I can’t make her happy, what’s the point? What’s the point of anything?’ Bear responded sadly.

“我只希望她能快乐。我希望我能让她快乐。我以前能。如果我不能让她快乐，那还有什么意义？一切还有什么意义？”熊悲伤地回答道。

It seemed that for Bear and Saffron, heavy breaths, huffs, puffs and sighs was the only language they spoke, and Bear was hyper-alert to these ‘tells’, his antennae always out for these almost silent ‘accusations’.

对于熊和藏红花来说，沉重的呼吸、喘息、呼哧呼哧和叹息似乎是他们唯一能说的语言，而熊对这些“信号”格外警觉，他的触角总是伸向这些几乎无声的“指控”。

A few sessions later, he began by telling me he was feeling a little better. He talked about how much the weather could affect his mood and how much he’d enjoyed walking through Regent’s Park to my office. He said, ‘June is bustin’ out all over!’ And laughed. I said that I thought he looked like he was bustin’ out today too. Then, looking thoughtful, he began to talk about how he wished he could be more spontaneous and freer.

几次咨询后，他告诉我他感觉好多了。他谈到天气对他的情绪影响很大，还说他很享受穿过摄政公园来我办公室的这段路程。他说：“六月真是生机勃勃！”然后笑了。我说我觉得他今天看起来也精神抖擞。接着，他若有所思地开始说，他多么希望自己能更随性、更自由一些。

‘Spontaneous and free?’ I echoed, hoping he would say more about what he meant.

“自发和自由？”我重复道，希望他能更详细地解释一下他的意思。

He shrugged his shoulders and I noticed that he held his hands together and then seemed to place them protectively over his crotch.

他耸了耸肩，我注意到他双手合十，然后似乎将双手护在了胯部。

‘Is the spontaneity you long for anything to do with your sexual feelings?’ I asked.

我问：“你渴望的那种自发性与你的性欲有关吗？”

He nodded and then he talked about how he and Saffron had woken up early and had sex. It was the first time they’d made love for a long while. Gradually, he explained that when he was drinking their sex life had ‘gone down the toilet’. Most of the time, he’d been too drunk in the evenings to have sex and Saffron would be up early before him in the mornings. When he’d come out of rehab, they’d had quite a lot of sex but it just hadn’t worked very well, so they’d stopped.

他点点头，然后开始讲述他和萨弗伦如何早起做爱。这是他们很久以来的第一次性生活。他慢慢解释说，他酗酒的时候，他们的性生活“一团糟”。大多数时候，他晚上都喝得烂醉，根本没法做爱，而萨弗伦早上总是比他起得早。他从戒酒所出来后，他们做爱的次数不少，但效果并不理想，所以就停止了。

‘What was it that didn’t work, Bear?’ I asked.

“到底是什么方法行不通，贝尔？”我问。

He blew out his cheeks and looked uncomfortable but after some moments he told me that Saffron hadn’t liked it anymore. She didn’t get excited and he couldn’t make her come, though he tried and tried.

他鼓起腮帮子，看起来很不自在，但过了一会儿，他告诉我萨弗伦不喜欢这样了。她没有兴奋起来，他试了又试，也没能让她达到高潮。

‘This morning, she came. She seemed to be really enjoying it – I thought the kids would hear her she made so much noise.’

“今天早上她来了。她看起来玩得很开心——她弄得那么吵，我以为孩子们会听到。”

‘Sighing?’ I asked, smiling.

“叹气？”我笑着问。

‘Yes, sighing! A lot of sighing!’ he laughed.

“是啊，叹气！叹了很多气！”他笑着说。

We talked then about how much his sense of goodness was dependent on making Saffron happy and how before she was pregnant, whenever something went wrong between them, he could always make her happy in bed. It was how they made up – without words and with their bodies.

我们当时聊到，他的善良感很大程度上取决于让萨弗伦开心，以及在她怀孕之前，每当他们之间出现问题，他总能在床上让她开心起来。他们就是这样和好的——无需言语，用身体。

After that session, Saffron’s sighing didn’t anger Bear so much. Things opened up and we began to talk about his fragile sense of his own goodness – his uncertainty about whether he was a good man or a selfish beast.

那次谈话之后，萨弗伦的叹息不再那么惹贝尔生气了。我们敞开心扉，开始谈论他脆弱的自我认知——他对自己究竟是好人还是自私的野兽感到迷茫。

People repeat patterns. Patterns of relating learnt at the knees of their mothers or fathers. From the work we did together, I came to understand that Bear’s parents hadn’t been happy together. His father was an angry man, remote and cold, and his mother had often been sad and disappointed. Bear had been hyper-alert to his mother’s moods; she’d made the weather in the house. Very occasionally, she made the sun come out but mostly she made black clouds. The strongest image Bear had of his mother was of her watching television in her bedroom on a miniature set which she placed on a tray across her lap. He would knock gently and go in and sit gingerly, perched on the end of the bed, just to be near her. He remembered the blue candlewick bedspread and picking at it with his finger, bored and lonely and fearful she’d find him a nuisance and send him away. He grew up with an abiding sense that he wasn’t a delight, that he didn’t lift her heart or please her. Deep in his bones, he thought of himself as a burden and feared he was the cause of her sadness, he was the one who’d disappointed her. Now, he lived in fear of disappointing Saffron. Just as he’d monitored his mother’s moods, he had watched Saffron in exactly the same way, fearfully listening out for those black clouds. When Saffron was sunny, when he could make her sigh with delight, he felt like a prince amongst men, happy and proud. Without that assurance, he felt like a beast, angry and dangerous, bad inside.

人们总是重复着同样的模式。这些相处模式是从父母耳濡目染中习得的。通过我们一起做的调查，我了解到贝尔的父母并不幸福。他的父亲脾气暴躁，冷漠疏离，而他的母亲则常常悲伤失望。贝尔对母亲的情绪异常敏感；她仿佛掌控着家里的气氛。偶尔，她能让阳光普照，但大多数时候，她带来的都是乌云密布。贝尔对母亲印象最深刻的画面，是她坐在卧室里，用托盘把一台迷你电视机放在腿上看电视。他会轻轻敲门，走进去，小心翼翼地坐在床尾，只为了能靠近她。他记得那条蓝色的烛芯床罩，记得自己百无聊赖、孤独寂寞，害怕母亲觉得他碍事，把他赶走，便用手指轻轻拨弄着它。他从小就觉得自己不讨人喜欢，不能让她开心，也不能让她高兴。他骨子里觉得自己是个累赘，害怕自己是她悲伤的根源，害怕是自己让她失望。如今，他时刻提心吊胆，生怕让萨弗伦失望。就像他曾经观察母亲的情绪一样，他也用同样的眼光注视着萨弗伦，生怕她有任何不快的迹象。当萨弗伦心情愉悦，当他能让她发出满足的叹息时，他觉得自己就像个王子，快乐而骄傲。而一旦失去了这种确定感，他就觉得自己像头野兽，愤怒而危险，内心充满罪恶。

Part Two

第二部分

BETRAYAL

背叛

Of course I’ll hurt you. Of course you’ll hurt me. Of course we will hurt each other. But this is the very condition of existence. To become spring, means accepting the risk of winter. To become presence, means accepting the risk of absence.

—Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, Manon, Ballerina

我当然会伤害你。你当然会伤害我。我们当然会互相伤害。但这正是存在的本质。成为春天，意味着接受冬天的风险。成为存在，意味着接受缺席的风险。——安托万·德·圣埃克苏佩里，《玛侬，芭蕾舞女》

What is betrayal? It nearly always involves lies and it always involves selfishness. The betrayer puts their own interests, wishes and needs first; whilst their loved one had trusted, they would not. To be an adulterer or a traitor is still, in many places in the world a very dangerous thing to be; though in the West, at least, neither offence will bring about dire consequences. No hands will be cut off or eyes gouged out, no banishment enforced. Despite this, we condemn adulterers – revile them in the press and send flowers and love to the cuckold. But imagine if we could get inside their heads, and understand more about both ‘victim’ and ‘perpetrator’?

什么是背叛？它几乎总是与谎言和自私有关。背叛者将自己的利益、愿望和需求放在首位；尽管他们所爱的人曾经信任他们，他们却不会。在世界许多地方，通奸或叛国仍然是一件非常危险的事情；尽管至少在西方，这两种罪行都不会带来可怕的后果。不会有人被砍手或挖眼，也不会有人被流放。尽管如此，我们仍然谴责通奸者——在媒体上对他们进行抨击，并向被戴绿帽的丈夫送上鲜花和爱意。但试想一下，如果我们能够走进他们的内心，更多地了解“受害者”和“加害者”，那会怎样呢？

Perhaps the first betrayal comes, as Freud suggested, when we are confronted with our parents’ relationship. The devastating discovery that our beloved parent loves another, leaves most of us uncomfortable in a threesome and many of us unconsciously play out unresolved feelings from that first betrayal in our own love affairs.

或许，正如弗洛伊德所言，我们第一次遭受背叛，是在面对父母的感情关系时。当我们发现自己挚爱的父母爱着别人时，这种毁灭性的打击会让大多数人对三人关系感到不自在，而许多人也会在自己的感情生活中，无意识地重演第一次背叛带来的未解心结。

When we break our vows, when we attack the bonds of love and trust, are we unconsciously attacking our parents’ loving link in our minds? When a woman begins an affair with a married man, is she paying back her mother for coming first with her father? When a man finds a mistress is he triumphing over his big daddy who took his precious mummy from him?

当我们违背誓言，当我们破坏爱与信任的纽带时，我们是否在无意识中破坏了父母之间深厚的爱？当一个女人与已婚男人发生婚外情时，她是否在报复母亲当年优先于父亲？当一个男人找到情妇时，他是否在战胜夺走他挚爱母亲的父亲？

But betrayal isn’t all about sex; there are many forms of dishonesty in relationships and all of them undermine the glue that holds our most intimate and meaningful relationships together.

但背叛并非都与性有关；人际关系中存在许多形式的不诚实，所有这些都会破坏维系我们最亲密、最有意义的人际关系的纽带。

Kamal Discovers Who’s Been Sleeping in His Bed

卡迈勒发现谁睡在他的床上

‘You must be fucking joking. No way … absolutely, no fucking way,’ Kamal exploded.

“你他妈在开玩笑吧。不可能……绝对不可能！”卡迈勒怒吼道。

Cecily sat there, her face streaked with tears and her chest heaving with unspoken feelings. Kamal began to leave. ‘I’m not staying to listen to this. I’m sorry, Susanna.’ He rose and made his way towards the door. Then he hesitated, turned back to Cecily and said plaintively, ‘Do you want me to go? Do you?’ She looked at me and then him and in a quiet, small voice said, ‘No. No.’

塞西莉坐在那里，脸上满是泪痕，胸口剧烈起伏，难以言表。卡迈勒转身要走。“我不想留下来听这些。对不起，苏珊娜。”他站起身，朝门口走去。然后他犹豫了一下，转过身来，哀求地问塞西莉：“你想让我走吗？你想吗？”她看了看我，又看了看他，用轻柔的声音说：“不，不。”

So here it was. I’d kind of known it for weeks. Had scribbled in my notebook several times: ‘Cecily – affair?’ And now it was out in the open. Well, kind of. It felt a relief. Perhaps now the work could start and we could all stop shilly-shallying around. It wasn’t that Cecily had told me in words, it was just that everything she said about herself and their life together screamed AFFAIR! AFFAIR! AFFAIR! What was interesting was why Kamal had taken so very long to cotton on. Or even to ask the question why she always seemed to have to work late and why she was constantly needing to make phone calls at the weekend. Was this a deliberate turning of a blind eye, I wondered? Did Kamal actively not want to know? Or perhaps this failure to notice was something more deeply unconscious?

事情就是这样。其实几周前我就隐约感觉到了。我在笔记本上潦草地写下了好几次：“塞西莉——出轨了？” 现在，一切都真相大白了。嗯，算是吧。感觉如释重负。或许现在工作可以开始了，我们也可以不再犹豫不决了。塞西莉并没有亲口告诉我，但她所说的关于自己和他们共同生活的一切都在呐喊着：出轨！出轨！出轨！有趣的是，卡迈勒为什么过了这么久才察觉到。甚至都没问过她为什么总是要加班到很晚，为什么周末还要不停地打电话。我心想，这是故意视而不见吗？卡迈勒是故意不想知道吗？或者，这种无视或许源于更深层次的潜意识？

They’d been coming for several months at Cecily’s instigation. She said she was worried that things had got a bit stale between them and that if they didn’t do something, they’d end up like their parents. Cecily’s hair was startlingly short, cropped close to her head and bleached blonde; one nostril was pierced with a tiny diamond and she was petite and deliciously rounded. She reminded me of Rihanna and had the same glow and sensuality as the singer, though in reality she was nothing so glamorous as she had recently been elected as a local politician in the far reaches of east London. Kamal was also striking. He was always dressed in black and his hair, long and straight, was just beginning to be streaked with grey and he wore it tied back into a low bun. There was something cool and clever about them – and they were a bit cool in their approach to the therapy, too.

在塞西莉的提议下，他们已经来了好几个月了。她说她担心他们之间的关系有点冷淡，如果他们再不采取行动，最终会像他们的父母一样。塞西莉的头发短得惊人，贴着头皮，漂成了金色；她的一个鼻孔里戴着一颗小小的钻石鼻钉，身材娇小，曲线玲珑。她让我想起了蕾哈娜，和这位歌手一样光彩照人，性感迷人，但实际上她远没有那么光鲜亮丽，因为她最近才当选为伦敦东区偏远地区的一名地方议员。卡迈勒也很引人注目。他总是穿着一身黑衣，长长的直发开始夹杂着些许灰白，他把头发扎成一个低低的发髻。他们身上有一种酷劲儿，很聪明——他们对待治疗的态度也同样如此。

At the first session, Kamal seemed barely interested in me or the process and when I asked them why they’d come, he said it was for Cecily; he thought they were fine and didn’t really believe in talking to a stranger about their relationship. Then he grilled me about my experience, my qualifications and my fee. Could they negotiate to pay less? Could they have a reduction because they had three children? I enquired about their financial situation; I didn’t want to be rigid if they really couldn’t afford it but it became quickly clear that both had reasonable earnings, so, instead, I turned my attention to his ambivalence about coming. I didn’t get far. Kamal was abrupt and stuck to his guns that he was here because she’d asked him to come, and if Cecily wanted that, he supposed he would go along with it.

第一次咨询时，卡迈勒似乎对我和咨询过程都漠不关心。当我问他们为什么来时，他说是为了塞西莉；他觉得他们关系很好，不太愿意跟陌生人谈论他们的感情生活。然后他开始盘问我，问我的经验、资质和收费。问他们能不能协商少付点钱？问他们能不能因为有三个孩子而减免一些费用？我询问了他们的经济状况；如果他们真的负担不起，我不想显得太强硬，但很快我就发现他们俩的收入都还不错，所以，我转而关注他来咨询的犹豫态度。但我没能成功。卡迈勒态度生硬，坚持说他是塞西莉让他来的，如果塞西莉希望他来，那他就答应。

Twenty minutes in and Kamal’s hostility had melted away, to be replaced by a charming but somewhat cool front. It soon became clear that the ambivalence about coming for therapy was in fact shared by both of them. It took ages to agree a session time because Cecily was so busy. She asked if I could see them at 7am. Or perhaps I worked at 10pm? Were Saturday mornings or Sunday afternoons possible? It was clear that it was going to be tough for them to make a commitment to couple therapy.

二十分钟后，卡迈勒的敌意消散了，取而代之的是一种迷人却略显冷淡的态度。很快，很明显，他们俩对接受治疗都感到矛盾。由于塞西莉非常忙，我们花了很长时间才确定治疗时间。她问我早上七点能不能见他们。或者我晚上十点上班？周六上午或周日下午可以吗？很明显，对他们来说，坚持接受伴侣治疗并非易事。

When, several weeks later, they did eventually start their sessions, it seemed they didn’t know what to talk about. Kamal would often be quiet and only interested in hearing what Cecily had to say. When she did speak, it was in a roundabout, unspecific way about how unhappy she was. A kind of impatience would come over me about wasting so much time; this prevarication and evasion was frustrating. His slightly superior nonchalance and her trippy vagueness made it harder for me to see this as a defence and that underneath, they were most probably very frightened of what might happen if they really began to talk.

几周后，他们终于开始咨询，但似乎都不知道该聊些什么。卡迈勒常常沉默不语，只对塞西莉的话感兴趣。而塞西莉开口时，总是拐弯抹角、含糊其辞地诉说着自己的不快乐。我感到有些不耐烦，觉得浪费了太多时间；这种闪烁其词、回避问题的做法令人沮丧。他那略带优越感的漫不经心和她含糊不清的语气，让我很难把这看作是一种自我保护，也很难意识到，在他们内心深处，或许他们非常害怕一旦真正开始交谈会发生什么。

The unhappiness seemed to stem from Kamal’s disinterest in having sex but this was skirted around, mentioned only in passing or jest, so we never could explore it in any depth. In some sessions, they talked, in a stilted manner, about their children, who were four, three and two, but even these conversations never seemed to develop. What things I said felt rather dull and pedestrian, as though I’d taken my comments from some rather basic ‘Making Your Marriage Work’ handbook. They wouldn’t let me in and so I had nothing meaningful to say.

他们的不快乐似乎源于卡迈勒对性生活的冷淡，但他们对此避而不谈，只是轻描淡写或以玩笑的方式提及，所以我们始终无法深入探讨。在一些咨询中，他们会生硬地谈论他们的孩子，分别是四岁、三岁和两岁，但即使是这些对话也从未真正展开。我说的话也显得枯燥乏味，仿佛我只是从一本非常基础的“婚姻经营指南”里照搬过来的。他们不让我走进他们的内心，所以我也说不出什么有意义的话。

The weeks went by and all I heard was more and more about Cecily’s busyness. Kamal would pick the children up from nursery. Kamal would make the children their tea. Kamal would put them to bed and then Cecily would come home, often slightly drunk, and wake them up to cuddle. I was, in truth, feeling more and more judgemental about her. But still Kamal seemed dead set on avoiding any showdown. He would only say mildly that he thought Billy, their four-year-old, would like to see more of her. And then I would hear that Kamal had spent the weekend on his own with the children and Cecily had gone to a conference for work.

几周过去了，我听到的全是关于塞西莉忙碌的消息。卡迈勒会去幼儿园接孩子们，给他们准备下午茶，哄他们睡觉，然后塞西莉会回家，通常带着些许醉意，把孩子们叫醒抱抱。说实话，我对她越来越反感。但卡迈勒似乎铁了心要避免任何冲突。他只是轻描淡写地说，他觉得他们四岁的儿子比利会希望多见见她。然后我又会听说，卡迈勒周末独自带孩子，而塞西莉则去参加工作会议了。

She eventually told him about the affair in the session just before the Easter break. It came out because he wanted her to go to his parents in Turkey for the holidays and she’d been resisting. ‘I have to work; you know I have to work. I’ll need to spend the bank holiday canvassing; I can’t be out of the country for the whole week. You take the kids and I’ll fly over after the Easter weekend, if I can.’ This statement sat in the room like a stark challenge. Kamal had said the previous week how much he was looking forward to spending time with her and she’d promised that she’d put the children first – but here she was backtracking. I found myself feeling very cross with her; it seemed so provocative.

在复活节假期前的咨询中，她最终还是向他坦白了这段婚外情。事情之所以曝光，是因为他想让她去土耳其和他父母一起过节，而她一直拒绝。“我得工作，你知道我得工作。我得利用银行假日去拉票，不可能整整一周都待在国外。你带着孩子们，如果可以的话，我会在复活节周末之后飞过去。” 这句话像一道刺耳的挑战，在房间里回荡。卡迈勒上周还说他多么期待和她共度时光，她也承诺会把孩子放在第一位——可现在她却出尔反尔了。我感到非常生气，她的话简直是在挑衅。

Kamal looked defeated. Then he rallied, turned his head to look at her and said, ‘Are you lying to me, Cecily? Don’t lie to me.’ She looked at him, panicked. Then she looked at me.

卡迈勒看起来很沮丧。然后他振作起来，转头看着她，说：“塞西莉，你在骗我吗？别骗我。”她惊慌地看着他，然后看向我。

‘I think he wants you to be straight with him, Cecily.’ I knew, as I spoke, that she knew I knew.

“我觉得他希望你对他坦诚相待，塞西莉。”我说话的时候就知道，她也知道我知道。

She nodded. A look of terror spread across her face. ‘I’m really sorry.’ And, after a long pause, ‘You know, don’t you? You know I’ve been seeing someone else?’

她点了点头，脸上浮现出惊恐的神色。“我真的很抱歉。” 沉默良久后，她又说：“你知道的，对吧？你知道我一直在和别人交往。”

Kamal put his head between his hands. It looked like he was trying to shut out what she was saying. Cecily was agitated and crying, ‘I’m sorry … I’m so sorry.’

卡迈勒双手抱头，似乎想屏蔽掉她的话。塞西莉情绪激动，哭着说：“对不起……我真的对不起。”

I watched, silent and transfixed.

我默默地、目不转睛地看着。

‘Who?’ asked Kamal, his voice hard and angry.

“谁？”卡迈勒问道，语气生硬而愤怒。

There was a silence and then, in a small, quiet voice, she said, ‘Frankie.’ And then he erupted.

一阵沉默之后，她用轻柔的声音说：“弗兰基。”然后他爆发了。

Kamal’s explosion and anger was like a passing cloud; by the next session, he seemed almost back to his cool, calm and in control self. But as they began to talk, for once they let me in and showed me how things really were. They’d talked exhaustively since they’d left the previous week, staying up into the small hours, riding these big, emotional waves, taking it in turns to weep in despair. Every single night they’d conclude they had to separate and then, every morning, they’d wake at dawn and, desperate and broken, they’d make love and be back at square one. Because they were now completely open to each other, I had a sense that they were more connected than they’d ever been.

卡迈勒的爆发和愤怒就像一阵飘过的乌云；到了下一次咨询，他似乎又恢复了冷静、沉着、自律的模样。但当他们开始交谈时，他们破天荒地让我了解了事情的真相。自从上周离开后，他们就一直在没日没夜地倾诉，彻夜长谈，任由情绪的巨浪翻涌，轮流绝望地哭泣。每天晚上，他们都会得出结论，必须分开，然后，每天清晨，他们都会破晓醒来，带着绝望和破碎，再次做爱，一切又回到了原点。因为他们现在对彼此完全坦诚，我感觉他们之间的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

From experience, I know that an affair can sometimes be a catalyst towards something much more satisfying, particularly when a relationship has avoided all conflict, leading to something stultifying and dead. In conflict-free relationships, there is often no sex at all but the discovery of an affair can trigger desire and suddenly there is passionate love-making. Why might this be so? One part of the reason is with the truth now on the table, all certainty about the future is gone and love-making becomes a way for the couple to mutually reassure each other, re-establishing the illusion of some sense of security. But I’ve also noticed that an affair can make a couple see each other differently; being suddenly separate and wanted by someone else can bring new excitement and desire. Was Cecily’s affair going to shake something up between them that would bring them closer or was her affair a transitional process that would lead her out of the relationship towards a real separation? Was it in fidelity or out fidelity?

根据我的经验，婚外情有时可以成为促成更令人满意的关系的催化剂，尤其是在一段关系一直避免冲突，最终导致关系僵化死寂的情况下。在没有冲突的关系中，往往根本没有性生活，但婚外情的发现却能激发欲望，突然间，激情四溢的性爱就会出现。这是为什么呢？部分原因是，当真相大白于天下时，对未来的所有确定性都消失了，性爱成为伴侣互相安慰、重建某种安全感的一种方式。但我同时也注意到，婚外情会让伴侣以不同的视角看待彼此；突然分离，又被其他人渴望，这会带来新的兴奋和欲望。塞西莉的婚外情会让他们之间的关系发生一些变化，从而拉近彼此的距离吗？还是说，这只是一个过渡过程，最终会引导她走出这段关系，走向真正的分离？这究竟是背叛，还是背叛？

‘It’s not serious, Kam. You don’t have to be threatened by Frankie,’ Cecily pleaded. ‘You know I just needed to find out what it’d be like, being with a woman.’ And then it dawned on me that Frankie wasn’t a man.

“卡姆，别那么严重。你不用害怕弗兰基，”塞西莉恳求道，“你知道我只是想体验一下和女人在一起是什么感觉。”这时我才恍然大悟，弗兰基不是男人。

‘But Frankie, of all people? I don’t understand how you could do that. Don’t you know the first principle? Don’t shit in your own backyard.’

“可是弗兰基，你居然能做出这种事？我真不明白你怎么能这么做。你难道不知道第一要务吗？别在自家后院拉屎。”

It became clear that they were both close and intimate friends with Frankie. She was politically active and a comrade of Cecily’s, and she lived just around the corner and had children the same age as theirs. Her husband had left the previous year and since then, she’d been in their life on a daily basis. Kam took Frankie’s kids to nursery; Frankie picked up theirs. Kam had Frankie’s kids for sleepovers when she wanted to go out … out, it now transpired, with Cecily. Whilst Kam had been caring for the children, Frankie and Cecily were around the corner making love.

很明显，他们俩都和弗兰基关系亲密。弗兰基积极参与政治活动，是塞西莉的同志，她就住在附近，孩子和他们的孩子年龄相仿。她的丈夫去年离开了，从那以后，她几乎每天都出现在他们的生活中。卡姆送弗兰基的孩子去幼儿园，弗兰基则去接他们的孩子。卡姆想出去的时候，就把弗兰基的孩子带去她家过夜……现在看来，她出去的对象正是塞西莉。卡姆照看孩子的时候，弗兰基和塞西莉就在附近幽会。

As this story unfolded, I wondered how Kamal could be so calm. It was such a betrayal, so humiliating to do this with someone so central to their lives. I felt the outrage boil inside me whilst Kam, still impassive, refused to. As the session drew to a close, Kam said that Cecily should have a session on her own with me – she needed help to decide what she wanted to do. He was going to Istanbul as planned and the kids were coming with him.

随着事情的进展，我不禁纳闷卡迈勒怎么能如此冷静。这简直是莫大的背叛，对一个如此重要的人做出这种事，简直是奇耻大辱。我感到怒火在心中翻腾，而卡迈勒却依然面无表情，强忍着怒气。会谈临近尾声时，卡迈勒说塞西莉应该单独跟我谈谈——她需要帮助来决定自己未来的方向。他按计划要去伊斯坦布尔，孩子们也会跟他一起去。

Cecily looked pinched and thin as she sat down the following week, her plump glow gone. She rummaged in her bag, apologised for nothing in particular and then, with her own tissues safely positioned on her lap, she burst into tears.

一周后，塞西莉坐了下来，看起来憔悴消瘦，原本丰腴的光彩荡然无存。她在包里翻找了一会儿，莫名其妙地道了歉，然后，她把手里的纸巾放在腿上，突然嚎啕大哭起来。

‘What shall I do? What shall I do, Susanna? I’m going to fuck up Kam, fuck up the kids, fuck up our home. What shall I do?’ She blew her nose loudly and looked at me as though I could give her an answer. ‘I love Kam. I love our life together. I don’t know why I’ve done this. I’ve tried and tried to break it off with Frankie but …’ She trailed off. ‘Tell me what to do. Please.’

“我该怎么办？我该怎么办，苏珊娜？我会毁了卡姆，毁了孩子们，毁了我们的家。我该怎么办？”她用力擤了擤鼻子，看着我，好像我能给她一个答案。“我爱卡姆。我爱我们在一起的生活。我不知道我为什么会这样做。我试过很多次想和弗兰基分手，但是……”她声音越来越小。“告诉我该怎么办。求你了。”

‘It’s really hard to be in such a dilemma. I can see how torn you feel,’ I said neutrally.

“陷入这种两难境地确实很让人难受。我能理解你内心的纠结，”我语气平静地说。

She took a deep breath. Looked at me. Then looked away.

她深吸了一口气，看了我一眼，然后又移开了视线。

‘Will I fuck up the kids?’

“我会不会把孩子们害惨？”

‘If you leave?’ I asked.

“如果你离开的话？”我问。

She nodded. ‘I don’t want what I want to hurt them … how can I justify that?’

她点点头。“我不想让我的愿望伤害他们……我怎么能这样呢？”

‘It sounds as though you feel it’s either them or you? Is it quite that stark?’

“听起来你觉得要么选他们，要么选你？情况真的这么泾渭分明吗？”

‘Kamal will hate me. The kids will hate me …’

“卡迈勒会恨我。孩子们会恨我……”

‘I think you’re frightened of how much you might hate yourself?’

“我想你是害怕自己会有多恨自己吧？”

‘Yes. I do hate myself and I’m going to hate myself either way.’ And she began to cry again.

“是的，我恨我自己，无论如何我都会恨我自己。”说着，她又哭了起来。

As the session went on, Cecily told me more about her relationship with Frankie and how it had been a revelation for them both. Neither had been with a woman before. She felt that they really got each other – partly because they were both women and like her Frankie was mixed race and very politically engaged. They were deeply in love and as she spoke to me, she conveyed the intensity and pleasure of their physical relationship.

随着谈话的进行，塞西莉向我详细讲述了她和弗兰基的关系，以及这段关系对她们两人来说是多么的一次顿悟。她们之前都没有和女人有过性经历。她觉得她们彼此非常了解——部分原因是她们都是女性，而且弗兰基和她一样是混血儿，并且非常关注政治。她们深深地爱着对方，塞西莉在和我交谈时，也流露出她们之间亲密关系的强烈和愉悦。

‘I’ve also loved being with Kam but I’m not sure he’s loved being with me.’

“我也很喜欢和卡姆在一起，但我不太确定他是否喜欢和我在一起。”

‘Sexually, you mean?’

“你是说性方面吗？”

‘Yeah.’ She paused. ‘It’s never been that great. He’s never seemed keen. I mean, even this last couple of weeks we’ve had a lot of sex but, well, it’s all my initiative, not his.’

“是啊。”她停顿了一下。“我们的关系从来就没那么好。他似乎从来都不太热衷。我的意思是，即使最近几周我们性生活很频繁，但是，嗯，这都是我的主动，不是他的。”

‘I think you feel really desired by Frankie and really not desired by Kam.’

“我觉得你很渴望得到弗兰基的认可，但卡姆却并不渴望你。”

‘Exactly. Yes, exactly. She wants me. I don’t think he does. Not really. I don’t think he ever has. And since I was elected, it’s hard for us to share stuff. Frankie knows what I’m doing and why. I don’t think Kam really gets it.’

“没错。对，没错。她想要我。我觉得他并不想。真的不想。我觉得他从来就没想过要我。自从我当选以来，我们很难分享彼此的事情。弗兰基知道我在做什么，也知道为什么。我觉得卡姆并不真正理解。”

We sat in silence.

我们沉默地坐着。

‘He can’t come,’ she said suddenly. ‘He doesn’t come. I’ve never been able to make him come. It’s gone on for years.’

“他来不了，”她突然说道。“他从来不来。我从来没能让他来过。这种情况已经持续好几年了。”

I waited, wondering about the children and how they’d been ‘made’. As though following my thoughts, Cecily said, ‘We went to a clinic. In Oxford. We had IUI.’

我等着，心里想着孩子们，想着他们是怎么“生”出来的。仿佛看穿了我的心思，塞西莉说：“我们去了一家诊所。在牛津。我们做了宫腔内人工授精。”

‘IUI?’

“宫腔内人工授精？”

‘I forget what it stands for but basically he masturbated into a jar and then they injected me. They checked when I was fertile. Worked every time, straight away.’

“我忘了它具体是什么意思，但基本上就是他把精液射进一个罐子里，然后他们给我注射。他们检查了我什么时候排卵。每次都有效，立竿见影。”

Lots of questions went through my head. How had they decided this? Why hadn’t they sought treatment for this difficulty and why had she gone along with it? And why, if the sex had always been that problematic, had she got involved with him in the first place?

很多问题涌上心头。他们是怎么做出这个决定的？为什么他们没有寻求治疗？她为什么会同意？如果性生活一直这么不顺利，她当初为什么还要和他在一起？

‘It sounds as though things haven’t been satisfactory for either of you.’

“听起来你们俩的情况都不太理想。”

She shrugged. ‘I don’t know. I don’t think Kam ever minded.’

她耸了耸肩。“我不知道。我觉得卡姆从来都不介意。”

I was left puzzled and surprised. I’d known that Kamal was less keen on having sex than her but he was devoted to Cecily. His whole identity conveyed his wish to be a good husband and father and he emanated a very masculine confidence. It was hard to put that persona together with what Cecily had just told me.

我感到困惑又惊讶。我知道卡迈勒对性爱的渴望不如她，但他对塞西莉却十分忠诚。他的一切言行都表明他渴望成为一位好丈夫、好父亲，而且他身上散发着一种非常阳刚的自信。我很难将他展现出的这种形象与塞西莉刚才告诉我的事情联系起来。

There were no seats on the crowded Tube. From Euston to Camden Town, I hung from the strap and hoped someone would give up their seat. Just as I was beginning to accept that I’d be standing all the way to Highgate, a tall man in his thirties smiled at me, gesturing to ask if I wanted to sit. I nodded gratefully and swapped places with him, plonking myself down on the warm moquette. This gallant deed took my thoughts back to Kamal. Clearly there was something important going on surrounding sexual identity. It wasn’t the first time that I’d come across a situation like this. If Cecily now thought she was probably lesbian and Kam didn’t seem to like sex with her, what did this mean? Had there been an unconscious collusion between them that had largely kept sex off the agenda? Were both in fact unsure about their heterosexuality and was that why they’d – unconsciously – chosen each other?

拥挤的地铁里没有座位。从尤斯顿到卡姆登镇，我只能抓住扶手，盼着有人能让座。正当我开始接受自己要一路站到海格特的现实时，一个三十多岁的高个子男人朝我微笑，示意我坐下。我感激地点点头，和他换了位置，一屁股坐在温暖的地毯上。这番举动让我想起了卡迈勒。显然，性取向方面存在着一些重要的事情。这并非我第一次遇到这种情况。如果塞西莉现在认为自己可能是女同性恋，而卡迈勒似乎并不喜欢和她发生性关系，这意味着什么？他们之间是否存在某种无意识的默契，使得性在他们之间几乎不被提及？他们其实都对自己的异性恋倾向感到迷茫，而这是否就是他们——无意识地——选择彼此的原因？

Understanding and working with sexuality can be the most puzzling part of my job and I’ve long wondered why that might be. Part of the reason is of course the difficulty that many couples have in sharing the very intimate details of their lives, but it’s also because sexual desire, and the fantasies that inevitably accompany it, are often buried in the deeper layers of the unconscious, hard to reach and disconnected from words and reason. Couples quite often come with a sexual ‘symptom’ – bringing difficulties that prevent them from having a satisfying sex life together. Whilst some of these sexual ‘symptoms’ can be relatively straightforward, sometimes they are not. Strong, potent husbands are disgusted by their wives’ bodies but excited by elder porn; loving, open and friendly wives are unable to be aroused and remain frozen and unmoved when touched. Our bodies tell the story but translating the story into something verbal, which can be understood and shared, can be very difficult to do.

It wasn’t difficult to answer – I was fresh from a passionate engagement with feminism and had spent years marching for women’s rights, attending conferences and consciousness raising groups. I was, I told the selection committee, worried that I wouldn’t be able to cope with the men: the bullying husbands demanding sex and pushing around their wives. Instead, for most of my career, it’s tended towards the opposite – angry, accusing women and rather compliant but disconnected and withdrawn men. Via this dance, a kind of equality of arms is reached, where what is most valued by the couple is the creative exchange that brings forth new thoughts, ideas, projects and sexual pleasures.
