‘For you’ he gestured with his head as he struggled out of his jacket.

“给你，”他一边费力地脱下外套，一边点头示意。

I looked at him enquiringly and placed the bag on the floor by the door.

我疑惑地看了他一眼，然后把包放在门口的地板上。

‘Rainier cherries – the best. We import them. They just came in today. The season’s verrry short. Three weeks, maybe.’

“雷尼尔樱桃——最好的。我们进口的。今天刚到货。产季非常短，大概只有三周。”

I smiled.

我笑了。

‘I wanted to say thank you. I think we’re in a much better place and I think we know we’re going to separate.’ He paused. ‘It’s OK. We’re going to come next week together – we want to discuss what to say to the children. Hope that’s OK?’

“我想说声谢谢。我觉得我们现在的情况好多了，我们也知道我们最终会分开。”他停顿了一下。“没关系。我们下周会一起过来——我们想商量一下该怎么跟孩子们说。希望你们不介意吧？”

‘Of course.’

'当然。'

‘I wanted to talk about my … er … difficulty. You know. With sex.’

“我想谈谈我的……呃……困难。你知道的。关于性方面的困难。”

I nodded. And as I looked down, I could see the hessian bag and the image of the red cockerel out of the corner of my eye and it occurred to me, here was such a clear symbol of male potency.

我点了点头。当我低头看时，眼角瞥见了粗麻布袋和上面的红色公鸡图案，我突然意识到，这真是男性力量的鲜明象征。

‘You said in that session when I came on my own that you thought my problem was because I was angry with Cecily?’

“你上次在我独自前来咨询时说，你认为我的问题是因为我生塞西莉的气？”

I nodded.

我点了点头。

‘I’m not sure that’s right.’ There was a long pause and I waited for Kam to say more.

“我不确定那样对不对。” 一阵长时间的沉默后，我等着卡姆继续说下去。

‘When I was about 15, my mother caught me looking at porn.’ He looked around the room, as though trying to find an escape route.

“我大概15岁的时候，被我妈发现我在看色情片。”他环顾四周，似乎在寻找逃跑的路线。

Hesitantly, he told me what porn he’d been watching and, though he struggled to be explicit, I gradually came to understand that it was incestuous in nature and involved a boy and his younger sister. His mother had been furious and had told him he was sick and a pervert. He felt as though his mother had never quite looked at him the same after that. We talked about how ashamed he’d felt and he wondered if that experience had made him ‘funny’ about sex. He certainly often felt guilty about it. Guilty if he didn’t try to have sex with Cecily and very guilty when they did.

他犹豫了一下，告诉我他一直在看什么色情片。虽然他难以启齿，但我逐渐明白，那片片子是乱伦题材的，讲述的是一个男孩和他的妹妹的故事。他的母亲勃然大怒，骂他变态、有病。他感觉从那以后，母亲看他的眼神就完全不一样了。我们聊到他当时的羞耻感，他想知道那次经历是否让他对性产生了“怪癖”。他确实经常为此感到内疚。如果他没有尝试和塞西莉发生性关系，他就会感到内疚；而当他们真的发生了性关系时，他会更加内疚。

‘You’ve never talked to me about your sister, Kam,’ I said, sometime later.

“卡姆，你从来没跟我谈起过你的妹妹，”过了一段时间，我说。

‘No. We don’t get on. She’s gone back to Istanbul and lives near my parents. I don’t really see her, even when we visit.’

“不，我们关系不好。她已经回伊斯坦布尔了，住在我父母家附近。即使我们去看望她，我也很少见到她。”

Jasmina, he told me, was a year younger than him and had always been the ‘weakling’ of the family and used that to manipulate his parents. She was always complaining and a real pain but his parents worshipped the ground she walked on.

他告诉我，贾斯米娜比他小一岁，一直是家里的“弱女子”，并以此来操控他的父母。她总是抱怨个不停，令人头疼，但他的父母却对她百依百顺。

‘Did you have to look after her when you were children?’ I asked.

“你们小时候要照顾她吗？”我问。

‘Not really. My mother wouldn’t have trusted me, I was too mean to her. I was always in trouble for not being nice enough to her or for hitting her or taking her toys.’ He laughed. ‘She had my parents wrapped round her little finger … still does.’

“其实不是。我妈不会信任我的，我对她太坏了。我总是因为对她不够好、打她或者抢她的玩具而挨骂。”他笑了。“她把我爸妈吃得死死的……现在也是。”

‘You felt she was the favourite? That they preferred her to you?’

你觉得她是他们最喜欢的？他们更喜欢她而不是你？

‘Abso-fucking-lutely! My mother was always telling me to be more like her and to be nice to her.’

“绝对没错！我妈总是跟我说要多向她学习，要对她好。”

Then he said, shamefaced, ‘The porn … it wasn’t about her. The girl in it wasn’t anything like Jasmina.’

然后他羞愧地说：“那部色情片……跟她无关。片中的女孩和贾斯米娜一点都不像。”

We were silent for a while, both of us contemplating this link. Then I said, ‘I think, Kam, there are lots of things wrapped up in this “symptom” of yours. There are the mixed feelings you have about Cecily, about having to give way to her needs a lot – perhaps like you were expected to do with your sister. And there are the mixed feelings of loving Cecily and your sister but at times hating them too?’

我们沉默了一会儿，都在思考这其中的联系。然后我说：“卡姆，我觉得你的这个‘症状’里包含了很多东西。一方面是你对塞西莉的复杂情感，你不得不经常迁就她——也许就像你小时候被要求对你妹妹那样。另一方面，你既爱塞西莉，也爱你的妹妹，但有时又恨她们，这种复杂的情感也包含在内。”

He nodded. ‘Cecily and my sister have quite a lot in common. Not looks-wise, but in some ways they’re both very …’ he searched for the words, ‘… difficult but also fragile.’

他点点头。“塞西莉和我妹妹有很多共同点。不是外貌上的相似，而是在某些方面，她们都很……”他斟酌着措辞，“……既难搞又脆弱。”

‘Perhaps, when you’ve felt sexual towards Cecily – who you believe is fragile – a part of you hasn’t been sure whether your sexual feelings are loving or destructive? Whether your penis is a good thing or something rather bad. And you bring me cherries in a bag with a big cock on it.’ I said, smiling.

“或许，当你对塞西莉——你认为她很脆弱——产生性欲时，你内心深处并不确定这种性欲是爱意还是伤害？不确定你的阴茎究竟是好事还是坏事。而你却给我带了一袋樱桃，袋子上还印着个大鸡巴。”我笑着说。

He laughed and then he looked at me intently. ‘I think my mother thought sex was just a bad thing. And especially a bad thing for a woman.’

他笑了笑，然后专注地看着我。“我觉得我妈妈认为性是一件不好的事。尤其对女人来说更是如此。”

‘Well, that’s a powerful message you got from your mother. When you don’t come inside Cecily, are you protecting her? But maybe you’re punishingly withholding something from her, too?’

“嗯，你从你母亲那里得到了一个很深刻的启示。当你不让塞西莉进屋时，你是在保护她吗？但也许你也在惩罚她，让她得不到某些东西？”

I’d like to tell you that after these sessions everything got sorted. But psychotherapy isn’t like that. For every step forward, there are often steps back. Therapy progresses in a spiral, looping back and forth, reworking old conflicts and circling around new challenges. Jung described it well: ‘We can hardly escape the feeling that the unconscious process moves spiral-wise round a centre, gradually getting closer, while the characteristics of the centre grow more and more distinct.’ fn1

我想告诉你，经过这些疗程，一切都迎刃而解了。但心理治疗并非如此。每向前迈进一步，往往就会有退步。治疗是一个螺旋式的过程，来回循环，不断重塑旧有的冲突，并围绕着新的挑战打转。荣格对此描述得非常精辟：“我们很难摆脱这样一种感觉：无意识的过程围绕着一个中心螺旋式地运转，逐渐靠近，而这个中心的特征也变得越来越清晰。”<sup>1</sup>

Cecily and Kam continued in therapy for another six months before Cecily moved out to live with Frankie. During those months, they cried a lot but they also became gradually gentler with each other and more determined to work together to ensure the children were protected as much as possible. In the last sessions, when they came alone, I sensed they both felt relieved it was over. Cecily seemed more grounded and happier, and Kam, slightly nervously, told me he had begun seeing a woman he worked with, someone much younger than him.

塞西莉和卡姆又接受了六个月的心理治疗，之后塞西莉搬去和弗兰基一起住。这几个月里，他们经常哭泣，但彼此之间也逐渐变得温柔，更加坚定地共同努力，尽最大可能保护孩子们。在最后几次单独咨询时，我感觉他们都如释重负，终于结束了。塞西莉看起来更加踏实快乐，而卡姆则略带紧张地告诉我，他开始和一位同事见面，那位女士比他年轻得多。

During those six months, I was never quite sure what the outcome would be. Would they find a way to stay together or would they split? When couples skirt that border between separation and staying together it always feels utterly mysterious to me. I never know when someone will cross that border from being in the relationship, however disappointing, to standing on the other side, out of it. For me, it’s even more mysterious than the process of falling in love and becoming a couple. Sometimes, couples come right up against the separation and then pull back and this can be because a psychic separation has taken place, rather than an actual house move – each partner becoming more their own person and less entangled with each other. Sometimes, couples don’t properly separate at all. Each moves to a new home, they get new partners, even have more children, but they can never quite let each other go.

在那六个月里，我始终无法确定结局会如何。他们会找到继续在一起的方法，还是会分道扬镳？当情侣徘徊在分居与继续在一起的边缘时，我总是觉得这无比神秘。我永远无法预知，一个人何时会跨越那条界限，从身处一段令人失望的关系中，彻底离开。对我而言，这甚至比坠入爱河、成为伴侣的过程更加神秘。有时，情侣们几乎就要分手了，却又退缩了，这可能是因为彼此之间产生了一种心理上的分离，而非实际的搬家——双方都变得更加独立，彼此之间的联系也越来越少。有时，情侣们根本无法真正分手。他们各自搬到新的住所，各自有了新的伴侣，甚至又有了孩子，但他们始终无法真正放下彼此。

# ↩

Rhoda Feeds on the Poison Apple

罗达以毒苹果为食

I’d just returned from the Easter break when this email appeared in my inbox:

我刚结束复活节假期回来，就收到了这封邮件：

Dear Susanna,

My daughter tells me I need a shrink. I found your name online. How much do you charge for a session?

Regards,

Rhoda

亲爱的苏珊娜：我女儿说我需要去看心理医生。我在网上找到了你的名字。请问你每次咨询收费多少？此致，罗达

I wrote back:

我回复道：

Dear Rhoda,

Thank you for your enquiry. We could meet for a consultation at my practice in Queen Anne Street next Wednesday at 10.15. Would that suit?

My fee would be £XX.

Best wishes,

Susanna

亲爱的罗达，感谢您的咨询。我们可以下周三上午10点15分在我位于皇后街的诊所进行咨询，您觉得合适吗？我的咨询费是XX英镑。祝好，苏珊娜

An hour later, I received a reply:

一小时后，我收到了回复：

I’ll think about it.

我会考虑一下。

Whilst it’s not unusual for an enquiry to evaporate without outcome, it is unusual for a prospective patient to be so forthright about their ambivalence. It was rather refreshing, to be honest. I remember years ago, a senior colleague saying that one would always find the most ambivalence about starting therapy right at the moment someone makes the first contact. In the various clinics I’ve worked in, it was expected that at least a third of the enquiries we received wouldn’t progress to any treatment.

虽然咨询最终不了了之并不罕见，但像他这样坦率地表达犹豫不决的潜在患者却实属罕见。说实话，这着实令人耳目一新。我记得多年前，一位资深同事曾说过，人们在初次咨询时往往对是否立即开始治疗最为犹豫。在我工作过的各个诊所，我们预计至少有三分之一的咨询最终不会接受任何治疗。

However, a few days later the following email arrived in my inbox:

然而，几天后，我的邮箱里收到了以下邮件：

I’ve thought about it.

I’ll come on Wednesday at 10.15am as you requested.

Please let me have your bank details so I can pay you the required amount. However, I must say your fee seems very expensive to me.

Regards,

Rhoda

我考虑过了。我会按您要求的，周三上午10点15分过来。请把您的银行账户信息给我，以便我支付您所需的费用。不过，我必须说，您的收费对我来说似乎太贵了。此致，罗达

Given the brusque nature of this communication, it was with some trepidation (and curiosity) that on Wednesday morning I awaited Rhoda’s arrival. I smiled as I opened my door and gestured for her to come in, as she seemed to hesitate on the threshold. She did not smile back.

鉴于这种生硬的沟通方式，周三早上我怀着忐忑（也带着一丝好奇）的心情等待着罗达的到来。我打开门，微笑着示意她进来，因为她似乎在门槛上犹豫了一下。她没有回以微笑。

‘Where do you want me?’ she asked. ‘Shall I lie down there?’ She pointed at my sofa.

“你想让我躺在哪儿？”她问。“我躺在那儿好吗？”她指着我的沙发。

‘Why don’t you just take a seat today,’ I suggested, and with that she perched rather awkwardly on the edge of the chair and screwed up her eyes to scrutinise me as closely as possible. She was a petite woman, elegant and athletic, with cropped short, silver hair. Her hands, which she folded in her lap, looked strong and purposeful.

“今天就坐下吧。”我提议道。她略显局促地坐在椅子边缘，眯起眼睛仔细打量着我。她身材娇小，优雅而充满活力，留着一头利落的银色短发。她交叠放在膝上的双手，看起来有力而坚定。

She then launched into what felt like a prepared speech in which she proceeded to tell me, in no uncertain terms, that she thought it highly unlikely I’d be able to help her. She was only here because her daughter, Tamar, had thought it a good idea. She mentioned several times that I was expensive and even at one point asked directly why I charged so much. I told her this was my usual fee but that if she was struggling financially this could be discussed. She waved a hand dismissively and eventually managed to tell me what had brought her to my consulting room. Her concerns centred on her childhood friend Michelle, whom she was no longer in contact with. They’d known each other since they were babes in arms as their mothers had been close friends. It seemed, from what she relayed, that she and Michelle had been inseparable most of their lives. However, they’d fallen out and Rhoda had ‘cut’ Michelle from her life. When I commented that this must have been extremely sad after such a long friendship, Rhoda scoffed disdainfully.

然后她开始滔滔不绝地讲起话来，语气像是事先准备好的，她斩钉截铁地告诉我，她觉得我不太可能帮到她。她来这里只是因为她女儿塔玛觉得这是个好主意。她好几次提到我的收费太贵，甚至一度直接问我为什么收费这么高。我告诉她这是我的正常收费，但如果她经济困难，我们可以商量。她不屑地挥了挥手，最后才告诉我她来我诊室的原因。她担心的是她儿时的朋友米歇尔，她们现在已经失去了联系。她们从小就认识，因为她们的母亲是好朋友。从她描述的情况来看，她和米歇尔几乎形影不离。然而，她们后来闹翻了，罗达把米歇尔从自己的生活中“剔除”了。当我感叹这么多年的友谊走到今天，这一定非常令人难过时，罗达不屑地嗤之以鼻。

As the session progressed and I dug a little deeper, Rhoda described how Michelle had committed an unforgivable betrayal. But as she spoke about the events that had led to their estrangement, she became increasingly animated and less and less coherent.

随着谈话的进行，我深入挖掘，罗达描述了米歇尔如何犯下了不可饶恕的背叛。但当她谈及导致她们疏远的事件时，她变得越来越激动，说话也越来越语无伦次。

‘I’ve never spoken to anyone in my life the way she spoke to me. It was just rude, really rude and …’ she fished around for the right word. ‘Rude!’

“我这辈子都没跟人说过她那样的话。太没礼貌了，真的太没礼貌了……”她斟酌着寻找合适的词。“没礼貌！”

I couldn’t help thinking how ironic it was that the word she used to describe Michelle was just the word that I’d been thinking fitted her.

我不禁觉得这真是莫大的讽刺，她用来形容米歇尔的那个词，正是我一直觉得最适合她的那个词。

Rhoda’s narrative was long and winding but, eventually, I began to get a clearer picture of what had happened between them. It seemed that although Michelle had been Rhoda’s closest friend and confidante, they’d often had ups and downs. Over the years, they’d fallen out over a broken vase, over a holiday booked and then cancelled and hadn’t spoken for a year because Rhoda had taken exception to Michelle’s new dog. But when Rhoda’s husband had left her, Michelle and Rhoda had renewed their bond and they had become very friendly and close.

罗达的叙述冗长而曲折，但最终，我开始逐渐了解她们之间发生的事情。米歇尔虽然一直是罗达最亲密的朋友和知己，但她们的关系也时常起伏伏。这些年来，她们曾因为打碎花瓶、因为预订后又取消的假期而闹翻，甚至因为罗达不喜欢米歇尔新养的狗而一年没联系。但罗达的丈夫离开她之后，米歇尔和罗达重拾旧谊，变得非常友好亲密。

‘It sounds like Michelle is the one you turned to when things got really tough,’ I suggested gently.

“听起来，当你遇到真正困难的时候，你会向米歇尔寻求帮助，”我温和地说道。

‘Not really,’ Rhoda bristled, ‘we just hung out together. She was single. I was suddenly on my own – it was … convenient. And it wasn’t “really tough”, either. My husband was an idiot and when he left, it was, frankly, rather marvellous.’

“才不是呢，”罗达生气地说，“我们只是经常一起玩。她是单身。我突然就一个人了——这……挺方便的。而且也不算‘真的很难熬’。我丈夫是个白痴，他离开后，坦白说，真是太好了。”

I didn’t know quite how to reply to that but I noted the angry scorn in her voice and the way she’d pushed back very strongly at my attempt to connect with a softer side of her.

我不太清楚该如何回应，但我注意到她语气中的愤怒和轻蔑，以及她对我试图与她温柔的一面建立联系的强烈抵制。

‘The problem with Michelle, as I’ve been trying to explain to you, is that she’s rather conventional, terribly finicky – judgemental,’ Rhoda concluded and I gave her a quizzical look to encourage her to continue. ‘She didn’t approve of Nigel.’

“正如我一直试图向你解释的那样，米歇尔的问题在于她相当保守，而且非常挑剔——爱评判别人，”罗达总结道，我疑惑地看着她，示意她继续说下去。“她不喜欢奈杰尔。”

‘Nigel?’

“奈杰尔？”

‘When I started to see Nigel, she thought it was …’ she shrugged her shoulders. ‘Wrong. She doesn’t approve of affairs.’ Rhoda rolled her eyes and sat back, waiting for me to speak.

“我刚开始和奈杰尔交往的时候，她以为……”她耸了耸肩。“错了。她不赞成婚外情。”罗达翻了个白眼，往后靠了靠，等着我开口。

‘And that’s why you stopped speaking to her?’

“所以你才不再跟她说话？”

She then explained that Michelle had avoided asking her to dinner. Michelle made a big Friday night dinner every week and Rhoda had gone regularly but now suddenly she was ‘ persona non grata ’.

她接着解释说，米歇尔一直避免邀请她共进晚餐。米歇尔每周五晚上都会准备丰盛的晚餐，罗达以前经常去，但现在突然间她就成了“不受欢迎的人”。

‘She made her feelings crystal clear. She may not have said anything directly but I’m not stupid – she treated me like a pariah and she treated Nigel worse.’

“她把自己的感受表达得非常清楚。她可能没有直接说出来，但我并不傻——她把我当成弃儿，对奈杰尔的态度更糟。”

‘Did you talk to her about it?’ I asked. She looked at me contemptuously, as though my question was ridiculous, and then, ignoring my enquiry, she continued with her story.

“你跟她谈过这件事吗？”我问。她轻蔑地看了我一眼，仿佛我的问题很荒谬，然后，她没有理会我的询问，继续讲她的故事。

‘Every year, we all go to my house on the Isle of Wight. Michelle and her family, my children. We’ve been doing it for years. Then, because Nigel was coming, she didn’t want to come. And then because she wasn’t coming her children didn’t either.’

“每年，我们全家都会去我在怀特岛的房子。米歇尔和她的家人，还有我的孩子们。我们已经这样做了好几年了。后来，因为奈杰尔也要来，她就不想来了。然后因为她不来，她的孩子们也不来了。”

‘She didn’t come because she doesn’t like Nigel?’ I asked, trying to get the story straight.

“她没来是因为她不喜欢奈杰尔吗？”我问道，试图弄清楚事情的来龙去脉。

‘No! She doesn’t approve . Because he was well, sort of married. He doesn’t really even live with his wife, most of the time, so I don’t know why she made such a silly fuss about it.’

“不！她不赞成。因为他，嗯，算是已婚吧。而且他大部分时间都不和妻子住在一起，所以我不知道她为什么对此反应这么大。”

She went on to explain that, as far as she was concerned, Michelle’s behaviour was completely unacceptable, so she’d told Michelle their friendship was over. I asked Rhoda how Michelle had taken this and Rhoda, scornfully, said that Michelle had cried and made a huge fuss.

她接着解释说，在她看来，米歇尔的行为完全不可接受，所以她告诉米歇尔她们的友谊结束了。我问罗达米歇尔对此作何反应，罗达轻蔑地说，米歇尔哭了，大吵大闹。

‘But she’s a bit of a drama queen anyway, so she’s always making a fuss about something or other. She sends me a birthday card every year with some stupid sentimental message in it. I don’t know why she bothers. It’s a ridiculous waste of time and money. She can’t seem to get it through her head that we’re no longer friends.’

“不过她本来就有点爱演戏，总是为这做那做。她每年都给我寄生日贺卡，里面写着一些愚蠢的煽情话。我不知道她为什么还要这么做。这简直是浪费时间和金钱。她好像永远也搞不明白我们已经不是朋友了。”

The ‘every year’ snagged and I began to wonder how long it was since this falling-out had taken place.

“每年”这个词让我感到困惑，我开始想知道这次争吵究竟是什么时候发生的。

‘How long ago did this happen, Rhoda?’ I asked.

“罗达，这件事是什么时候发生的？”我问。

‘Ten, maybe eleven years. I can’t really remember.’

“十年，也许是十一年。我记不太清了。”

‘Oh!’ I exclaimed, failing to hide my surprise. ‘Well, that’s quite a long while. It makes me wonder why you’re coming now. Why does your daughter think you need to come now?’

“哦！”我惊呼道，难掩惊讶。“嗯，那可是过了好久啊。我很好奇你为什么现在才来。你女儿为什么觉得你现在必须来呢？”

‘She thinks I’m obsessed.’

“她觉得我着迷了。”

‘Obsessed with Michelle? Are you?’ I asked.

“你迷恋米歇尔吗？”我问。

She didn’t answer my question but proceeded to show me the answer by talking for the next 20 minutes about Michelle and the various unforgivable things she’d done. She felt betrayed and wronged and also angry that Michelle had ‘got away with it’. Her daughter was also in the firing line because she remained close with Michelle’s children and had continued to celebrate birthdays and Christmases in her presence.

她没有回答我的问题，而是用接下来的二十分钟滔滔不绝地讲述米歇尔以及她所做的种种不可饶恕之事，以此来向我展示答案。她感到被背叛、被冤枉，同时也愤怒于米歇尔“逍遥法外”。她的女儿也成了众矢之的，因为她和米歇尔的孩子们关系密切，并且一直和米歇尔一起庆祝生日和圣诞节。

‘My daughter wants me to “make it up” with Michelle so she can invite her to the wedding.’

“我女儿想让我和米歇尔‘和好’，这样她就可以邀请米歇尔参加婚礼了。”

‘The wedding?’

“婚礼？”

‘Tamar’s getting married at Christmas,’ she replied curtly, as though I was somehow slow for not knowing her daughter was getting married.

“塔玛尔圣诞节要结婚了，”她简短地回答道，仿佛我不知道她女儿要结婚这件事很迟钝似的。

Betrayal comes in many forms; it occurs between lovers, between colleagues and between siblings. But betrayal between women friends seems to be particularly disillusioning and hard to recover from. Over the years, I’ve observed the nature of women’s relationships and the particular quality of those bonds. As women mature and give up the fantasy of the ideal lover – the selfless heroic prince who’ll care for them seamlessly and selflessly – and as they face the fact that their lover isn’t and cannot be a good mother to them, they often seem to compensate for this by turning to their friends for that particular kind of unquestioning, unconditional care. Frequently, friendships between women are constructed to confirm each other by mirroring and harmonising, protecting each other from harsh reality. In these reassuring and like-minded states, female friendship tries to recover the romantic ideal, providing a cosy bubble away from disappointments and limitations. But friendship can be hard to maintain, jealousies can emerge when one friend has more than the other and when that bubble bursts, a vengeful fury can be unleashed, the unspoken contract not to question, disapprove or challenge lies in tatters and visceral hatred replaces the romance.

背叛的形式多种多样，恋人之间、同事之间、兄弟姐妹之间都可能发生背叛。但女性朋友之间的背叛似乎尤其令人失望，也更难释怀。多年来，我观察了女性关系的本质以及这些关系的特殊性质。随着女性逐渐成熟，她们不再幻想理想伴侣——那种无私奉献、无条件呵护她们的英雄王子——当她们面对伴侣无法成为她们的好母亲这一现实时，她们往往会转向朋友，寻求那种无条件、不加质疑的关爱。女性之间的友谊常常建立在相互映照、彼此呼应的基础上，保护彼此免受残酷现实的伤害。在这种令人安心、志同道合的氛围中，女性友谊试图重拾浪漫的理想，为彼此提供一个远离失望和局限的舒适空间。但友谊很难维系，当一个朋友拥有的比另一个朋友多时，嫉妒就会滋生；当这种美好的幻想破灭时，复仇的怒火就会爆发，不质疑、不反对、不挑战的潜规则就会瓦解，而本能的仇恨就会取代浪漫。

I once had a patient, many, many years ago, who purported to be a witch; she celebrated the solstice, kept many cats and always wore black. She earned her living making penis- and vagina-shaped candles but she also wrote personalised spells and incantations that she sold on the internet. Mostly her customers were other women and in one session she gave me a series of printed cards with curses printed on them.

很多年前，我曾遇到一位自称女巫的病人；她庆祝冬至，养了很多猫，总是穿着一身黑衣。她靠制作阴茎和阴道形状的蜡烛为生，也撰写个性化的咒语和符咒，并在网上出售。她的顾客大多是女性，有一次，她给了我一系列印有诅咒的卡片。

By the witch’s breath

And the darkening storm

I invoke my anger

And wish you grievous harm

Since your sight is flawed

And your heart unkind

I invoke my anger

To turn your green eyes blind

When the dawn is breaking

And the light comes back

I won’t need my anger

I won’t feel the lack

But you, my dear, will suffer

In your crazy mind

From envy, fear and darkness

From guilt that chafes and binds.

以女巫的呼吸和渐暗的风暴，我唤起我的愤怒，愿你遭受重创。因为你的目光有缺陷，你的心肠冷酷无情，我唤起我的愤怒，让你的绿眼睛失明。当黎明破晓，光明重现，我将不再需要我的愤怒，我将不再感到匮乏。但你，我亲爱的，将在你疯狂的头脑中受苦，受嫉妒、恐惧和黑暗的折磨，受那令人痛苦和束缚的罪恶感的折磨。

I saw Rhoda for a dozen sessions before she decided my services were no longer required. She sought from me an audience for her grudge, not a solution or a route to healing. I worked hard to encourage her to explore why she was so preoccupied. Could we make, perhaps, a link to some loss or sense of betrayal in her past? Was there some unfinished business that this falling-out with Michelle had come to symbolise for her? But I got nowhere; she loved her anger and enjoyed sharing her grievance with me. It was as though she couldn’t see the poison inside the shiny red apple of revenge.

我为罗达做了十几次咨询，之后她决定不再需要我的帮助。她来找我倾诉怨恨，而不是寻求解决之道或疗愈之路。我努力引导她探究自己为何如此执着于此。或许，我们可以找到一些与她过去经历的某种失去或背叛感相关的线索？与米歇尔的决裂是否象征着她心中未了的心愿？但我一无所获；她沉溺于愤怒之中，乐于向我倾诉她的委屈。仿佛她看不到复仇这颗闪亮红苹果里隐藏的毒药。

As I struggled to help her move on, I came to see that her sense of betrayal had become an integral part of who she was. To lose or lessen this grievance, to change her feelings towards Michelle in any way, would have meant confronting and grieving her loss; something she was too afraid to do. Every year that she’d wasted on the grudge had to be justified so that the anger and bitterness she felt towards Michelle was required to grow, year in, year out. All this hatred provided the oxygen to justify her position and I felt that in her unrelenting refusal to mourn and forgive she was trying to destroy her need for love.

当我努力帮助她走出阴影时，我渐渐意识到，她内心深处的背叛感已经深深融入了她的生命。想要消除或减轻这种怨恨，想要改变她对米歇尔的任何感受，都意味着要面对和哀悼失去的痛苦；而这正是她所恐惧的。她必须为浪费在怨恨上的每一年找到理由，才能让对米歇尔的愤怒和苦涩年复一年地滋长。所有这些仇恨都为她的立场提供了支撑，而我感觉，她执意拒绝哀悼和原谅，其实是在试图摧毁自己对爱的渴望。

After weeks of listening to her bitter complaints, I began to think of Rhoda as a kind of Miss Havisham, the scorned and bitter spinster of Dickens’s novel Great Expectations, who, betrayed by her lover, turns forever away from life. Miss Havisham is envious and withholding, training her young ward, Estella, to hate men and to break their hearts, killing her capacity for love. ‘But that, in shutting out the light of day, she had shut out infinitely more; that, in seclusion, she had secluded herself from a thousand natural healing influences; that, her mind, brooding solitary, had grown diseased …’

听了罗达几个星期的苦涩抱怨后，我开始觉得她有点像狄更斯小说《远大前程》中那个被抛弃、愤世嫉俗的老处女哈维沙姆小姐。哈维沙姆小姐被情人背叛后，从此与世隔绝。她嫉妒成性，冷漠疏离，教唆她的年轻养女艾丝黛拉憎恨男人，伤透他们的心，扼杀了她爱的能力。“但是，她封闭了自己，隔绝了更多的阳光；她把自己与世隔绝，也隔绝了无数自然的疗愈力量；她孤寂沉思的心灵，已经病入膏肓……”

I thought that Rhoda was also filled with envy and, like the evil queen in Snow White, she was both poisoned and poisonous in her vengeance.

我认为罗达也充满了嫉妒，就像白雪公主里的邪恶皇后一样，她既被嫉妒所毒害，又因复仇而变得恶毒。

I’d come across this kind of difficulty before and recognised the bleakness of its tenacious hold on some patients. It was an addiction to a kind of psychic revenge, one that was crushing her much more than it was affecting the object of her hate. I pointed out that her vindictive feelings seemed to be taking her nowhere, that Michelle’s attempts to reconnect sounded loving and hopeful, whilst she seemed to be suffering terribly. Her anger had become a kind of poison infecting her whole life and now she was in danger of seriously falling out with her daughter. I tried to help her to see that revenge is pointless if the act is masochistic.

我以前也遇到过类似的困境，也意识到它对某些病人来说是多么根深蒂固、难以摆脱。这是一种精神上的复仇瘾，这种复仇对她自身的伤害远大于对她所憎恨的对象的影响。我指出，她的报复心理似乎毫无益处，米歇尔试图与她重新建立联系的努力听起来充满爱与希望，而她自己却似乎正在承受巨大的痛苦。她的愤怒就像毒药一样侵蚀着她的整个生活，现在她甚至面临着与女儿彻底决裂的危险。我试图帮助她明白，如果复仇是一种自虐行为，那么它就毫无意义。

‘Rhoda, it’s almost as if you don’t care if you hurt yourself, as long as you can hold onto the fantasy that you’re getting back at Michelle. It’s as if you’re driving your brand new BMW into her garden wall each day – her wall might have lost a brick or two but you keep totalling your brand new car.’

“罗达，你好像根本不在乎自己是否会受伤，只要你能继续幻想自己是在报复米歇尔就行了。这就像你每天都开着你的新宝马撞她家的花园围墙——她的围墙可能只是掉了一两块砖，但你却不断地把你的新车撞得面目全非。”

But nothing I said seemed to move Rhoda. She remained untouched and unreachable and ended her treatment without, it seemed, a backward glance.

但我说什么似乎都无法打动罗达。她依旧无动于衷，难以接近，似乎头也不回地结束了治疗。

# ↩

Don Juan Grows up and Settles Down

唐璜长大后安定下来

James was a rather unprepossessing patient considering his reputation as a Lothario. He contacted me by text in late July saying he’d read something I’d written in a newspaper article about infidelity that had struck him enormously and did I by any chance have an appointment I could offer? I replied that I didn’t currently but thought it likely I’d have a space when I returned from holiday in September. ‘Could you wait?’ I asked. The answer came back immediately that he’d be only too happy to wait and that he was really looking forward to meeting me.

考虑到詹姆斯风流成性的名声，他本人其实并不起眼。七月下旬，他发短信联系我，说他读到我在报纸上发表的一篇关于婚外情的文章，深受触动，问我是否还有空位可以预约。我回复说目前没有，但九月份度假回来后应该会有空位。“您能等吗？”我问。他立刻回复说非常乐意等，而且很期待见到我。

I love holidays and many psychotherapists plan their breaks to coincide with the academic year. The period up to the long summer vacation, however, can be wearying for psychotherapists. There’s the natural tiredness everyone feels at the end of a long year but it can also be tough because it’s common for long-term patients to end their treatment just before the August break. Thus, alongside the build-up of excitement and anticipation at the thought of a month to myself, there’s often a tinge of sadness at bringing to a close sessions with patients who’ve been on a long journey with me.

我热爱假期，许多心理治疗师也都会安排假期与学年同步。然而，漫长的暑假前的这段时间对心理治疗师来说却可能格外疲惫。每个人都会在漫长的一年结束后感到自然的疲惫，但更难熬的是，许多长期患者会在八月假期前结束治疗。因此，在想到即将迎来一个月的独处时光而感到兴奋和期待的同时，也常常会因为要结束与那些陪伴我走过漫长旅程的患者们的治疗而感到一丝伤感。

It’s common knowledge that psychotherapists get their largest number of referrals at two points in the year: in September, after the summer holidays, and in January, after the Christmas holidays. This particular September was no different; my email and phone were full of messages from potential patients wanting appointments and there were several friendly prompts from James, reminding me I’d ‘committed’ to seeing him on my return.

众所周知，心理治疗师一年中有两个时期会收到最多的转诊：一个是暑假后的九月，另一个是圣诞假期后的一月。今年九月也不例外；我的邮箱和手机里塞满了潜在患者的预约信息，詹姆斯也多次友好地提醒我，我已经“答应”回来后要见他。

James’s texts led me to expect a dynamic and engaging person but when he entered my consulting room, he seemed rather nondescript – someone you’d walk past in the street without a second glance. His hair appeared unwashed and thinning, his clothes were ill-fitting and his trainers were caked with the dirt of ages. He seemed bowed and rather fragile.

詹姆斯的短信让我以为他是个充满活力、风趣幽默的人，但当他走进我的诊室时，却显得平平无奇——就像那种你在街上擦肩而过都不会多看一眼的人。他的头发看起来稀疏蓬乱，衣服也不合身，运动鞋上积满了厚厚的灰尘。他佝偻着身子，显得有些虚弱。

He told me he’d wanted to come because, at an after-work drinks party, his friend had described him as ‘a bigger philanderer than Boris Johnson’. Everyone laughed but whilst the all-male group seemed good-natured and jocular about this description, James felt deeply uncomfortable. He’d gone home that evening ‘feeling really sick’, been unable to sleep that night and this nausea and sleep disturbance had continued from then on. He spoke at length about how previously he’d been a very good sleeper and generally untroubled about things but since that evening, he really hadn’t been able to settle down to anything.

他告诉我他想来是因为在一次下班后的聚会上，他的朋友形容他“比鲍里斯·约翰逊还花花公子”。大家都笑了，虽然这群男人看起来对这个形容毫不在意，也乐于开玩笑，但詹姆斯却感到非常不舒服。那天晚上他回家后“感觉非常难受”，整晚都没睡着，而且这种恶心和睡眠障碍从那以后就一直持续着。他详细地讲述了自己以前睡眠很好，也总是很放松，但自从那天晚上之后，他就真的什么都做不了了。

I tried to explore with James what he’d found so troubling about the off-hand remark. Was it the actual idea of himself as a philanderer? Indeed, did he think it to be true? Or perhaps he’d felt humiliated in some way?

我试图和詹姆斯探讨，他究竟对那句随口而出的话感到如此困扰。是因为他真的觉得自己是个花花公子吗？他真的认为那是真的吗？或者，他是不是感到受到了某种羞辱？

He listened to me carefully but seemed unable to pinpoint what had distressed him so much or whether the flippant Boris comparison had any basis in truth. ‘I just don’t get any of it. Usually, I sail through stuff but something about this has really got to me.’ He then gave me a big smile and added, ‘I’m hoping you’ll be able to tell me why.’

他认真地听我说，但似乎无法确切指出究竟是什么让他如此烦恼，也无法判断我轻率地将他比作鲍里斯是否真的有道理。“我完全不明白。通常情况下，我都能轻松应对，但这件事却让我耿耿于怀。”说完，他露出了灿烂的笑容，补充道：“我希望你能告诉我原因。”

There are multiple reasons why people have affairs but, in my experience, it is often to do with something that is going on between the couple. An affair can be a response to a problem the couple aren’t able to deal with together and sometimes the betrayal acts as a useful red flag. On the other hand, an affair can be a response to the lessening of attachment to a partner and a transition out of the relationship towards something new. But, in this instance, it seemed that James’s continual infidelity probably wasn’t much to do with his girlfriend but rather spoke to something about James and his difficulties with intimate relationships more generally.

人们出轨的原因有很多，但以我的经验来看，通常都与伴侣之间的某些问题有关。婚外情可能是伴侣无法共同面对的问题的一种回应，有时这种背叛本身就是一种警示信号。另一方面，婚外情也可能是对伴侣依恋感减弱的一种反应，是结束现有关系、开始新恋情的一种方式。但就詹姆斯的这个例子而言，他持续的不忠似乎并非与女友有关，而是反映了他自身以及他在亲密关系方面普遍存在的困难。

The rest of the session seemed to proceed at a snail’s pace; it was stilted and at times had a rather excruciating awkwardness to it. What I suggested to him didn’t seem to connect and my silence seemed to make him agitated. As we came to the end, I discussed the fee I would charge, the time I could offer on a regular basis and other administrative details of beginning therapy. I said that it seemed that it had been difficult for us to get to the bottom of what feelings were keeping him awake at night but perhaps we might meet again for a further consultation and think a bit more about it all? Immediately he came to life, saying firmly that yes, he definitely wanted to come back and that all the arrangements were fine and he would see me next week.

接下来的咨询过程仿佛蜗牛爬行，节奏缓慢，气氛生硬，有时甚至令人尴尬难耐。我提出的建议似乎并没有引起他的共鸣，而我的沉默似乎让他更加焦躁不安。临近结束时，我与他讨论了咨询费用、定期咨询时间以及其他一些开始咨询的行政细节。我说，我们似乎很难找到他夜不能寐的真正原因，或许我们可以再约一次，进行更深入的咨询，仔细探讨一下。他立刻来了精神，坚定地说，是的，他非常想再来，一切都安排妥当，下周见。

After he left, I remember feeling an initial uncertainty about whether I really wanted to see him again. I harboured serious doubts that he’d be able to settle down to treatment and I wondered if he and I made a good ‘fit’. But, although James certainly hadn’t made my heart sing with anticipation during our first session, this made me curious about the reason why. On the phone and in text, he’d seemed so responsive and charming. And yet, in the session he presented himself as a rather unattractive man, lacking in any charisma. Was my lukewarm response to him a reflection of how unlovable he felt, deep inside?

他离开后，我记得一开始有些犹豫，不知道是否真的想再见到他。我非常怀疑他能否安心接受治疗，也怀疑我们是否真的“合适”。虽然詹姆斯在第一次咨询中并没有让我心动不已，但这反而让我好奇原因。在电话里和短信里，他看起来那么热情迷人。然而，在咨询中，他却显得相当缺乏魅力，毫无吸引力。我对他的冷淡反应，是否反映了他内心深处觉得自己不值得被爱？

To my surprise, meeting him for a second time was totally different to our first encounter. This time, James was wearing a beautifully tailored suit and, despite his slightness and thinning hair, he presented as lithe, fit and well turned out. As it was a warm September day, he immediately took off his jacket to reveal an exquisitely sculpted shirt which, I noticed, framed his slight but athletic frame perfectly. Handmade, I thought to myself. As we began talking, James seemed unrecognisable from the rather fragile and uncertain character I’d met the week before. I quickly picked up on how present he seemed to be, how much less fragile he appeared and how much more assertive he was. It was becoming clearer to me that there were two sides to James and he had decided to show me both. An unloved, unlovable James and now this confident, shiny self. What was real? What was fake?

令我惊讶的是，第二次见到他与初次见面截然不同。这次，詹姆斯身着一套剪裁精良的西装，尽管他身材瘦削，头发也有些稀疏，但看起来却身姿矫健，体格健壮，衣着得体。九月的天气温暖宜人，他立刻脱下外套，露出一件剪裁精美的衬衫，我注意到，这件衬衫完美地衬托出他略显单薄却不失运动感的身材。我心想，这一定是手工缝制的。我们开始交谈后，我发现眼前的詹姆斯与一周前那个略显脆弱和不自信的他判若两人。我很快察觉到他变得多么专注，多么不再脆弱，多么自信。我越来越清楚地意识到，詹姆斯有两面性，而他决定将这两面都展现给我。一面是无人爱慕、不被人喜欢的詹姆斯，另一面则是如今这个自信闪耀的自己。究竟哪一面是真实的？哪一面又是虚假的？

Once he’d sat down and carefully raised his trouser leg to protect the crisp creases, he launched into telling me more of his story. He was now nearly 40, he said, and found himself, not for the first time, in a tangle between his present partner of three years, Grazyna, and two other women. He explained that he’d never really had a monogamous relationship and was given to seeing at least two if not three women at the same time. His duplicity often got found out and he was therefore regularly dumped. He rarely ended a relationship; usually the women gave up on him.

他坐下后，小心翼翼地撩起裤腿，以免裤子的褶皱被刮花，然后开始向我讲述他的故事。他说，他快四十岁了，发现自己又一次陷入了与交往三年的现任伴侣格拉齐娜和其他两个女人之间的纠葛之中。他解释说，他从未真正有过一段忠贞的感情，总是同时和至少两三个女人交往。他的两面三刀经常被识破，因此也经常被甩。他很少主动结束一段感情；通常都是女人放弃了他。

‘Do you mind when you’re “dumped”?’ I asked.

“你介意被甩吗？”我问。

‘Not really,’ James said brightly. ‘It’s kind of a bit upsetting but I usually know when it’s coming and have started another flirtation by then.’

“倒也不是，”詹姆斯兴高采烈地说。“这有点让人沮丧，但我通常都知道什么时候会发生这种事，而且在那之前我已经开始和别人调情了。”

He explained that he thought he was addicted to the ‘chase’ and he felt quite bad about messing around in this way but up to now he hadn’t been able to stop. He wondered if part of the problem for him was that Grazyna, felt a bit different; she was special.

他解释说，他觉得自己对这种“追逐”上瘾了，他很后悔自己这样胡闹，但至今为止他都无法停止。他想知道，对他来说，问题的一部分是不是因为格拉齐娜有点不一样；她很特别。

‘She’s too good for me, Susanna. Definitely punching above my weight with her,’ he said, laughing. I noticed his teeth were perfectly white and even and that they seemed to be a representation of the way he hid this darker stuff behind a glossy and charming front.

“苏珊娜，她太优秀了，我配不上她。跟她在一起，我绝对是高攀了。”他笑着说。我注意到他的牙齿洁白整齐，似乎正是为了掩盖他内心深处的阴暗面，用光鲜亮丽的外表掩盖着这一切。

‘The crunch is coming, though. She’s been working in Paris but her contract is coming to an end and she’s expecting to come back to London and move in with me.’ He raised his eyebrows and grimaced, as though this was a ridiculous idea. ‘We’ve been discussing and planning this for most of our relationship; it’s not news.’ And he laughed again, showing those perfect teeth.

“不过，关键时刻快到了。她一直在巴黎工作，但合同快到期了，她打算回伦敦和我一起住。”他挑了挑眉，做了个鬼脸，好像这个想法很荒谬。“我们交往以来一直在讨论和计划这件事，这根本不是什么秘密。”说完，他又笑了，露出一口洁白的牙齿。

‘You haven’t said how you feel about it, her moving in?’ I said, encouraging him to look a little deeper. He smiled at me warmly and said he thought he loved her and knew it was time he settled down to have a family but he felt ‘sick in his stomach’ at the thought of giving up his other women.

“你还没说你对她搬进来这件事的感受呢？”我问道，鼓励他深入思考一下。他温暖地对我笑了笑，说他觉得自己爱她，也知道是时候安定下来组建家庭了，但一想到要放弃其他女人，他就“难受得胃里翻江倒海”。

‘Is this the same feeling you have at night, James?’ I asked. ‘Is this the “sickness in your stomach” that is keeping you awake?’ He looked at me intently, as though I’d said something extraordinary rather than making a simple and rather obvious link.

“詹姆斯，你晚上也是这种感觉吗？”我问。“是不是那种让你睡不着觉的‘胃部不适’？”他专注地看着我，仿佛我说了什么惊天动地的大事，而不是一个简单而显而易见的联系。

‘Yes,’ he exclaimed, ‘now you say it, I see it. Do you think I’m not sleeping because of Grazyna? Maybe it’s nothing to do with being called out like that by Steve?’

“是啊，”他惊呼道，“你这么一说，我明白了。你以为我睡不着是因为格拉齐娜吗？也许跟史蒂夫那样指责我根本没关系？”

‘Yes, because you seem to be saying that you’re at a kind of crossroads in your life. A part of you wants to be closer and more committed to Grazyna but another part of you doesn’t know if you’ll be able to.’ James nodded, looking thoughtful.

“是的，因为你似乎在说你正处于人生的十字路口。你的一部分想要和格拉齐娜更亲近、更投入，但另一部分又不知道自己是否能够做到。”詹姆斯点点头，若有所思。

James’s enthusiasm for my observations and the warm gratitude he expressed as the session ended left me much more hopeful about the therapy. I could sense a shift in myself and a relief that he was turning out to be so engaging and ready to work. True, I could see things would move slowly – he had little insight into himself and found it difficult to see the links between his feeling states and his behaviours – but I was now hopeful, and the work began.

詹姆斯对我的观察表现出的热情，以及在咨询结束时他表达的由衷感谢，让我对治疗更有信心。我能感觉到自己有所转变，也松了一口气，因为他如此投入，并且愿意配合治疗。的确，我知道治疗进展会比较缓慢——他对自己缺乏了解，很难理解自己的情绪状态和行为之间的联系——但我现在充满希望，治疗也正式开始了。

Over the following weeks, I learnt that James worked in the city leading a successful PR company; that he’d been a ‘whiz kid’ and made a lot of money but was now struggling to consolidate his early success. He confessed that at university, he’d developed a problem with cocaine but had ‘cleaned up’ and was now devoted to the gym and well on the way to being completely vegan. Though work worried him from time to time, James felt his life to be ‘pretty perfect except for the mess I’m in with women’. When I didn’t respond to this and there was a lull, James said that he’d decided before starting therapy that he’d be completely frank with me. He knew that I couldn’t help him if he didn’t tell me everything.

接下来的几周，我了解到詹姆斯在城里经营一家成功的公关公司；他曾是个“神童”，赚了很多钱，但现在却难以巩固早期的成功。他坦白说，大学时他染上了可卡因的恶习，但已经戒掉了，现在全身心投入健身，并且正在努力成为一名纯素食主义者。虽然工作偶尔会让他担忧，但詹姆斯觉得他的生活“除了和女人之间的问题之外，几乎完美”。我没有回应，我们之间陷入了沉默，这时詹姆斯说，在开始接受治疗之前，他已经决定要对我完全坦诚。他知道，如果他不告诉我一切，我就帮不了他。

‘You need to know that no one else knows what I’m really like. Only you. I spend a lot of time convincing others I’m a straight-up, lovely, decent guy … I’m not.’

“你要知道，除了你，没有人真正了解我是什么样的人。我花了很多时间去说服别人我是一个正直、可爱、善良的人……但我不是。”

I half wondered to myself if he told me this to make me feel special in some way and if this was one of the ways he seduced women. But I concentrated on James’s negative feelings about himself and commented that it was interesting that he’d gone into PR, as it seemed that this was how he related to people, as though he needed to ‘curate’ his public persona. He agreed with my interpretation and said that he usually worked hard to get people to like him. I sensed that our working partnership was deepening as he shared more and more.

我心里暗暗琢磨，他跟我说这些是不是想让我觉得自己很特别，是不是这是他吸引女性的手段之一。但我还是把注意力集中在詹姆斯对自己的负面情绪上，并评论说他选择公关行业挺有意思的，因为这似乎正是他与人相处的方式，仿佛他需要“精心打造”自己的公众形象。他同意我的解读，说他通常会努力博得别人的喜欢。随着他分享的内容越来越多，我感觉我们的工作关系也在不断加深。

On the other hand, James was often late for his sessions. It wasn’t unusual for me to receive a text 20 minutes before the session was due to start telling me that he would be late, or even that he was sorry but he wasn’t going to make it at all. More interestingly, his texts, on occasion, would ask me to remind him what time the session was. This was most surprising as I believe strongly in what I call the three Rs of therapy: rhythm, regularity and reliability, which means that sessions are scheduled for the same time and same day every week. How could he keep forgetting, I wondered?

另一方面，詹姆斯经常迟到。我经常会在咨询开始前20分钟收到他的短信，告诉我他会迟到，甚至很抱歉他来不了。更奇怪的是，他有时还会发短信让我提醒他咨询时间。这让我非常惊讶，因为我坚信治疗的三大原则：节奏、规律性和可靠性，这意味着咨询应该每周在同一天同一时间进行。我纳闷，他怎么会总是忘记呢？

Psychoanalytic therapists pay close attention to the kind of relationship that is created between them and their patient; we try to notice the kinds of feelings that our patients stir up in us. Do we like them? Do we feel useless? Do we feel competitive? We notice these feelings in ourselves because sometimes they are useful clues to the patient’s inner world and the way they unconsciously construct their relationships.

精神分析治疗师会密切关注自己与患者之间建立的关系；我们会努力觉察患者在我们心中激起的各种感受。我们喜欢他们吗？我们感到自己毫无用处吗？我们感到竞争吗？我们之所以会注意到这些感受，是因为有时它们能为了解患者的内心世界以及他们无意识地构建人际关系的方式提供有用的线索。

I noticed that James treated me in two ways. Sometimes he made me feel as if I was a very good therapist whom he could truly trust. At these times, he let me know that I was special to him and that his therapy with me was important. But at other times, he made me feel I was peripheral to what really mattered to him, that he wasn’t attached to me or committed to the work we were doing together and that, at any moment, he could drop the sessions from his mind and his schedule. In other words, he blew hot and cold and I very much suspected this was how he treated many people in his life, not least the women he was involved with. Gradually, he began to tell more detail about his relationship with these two other women, Dominique and Marcie. He’d been involved with them for nearly two years and he admitted that this was very much part of a pattern, as he always had at least two relationships on the go. The affairs with Dominique and Marcie were something new, however, because they knew each other and also knew they were both sleeping with him. He left this revelation hanging and went silent and I was left sitting there wondering if he was talking about a threesome. I felt a bit teased and tantalised by what he’d told me and aware that there was a sense of excitement around this secret life. He told me just enough to pique my interest and then held back, and suddenly I realised here he was, drawing me in again, only to keep me at arm’s length. It made me feel shut out and a bit useless. Noticing how he treated me gave me an insight into how he drew women to him. Perhaps this was how he’d tantalised and drawn in Grazyna, Dominique and Marcie?

我注意到詹姆斯对我的态度截然不同。有时他让我觉得自己是一位非常优秀的治疗师，值得他完全信任。这时，他会让我知道我对他来说很特别，对我的治疗对他来说至关重要。但有时，他又让我觉得自己对他来说无关紧要，他对我并不上心，也不投入我们共同的治疗，仿佛他随时都可以取消治疗。换句话说，他忽冷忽热，我强烈怀疑他对待生活中的许多人都是如此，尤其是那些与他有染的女性。渐渐地，他开始更详细地讲述他与另外两个女人——多米尼克和玛茜——的关系。他与她们交往了近两年，并承认这早已成为一种模式，因为他总是同时维持至少两段关系。然而，与多米尼克和玛茜的婚外情却有所不同，因为她们彼此认识，也知道她们都与他有染。他把这番话戛然而止，沉默不语，我坐在那里，琢磨着他是不是在说三人行。他刚才说的那些话让我既感到被戏弄又感到被挑逗，也让我意识到，这种秘密生活似乎让他兴奋不已。他只说了一点点，就勾起了我的兴趣，然后又欲言又止。我突然意识到，他又一次把我拉近了距离，却又始终保持着距离。这让我感觉自己被拒之门外，有点儿没用。注意到他对待我的方式，让我明白了他是如何吸引女人的。或许，他就是靠这种方式来勾引格拉齐娜、多米尼克和玛茜的？

‘You say, James, that you’ve made a pact with yourself to be completely honest with me, yet I notice that you only half tell me things, that you share something and then leave it hanging. I wonder if this is your way of ensuring I stay interested and that you keep a sense of control. I think you really do want my help but you also want to keep the reins in your own hands by holding back things. If you share everything with me, then perhaps you’ll feel too exposed?’

“詹姆斯，你说你跟自己约定要对我完全坦诚，但我注意到你总是只说一半，说完一点就戛然而止。我怀疑你这样做是为了让我保持兴趣，也为了掌控局面。我觉得你确实需要我的帮助，但你也想通过有所保留来掌控一切。如果你什么都跟我说，也许你会觉得太暴露了？”

James sat with his fists in tight balls in his lap for what must have been 30 seconds. I left him with it as he was clearly chewing over my words. I could hear birds singing outside in the last throes of summer before they headed south. Eventually, James opened one of his balled fists and simply said, ‘OK.’

詹姆斯双手紧握成拳，放在腿上，大概过了三十秒。我没打扰他，因为他显然在琢磨我的话。我能听到外面鸟儿的歌声，那是夏末它们南迁前的最后时光。最后，詹姆斯松开一只拳头，简单地说了句：“好吧。”

What the ‘OK’ meant became clearer over the next few sessions as James tried to be more open. He described how he never actually had sex with either Dominique or Marcie but that the three of them went to group sex parties together and had sex with other people whilst watching each other. He found the parties both exciting and disturbing. He was often afraid he wouldn’t be able to ‘perform’ but when he did, he left exhilarated and this kept him ‘feeling good the whole week’. He didn’t want to give up this lifestyle and indeed he doubted he would be able to, even if Grazyna came back to London and moved in with him.

接下来的几次咨询中，随着詹姆斯逐渐敞开心扉，他所说的“OK”的含义也变得清晰起来。他描述了自己从未真正与多米尼克或玛茜发生过性关系，但他们三人经常一起参加多人性爱派对，在彼此观看的情况下与其他人发生性关系。他觉得这些派对既刺激又令人不安。他常常担心自己“无法勃起”，但一旦成功，他就会感到无比兴奋，这种感觉能让他“整整一周都心情愉悦”。他不想放弃这种生活方式，事实上，他怀疑自己是否能够做到，即便格拉齐娜回到伦敦和他一起生活。

One day, James turned up in an agitated state and started talking again about how his nights were still disturbed and how, when he did manage to sleep, he was plagued by dreams. I asked him to tell me about any he could recall. At first, he was evasive, saying he knew the dreams were scary and weird, but he was unable to remember any of the particulars. I waited and then said, ‘Really, you can’t remember anything?’ He then began to describe a recurring image that had been troubling him.

一天，詹姆斯情绪激动地来了，又开始说他晚上睡不好，即使睡着了，也总是被噩梦缠身。我问他能不能回忆起一些梦境。起初他闪烁其词，只说他知道那些梦很可怕也很怪异，但他记不起任何细节。我等了一会儿，然后问：“真的，你什么都记不起来了？”这时，他开始描述一个反复出现的、一直困扰着他的画面。

‘There’s this long pathway in a park with a hedgerow on one side and oak trees on the other. I think it’s Regent’s Park, where I used to run when I first came to live in London. I know that I’m absolutely parched and I must get a drink. I think there’s a fountain nearby but I can’t see it, even though I can hear water gushing and cascading all around me. I keep walking and walking towards the sound of the water but I can’t get any closer and can’t see where it’s coming from. I’m starting to panic because I’m dying of thirst.’ He stopped, frowned and said, ‘I can’t remember any more. Maybe that’s when I woke up?’

“公园里有一条长长的步道，一边是树篱，另一边是橡树。我想那是摄政公园，我刚来伦敦的时候经常在那里跑步。我知道我渴极了，必须得喝点水。我想附近应该有个喷泉，但我看不到，尽管我能听到周围潺潺的流水声。我一直朝着水声走去，但就是走不近，也看不到水是从哪里来的。我开始慌了，因为我快渴死了。”他停了下来，皱着眉头说：“我什么都记不起来了。也许我就是那时候醒的？”

I waited a bit to see if he wanted to say more and then asked, ‘What do you make of it?’

我等了一会儿，看看他是否还想多说几句，然后问道：“你对此有何看法？”

There was a pause.

一阵沉默。

‘I lay there a long time after that dream; I couldn’t get back to sleep. I felt really uncomfortable about it and haven’t been able to get it out of my mind.’ He paused again and we were silent together. Then he said, ‘The path, in the dream, is very scary – it’s a scary feeling walking to that fountain, or whatever it is.’

“做完那个梦之后，我躺在那里很久，再也睡不着了。我感觉很不舒服，一直挥之不去。”他又停顿了一下，我们俩都沉默了一会儿。然后他说：“梦里的那条路很可怕——走到那个喷泉，或者不管它是什么，都让人感到害怕。”

I asked him if he knew why he’d been so unsure about sharing this with me. It seemed he was quite troubled and scared by the dream, yet I had had to press him to hear it.

我问他知不知道为什么一直犹豫要不要跟我分享这个梦。看来他被这个梦困扰得挺厉害，也很害怕，但我还是得追问他才肯说出来。

He said that his nights were completely different from his days and he wasn’t sure he wanted me to know that much about him. ‘In the day, I feel generally OK, good even. But at night, especially when I can’t sleep, I feel …’ He struggled to find the words. ‘I suppose I feel a bit pathetic telling you I’ve been freaked out by a stupid dream.’

他说他的夜晚和白天截然不同，他不太确定是否想让我了解他这么多。“白天，我感觉一般都还好，甚至感觉不错。但到了晚上，尤其是我睡不着的时候，我就觉得……”他一时语塞。“我想我有点儿丢人，居然跟你说我被一个愚蠢的梦吓坏了。”

I said, ‘Perhaps that’s what the dream is about?’ He looked at me quizzically, so I went on. ‘Perhaps I’m the fountain in your dream? You know you need help but find it shameful to ask for it; in the dream, you’re desperate for something but feel scared to go towards it. It seems to me the dream is about your fear of needing me … perhaps of needing anyone?’

我说：“也许这就是梦的含义？”他疑惑地看着我，于是我继续说道：“也许我就是梦里的喷泉？你知道你需要帮助，却又羞于开口；在梦里，你渴望得到某样东西，却又害怕去追求。在我看来，这个梦是关于你害怕需要我……或许是害怕需要任何人？”

He looked at me intently and then simply said, ‘Maybe.’

他专注地看着我，然后简单地说：“也许吧。”

The following session, James didn’t turn up. No text or call to explain. Later that evening I emailed him, saying I was sorry he hadn’t come and hoped everything was OK.

下一次课程，詹姆斯没来。既没有短信也没有电话解释。当天晚上晚些时候，我给他发了邮件，表示很遗憾他没来，并希望他一切都好。

It was three days before I heard back from him. He left a message to say he was sorry he’d missed the session; he’d had to go to New York for work and was still there. He hoped to see me the following week. Was this his way of stepping back from any suggestion he might really need the work with me? I thought that he was ‘taking back control’ and letting me know that my suggestion that he was frightened of being dependent on me had been too much. I had probably hit the mark but that didn’t mean he liked it or could bear to know it.

三天后我才收到他的回复。他留言说很抱歉错过了这次咨询；他因为工作去了纽约，现在还在那里。他希望下周能见到我。这是不是他在回避我暗示他可能真的需要我的帮助？我当时觉得他是在“重新掌控局面”，让我意识到我之前暗示他害怕依赖我的话可能太过分了。我可能说对了，但这并不意味着他喜欢这样，或者能够承受这样的事实。

James had told me a little about his childhood, though only when I asked. His parents had divorced when he was a baby and by the time he was aged five, both had remarried and had new families. Suddenly, he wasn’t an only child but found himself surrounded by half-brothers and step-siblings. He spent his time travelling between his father’s home in Wandsworth and his mother in Woking, and, from the age of eight, his boarding school in Suffolk. He said that he’d felt most at home at school but that he’d never really felt as if he belonged anywhere. In one of our sessions, he told me about a Christmas when he was aged about eleven. He’d been going to spend Christmas Day with his mother and his stepfather but at the last minute this had changed because his baby half-brother had become quite ill. His father picked him up from Woking and took him back to the Wandsworth house late on Christmas Eve. The following morning, everyone realised that all his presents had been left in Woking. He had nothing to open, no stocking or anything, and had to watch whilst everyone else opened theirs.

詹姆斯跟我讲过一些他的童年往事，不过只有在我问起的时候他才会说。他还是个婴儿的时候父母就离婚了，到他五岁的时候，两人都再婚组建了新的家庭。突然间，他不再是独生子，而是被同父异母的兄弟姐妹和继兄弟姐妹包围着。他经常往返于父亲在旺兹沃思的家和母亲在沃金的家之间，从八岁起，他还要去萨福克郡的寄宿学校上学。他说，他在学校里感觉最自在，但他从来没有真正觉得自己属于任何地方。在我们的一次谈话中，他跟我讲了他大约十一岁那年的圣诞节。他原本打算和母亲以及继父一起过圣诞节，但最后一刻计划改变了，因为他同父异母的弟弟病得很重。平安夜那天晚上，他父亲很晚才从沃金接他回旺兹沃思的家。第二天早上，大家才发现他所有的礼物都留在了沃金。他什么都没有，没有袜子之类的东西，只能眼巴巴地看着其他人打开他们的礼物。

I felt moved listening to this memory that conveyed something deeply painful about being left out and not feeling cared for. He didn’t cry as he talked to me but he reached for a tissue, breathing deeply and slowly as if attempting to gain control over his emotions.

听着这段回忆，我深受触动，它传递出一种被冷落、不被关爱的痛苦。他跟我说话时没有哭，只是伸手去拿纸巾，深呼吸，仿佛在努力控制自己的情绪。

When James returned, we began to talk more about his dislike of feeling he needed anyone. He told me he wouldn’t even have a cleaner and scrubbed his own floors because he couldn’t bear it when she had let him down. We explored how he feared being let down by Grazyna and I suggested maybe that was why he needed at least two girlfriends, so he could protect himself by having ‘safety in numbers’. He had back-ups; if Grazyna wasn’t available, he had Marcie. If Marcie was cool or distant, he had Dominique. In this way, he never had to fear being let down; he kept his distance and thereby kept them needy, so he never had to be.

詹姆斯回来后，我们开始更多地谈论他不喜欢依赖任何人的感觉。他告诉我，他甚至连清洁工都不请，自己擦地板，因为他受不了被格拉齐娜辜负。我们探讨了他害怕被格拉齐娜辜负的原因，我建议他或许正是因为害怕被辜负才需要至少两个女朋友，这样他就能“人多势众”地保护自己。他有备选方案：如果格拉齐娜不在，他还有玛茜；如果玛茜冷淡疏远，他还有多米尼克。这样一来，他就永远不必担心被辜负；他保持距离，让她们对他有所依赖，这样他就永远不必真正依赖她们。

During the session, we also explored why he was so attached to the sex parties. What was it about watching Marcie and Dominique that was so compelling? It seemed a complete puzzle but at the next session he began to talk about his twin half-brothers and how he’d been to watch them play a gig at the weekend. They were, he said, exceptionally talented. They’d both been in TV shows when they were children and the younger twin had also been an amazing footballer. Now they were in this folk duo and becoming quite successful. I wondered if their achievements had been hard for him when he was growing up, if he’d felt jealous and competitive with them?

在咨询过程中，我们也探讨了他为何如此沉迷于性派对。观看玛茜和多米尼克的表演究竟有何魔力？这似乎完全是个谜，但在下次咨询中，他开始谈起他的双胞胎同父异母兄弟，以及他周末去看他们演出的经历。他说，他们才华横溢。他们小时候都上过电视节目，弟弟还是个出色的足球运动员。如今，他们组成了一个民谣二人组，并且相当成功。我不禁好奇，他们的成就是否在他成长过程中给他带来了压力，他是否曾感到嫉妒和竞争？

‘I spent a lot of time going to their games or their plays or whatever when I was growing up. It got a bit much at times,’ he admitted, laughing. ‘I tried to do the good big brother kind of thing but it was frustrating that no one ever seemed interested in what I was up to. I’d come home from boarding school for the weekend and then have to go and watch Danny play football or go to some stupid carol concert. And when I went to Dad’s, I always seemed to end up having to go and watch Lily in some ballet performance. Not much fun for a teenage boy,’ he said, smiling ruefully.

“我小时候经常去看他们的比赛、演出什么的，有时候真的有点儿太多了，”他笑着承认道。“我努力想做个好哥哥，但让人沮丧的是，好像没人关心我的近况。周末从寄宿学校回家，我又得去看丹尼踢足球，或者去参加什么无聊的圣诞颂歌音乐会。去爸爸家，我总是不得不去看莉莉的芭蕾舞表演。对一个十几岁的男孩来说，这可没什么乐趣可言，”他苦笑着说道。

I commented that it was interesting that he felt he’d spent much of his childhood being an onlooker and reminded him of the Christmas he’d described to me, when he watched everyone open their presents, whilst he had none. I thought that this position of being on the outside, always watching, had probably been painful for him and made him feel neglected and as though he didn’t really belong.

我评论说，他觉得自己童年大部分时间都像个旁观者，这很有意思。这让我想起了他跟我描述的那个圣诞节：他看着大家都在拆礼物，而他自己却什么也没有。我想，这种被排斥在外、总是旁观的感觉，对他来说可能很痛苦，让他觉得自己被忽视了，好像自己不属于这里。

He looked at me and said, ‘Yes, that’s exactly the feeling I had this weekend at the concert. I watched my mother and she literally couldn’t take her eyes off my brothers.’

他看着我说：“是的，我这个周末在音乐会上就是这种感觉。我看着我妈妈，她的目光简直无法从我兄弟身上移开。”

We sat in silence for a while and then I said, ‘It’s striking, given what you’ve just described, that you seem to be taking this onlooker position at these sex parties.’

我们沉默了一会儿，然后我说：“考虑到你刚才的描述，令人惊讶的是，你似乎在这些性派对中采取了一种旁观者的态度。”

‘I guess, yeah.’

“我想是的。”

We talked then about how although being an observer was difficult for him, it seemed he liked watching at the parties.

我们当时谈到，虽然对他来说做个旁观者很困难，但他似乎喜欢在聚会上观察别人。

‘I think at the sex parties you can be in control,’ I ventured. ‘You can turn the painful onlooker experience into something exciting, in which you’re kind of orchestrating the whole thing. It’s a way of gaining control over the thing you fear most.’

“我觉得在性派对上你可以掌控一切，”我试探性地说。“你可以把痛苦的旁观体验变成令人兴奋的事情，你可以掌控整个过程。这是一种掌控你最恐惧之事的方式。”

He nodded. ‘Fear most?’ he asked.

他点点头。“最害怕什么？”他问道。

‘Yes, the fear of being excluded; being the outsider; having no place …’

“是的，害怕被排斥；害怕成为局外人；害怕无处容身……”

The fear of exclusion is a universal experience. I remember as a child how much I hated any feeling of being left out, whether it was not being chosen for the netball team or hearing my parents’ absorbed conversation downstairs whilst I lay alone in bed. Even now, as a grown woman, in that awkward moment at the end of a meeting, when people break into huddles to chat, I always tremble inside, fearing I’ll have no one to talk to and, as a result, I rarely wait around to find out. This anxiety about exclusion stems from our earliest realisation that our one-to-one bonds, with mothers and fathers, are not actually exclusive. They are ‘playing away’ with each other and with our siblings; they are ‘unfaithful’ to us, interested and engaged with others. What a tragedy. What a betrayal. We don’t come first! This is a shocking, painful and potentially life-threatening realisation, because when this discovery is made, we are, in fact, completely dependent on our parents. Dependent for food, for shelter, for care and, indeed, for survival itself. For many people, intimate relationships revive these early terrors and a confusion between adult dependency and infantile dependency ensues. This confusion, which stimulates deep fears around survival, drives us to protect ourselves from this terror by building walls and defences that help us avoid any situation where we might feel dependent and vulnerable.

害怕被排斥是一种普遍的体验。我记得小时候，我多么讨厌被冷落的感觉，无论是没被选进篮球队，还是独自躺在床上听着父母在楼下热烈地交谈。即使现在，作为一个成年女性，在会议结束时，当人们三五成群地聚在一起聊天时，我总是内心忐忑不安，害怕自己无人可说。因此，我很少会留下来等待。这种被排斥的焦虑源于我们最早意识到，我们与父母的亲密关系并非真正专属。他们会和彼此玩耍，也会和我们的兄弟姐妹玩耍；他们“背叛”了我们，对其他人更感兴趣。多么悲剧！多么背叛！我们并非他们的第一位！这是一个令人震惊、痛苦，甚至可能危及生命的认知，因为当我们意识到这一点时，我们实际上完全依赖于父母。我们依赖他人获取食物、住所、照料，乃至生存本身。对许多人来说，亲密关系会唤起这些早期的恐惧，导致成人依赖与婴儿依赖之间的混淆。这种混淆会引发对生存的深层恐惧，驱使我们筑起高墙和防御体系来保护自己，避免任何可能让我们感到依赖和脆弱的境地。

In James’s case, this meant developing a persona that hid his fragility and through which he could charm and manipulate his lovers, thereby maintaining an illusion of control. But the saddest part is that the thing he feared most, the catastrophe he was trying to avoid, of being desperate and helpless like an infant, had, in fact, already happened. Donald Winnicott, the wise psychoanalyst who has written so eloquently about a child’s inner world, explains that when traumatic things happen to us in infancy it is impossible for us to make sense of and process the experience. At that stage in life, infants simply aren’t equipped to reflect and understand all the feelings linked to the trauma. And so, adults who’ve experienced trauma in infancy carry these unprocessed feelings into adulthood; they sit deep inside them as a fear about a disaster that is coming, when in fact it’s already happened.

对詹姆斯而言，这意味着他要塑造一个能够掩盖自身脆弱的形象，并以此魅力和操控他的爱人，从而维持一种掌控一切的假象。但最令人悲哀的是，他最恐惧的事情，他试图避免的灾难——像婴儿般绝望无助——实际上已经发生了。唐纳德·温尼科特是一位睿智的精神分析学家，他曾对儿童的内心世界进行过精辟的论述。他解释说，当我们在婴儿时期经历创伤时，我们根本无法理解和处理这些经历。在那个阶段，婴儿根本不具备反思和理解与创伤相关的所有感受的能力。因此，经历过婴儿期创伤的成年人会将这些未经处理的感受带入成年；它们深深地潜藏在他们内心，成为对即将到来的灾难的恐惧，而事实上，灾难早已发生。

For James, it seemed this trauma had occurred around the breakdown of his parents’ marriage and the consequent loss of a secure base that made him feel safe and held. Over the months, as we explored his childhood, I got such an acute sense of a very little boy shuffled between his mother and father, both of whom were preoccupied with themselves, their new partners and their new babies. It was as though, too early, he’d been dropped from his parents’ minds and, unable to cope with these feelings of exclusion and rejection, he had built a castle inside himself to protect him from the pain.

对詹姆斯来说，这种创伤似乎源于父母婚姻的破裂，以及随之而来的失去安全感和归属感。几个月来，随着我们深入探究他的童年，我强烈地感受到，这个小男孩夹在父母之间，而他的父母都忙于自己、各自的新伴侣和新生儿。仿佛他过早地被父母遗忘，无法承受这种被排斥和拒绝的感受，他便在内心深处筑起了一座城堡，保护自己免受痛苦。

Did this understanding mark a turning point? Things seemed to carry on pretty much as before, except that he began to talk about Grazyna. For the first time, I had a sense of her as a real person and I started to see just how involved James was with her.

这种理解是否标志着一个转折点？一切似乎都和以前一样，只是他开始谈论格拉齐娜。我第一次感觉她像个活生生的人，也开始明白詹姆斯和她之间究竟有多么深厚。

It was March when the crisis happened. It was something I’d been half expecting and in hindsight was almost inevitable. It was a Sunday evening when James texted me to ask if he could see me urgently; he couldn’t wait until Thursday. Grazyna had found out about him and Marcie and she’d broken it off. I texted him back and we agreed to meet on Tuesday.

危机发生在三月。其实我之前就有所预感，现在回想起来，几乎是不可避免的。那是一个星期天的晚上，詹姆斯发短信问我能不能赶紧见他，他等不了到星期四。格拉齐娜发现了詹姆斯和玛茜的事，已经和他分手了。我回复了他，我们约好星期二见面。

James looked broken when he arrived – not crisp and assured but fragile and uncared for. Straight away, he launched into telling me he’d been in Paris with Grazyna. He’d arrived late and gone straight into the shower, leaving his mobile phone on the kitchen counter right by where Grazyna was preparing him dinner. His phone had pinged and Grazyna had picked it up and seen a suggestive message from Marcie, which clearly signalled there was something sexual between them.

詹姆斯到的时候看起来很憔悴——不再是神采奕奕、自信满满，而是脆弱不堪、无人照料。他一到就跟我说他和格拉齐娜去了巴黎。他到得晚，直接冲了个澡，把手机放在厨房台面上，格拉齐娜正在那里给他准备晚餐。他的手机响了，格拉齐娜拿起来一看，发现是玛茜发来的一条暧昧短信，显然暗示着他们之间有暧昧关系。

This time, in the consulting room, James did cry. What was he to do? He’d fucked everything up and it was all hopeless. He’d been trying to get straight by coming to see me but now it was too late and he’d lost Grazyna.

这一次，在咨询室里，詹姆斯哭了。他该怎么办？他把一切都搞砸了，一切都没希望了。他来找我，是想改过自新，但现在太晚了，他失去了格拉齐娜。

Two days later, he was back for his regular session. He was in a tracksuit and said he’d taken a couple of days off work to go and see Grazyna in Paris. She was still very angry with him but he was hopeful he might win her back. He told me he’d had the dream again. Again, he was in the park and there was a fountain and he wanted to drink but couldn’t find the water. This time, however, he saw the fountain – it was one of those huge Victorian tiered ones. It was bright and white and looked like it was fragile and could crumble. He still couldn’t reach it though and he was still desperate to drink.

两天后，他像往常一样回来接受治疗。他穿着运动服，说他请了两天假去巴黎看望格拉齐娜。她仍然很生他的气，但他希望能够挽回她的心。他告诉我他又做了那个梦。梦里他又一次出现在公园里，那里有一个喷泉，他想喝水，却找不到水。不过这次，他看到了喷泉——那是一座巨大的维多利亚式多层喷泉。它洁白明亮，看起来脆弱不堪，仿佛随时都会坍塌。但他仍然够不着水，仍然渴望喝水。

I asked him if he had any more thoughts about the dream and about the fountain and he said that actually it looked like an enormous cake. ‘A wedding cake?’ I asked. And he nodded vigorously – yes, just like that.

我问他对梦境和喷泉还有什么想法，他说其实它看起来像个巨大的蛋糕。“婚礼蛋糕？”我问。他用力地点了点头——对，就是这样。

In July, nearly a year after we began work, Grazyna moved in with him and when I returned in September, he came eagerly to the session to tell me she was pregnant. Something had shifted in him but both of us knew that the work we were doing together was by no means finished.

七月，在我们开始咨询近一年后，格拉齐娜搬来和他同住。九月我再次来咨询时，他兴高采烈地告诉我她怀孕了。他身上发生了一些变化，但我们俩都知道，我们共同努力的成果远未完成。

James’s journey towards marriage involved a confrontation with the need and vulnerability he’d worked hard his whole life to avoid. Through the affairs and the casual use of women, he’d maintained an illusion of power and control, triumphing over the part of him that he hated and felt was too needy and fragile. In the therapy, these different parts of him were exposed and through this sense of being held and known, he began the process of understanding and accepting his ordinary human need for love and security.

詹姆斯的婚姻之路，是一场直面他毕生都在努力逃避的需求和脆弱的旅程。通过婚外情和随意玩弄女性，他维持着一种权力与控制的假象，以此来压制他内心深处那个他憎恨的、过于依赖和脆弱的部分。在治疗过程中，他这些不同的面向被揭露出来，在被接纳和理解的感受中，他开始理解并接受自己作为人类对爱与安全感的平凡需求。
