Red Riding Hood Protects the Wolf in Sheep’s Clothing

小红帽保护披着羊皮的狼

Betrayal is a fact of life; I doubt there is an adult alive that hasn’t felt its sting. To trust someone always poses a risk of treachery; realistic trust involves knowing and accepting this. But accepting that loved ones will, at times, lie, cheat or let you down, doesn’t mean that every betrayal is forgivable.

背叛是人生常态；我想，世上恐怕没有哪个成年人没尝过背叛的滋味。信任他人总是伴随着被背叛的风险；真正的信任需要了解并接受这一点。但是，接受所爱之人有时会说谎、欺骗或让你失望，并不意味着每一次背叛都可以被原谅。

Pippa and Claudine, a married couple in their early forties, came to see me because for several years Claudine had been suffering with a mysterious ME-like illness, which, from time to time, made her extremely ill. For nearly three years, Claudine had been investigated for strokes, asthma, multiple sclerosis and labyrinthitis – all conditions that might have explained why, at times, she would lose her balance and fall, black out or take to her bed with exhaustion. The tests found nothing conclusive, so the couple developed an understanding between them that Claudine had an atypical form of chronic fatigue syndrome or, as it’s sometimes called, ME.

四十出头的皮帕和克劳迪娜是一对夫妇，她们来找我看病，因为克劳迪娜多年来一直饱受一种神秘的、类似肌痛性脑脊髓炎（ME）的疾病折磨，这种疾病时不时会让她感到非常虚弱。近三年来，克劳迪娜接受过中风、哮喘、多发性硬化症和迷路炎等各种检查——这些疾病或许都能解释她为何有时会失去平衡摔倒、昏厥或精疲力竭地卧床不起。然而，所有检查结果都未能确诊，于是这对夫妇逐渐达成共识：克劳迪娜患有一种非典型慢性疲劳综合征，也就是我们常说的肌痛性脑脊髓炎（ME）。

Some months after this ‘diagnosis’, Claudine seemed to become increasingly unwell, which resulted in her becoming bed bound. She was unable to work or help in the house, prompting Pippa, in despair, to insist on further tests. Referred by their GP, Claudine underwent more hospital investigations, which once again drew a blank. No medical professional was able to identify any underlying condition that could account for her complete exhaustion, her occasional fainting fits and the myriad other symptoms she was suffering from.

在这次“诊断”几个月后，克劳迪娜的病情似乎越来越严重，最终卧床不起。她无法工作，也无法帮忙做家务，这让皮帕绝望不已，坚持要求做进一步检查。经家庭医生转诊，克劳迪娜接受了更多医院检查，但结果依然一无所获。没有一位医生能够找出任何潜在的病因，来解释她极度疲惫、偶尔晕厥以及其他种种症状。

Months passed and Claudine remained an invalid until a good friend suggested to Pippa that they try another specialist who worked in Paris. This doctor ran a clinic specifically dedicated to chronic, disabling and diffuse conditions, such as seemed to be afflicting Claudine. It was expensive and money was tight but there appeared to be no other option but to give it a try.

几个月过去了，克劳迪娜依然卧病在床，直到一位好友建议皮帕去巴黎找一位专科医生。这位医生开办了一家专门治疗慢性、致残性和弥漫性疾病的诊所，克劳迪娜似乎就患有这些疾病。虽然费用昂贵，而她们的经济状况又很拮据，但似乎别无选择，只能试一试。

In the meantime, Pippa had been supporting the family financially and managing the household, caring not only for Claudine but also for Claudine’s 12-year-old daughter, Milly. Pippa was becoming frantic with worry, fearful that Claudine would never get well and without a diagnosis, she fretted that something terrible was about to happen, even that Claudine might die.

与此同时，皮帕一直在经济上支持着这个家庭，操持着家务，不仅照顾克劳迪娜，还照顾克劳迪娜12岁的女儿米莉。皮帕越来越焦虑，害怕克劳迪娜永远好不了，而且由于没有确诊，她担心会发生可怕的事情，甚至担心克劳迪娜会去世。

Eventually the money was found and, leaving Milly behind with a friend, the couple travelled to Paris. Despite the nature of the trip, they were excited. They’d never been on the Eurostar before and it was years since they’d been away from home alone. At the first appointment, the nurse took some blood and urine. The results, later that day, were as shocking as they were devastating. Claudine had an extremely high reading for opioids. Was this an aberration? What could it mean?

最终他们找到了钱，把米莉托付给朋友照顾后，这对夫妇前往巴黎。尽管此行的目的并非如此，他们依然兴奋不已。他们从未乘坐过欧洲之星，而且已经多年没有独自离家了。第一次就诊时，护士抽取了他们的血液和尿液样本。当天晚些时候的检测结果令人震惊，也令人崩溃。克劳迪娜的阿片类药物含量极高。这只是异常现象吗？这又意味着什么呢？

They spent a hellish night, with tearful accusations and tearful denials, but the following morning, in the presence of the doctor, Claudine finally confessed she’d been abusing opioid painkillers for years. Her consumption had varied but she had avoided taking the medications entirely only when she’d been having tests. She didn’t have atypical MS, or some other unknown ailment, she was, simply, a drug addict. At this moment of crisis, as Claudine emerged from her detox, they sought therapy with me.

他们度过了一个噩梦般的夜晚，泪流满面地互相指责、互相否认，但第二天早上，在医生的面前，克劳迪娜终于承认自己滥用阿片类止痛药多年。她的用药量时有时无，但只有在做检查的时候才会完全停药。她没有非典型多发性硬化症，也没有其他什么不明疾病，她只是个瘾君子。在这个危机时刻，克劳迪娜戒断成功后，他们寻求了我的帮助。

This dishonesty felt to Pippa like a monstrous betrayal and she told me that Claudine’s secret drug abuse felt as unforgivable as any affair. Pippa confessed in that first session that she was on the verge of initiating a separation and I couldn’t help thinking that I really didn’t blame her. But any idea of leaving was impossible because Claudine, in the face of this threat, would withdraw into the most profound and deathly silence that scared Pippa witless.

这种不诚实在皮帕看来简直是骇人的背叛，她告诉我，克劳迪娜秘密吸毒的行为和任何婚外情一样不可饶恕。在第一次咨询中，皮帕坦白说她几乎就要提出分居，我不禁觉得我真的不怪她。但任何离开的想法都不可能实现，因为克劳迪娜一面对这种威胁，就会陷入一种深不见底、死一般的沉默，这让皮帕感到无比恐惧。

It was quite a challenge to hold onto the position central to any couple therapist of interest and attention to the shared aspects of the presenting issues as, in those early sessions, I felt downright punitive towards Claudine and protective of Pippa. But gradually, it began to be clear that there had been a strong, unconscious collusion between the couple and I could see that Pippa had turned a very blind eye to Claudine’s drug abuse in order to avoid something much worse.

对于任何一位伴侣治疗师来说，要保持对双方共同问题的关注和重视，都是一项不小的挑战。在最初的几次咨询中，我甚至对克劳迪娜充满了惩罚的意味，同时又极力保护着皮帕。但渐渐地，我开始意识到这对伴侣之间存在着一种强烈的、无意识的默契。我看得出，皮帕对克劳迪娜的吸毒行为视而不见，是为了避免更糟糕的事情发生。

As they talked more about the past and as Pippa railed against the lies, I began to wonder why Pippa had ignored so many tell-tale signs. Why had she overlooked the withdrawal of cash from their bank account with no satisfactory explanation? I felt sceptical when Pippa told me that she’d believed that the pill bottles she found hidden behind the shed had been chucked over the fence by local kids, as Claudine asserted. It became more and more clear that Pippa had overlooked all the signs. What was less clear was why.

随着她们对往事的深入交谈，以及皮帕对谎言的反驳，我开始疑惑，为什么皮帕会忽略那么多蛛丝马迹。为什么她会对银行账户里的现金取款一事视而不见，而且没有任何合理的解释？当皮帕告诉我，她相信克劳迪娜所说的，藏在棚子后面的药瓶是当地孩子扔过来的时，我感到十分怀疑。越来越明显的是，皮帕忽略了所有迹象。但究竟为什么，却始终是个谜。

It took some weeks for us to talk about anything other than the drug taking and the lies. Every session was hot with anger and shame, which left no room for gentle exploration. But during one session, as I became more and more puzzled by this couple, I insisted that they make space, between the forensic examination of the betrayals, to tell me something about their childhood and their families.

我们花了几个星期才开始谈论除了吸毒和谎言之外的其他话题。每次咨询都充满了愤怒和羞耻，根本没有空间进行温和的探讨。但在一次咨询中，随着我对这对夫妇越来越感到困惑，我坚持要求他们在深入剖析彼此背叛行为之余，抽出一些时间，向我讲述他们的童年和家庭。

‘I’m not sure Claudine will be up for talking about it, will you?’ Pippa said protectively. ‘I can tell you about mine though, if that’s of any help?’ Pippa was always like this, chatty and co-operative, whilst Claudine was often very silent. I nodded and Pippa began.

“我不确定克劳迪娜是否愿意谈论这件事，你呢？”皮帕带着保护的语气说道，“不过我可以跟你说说我的经历，或许对你有帮助？”皮帕总是这样，健谈又乐于助人，而克劳迪娜则常常沉默寡言。我点点头，皮帕便开始讲述起来。

‘Gosh. I haven’t really thought about my family for years! I see my sister from time to time but never my brother or my dad. My brother lives in Oman. My dad, well, he’s a real oddball. I don’t think he wants to see me and I don’t want to see him either. It’s mutual!’ she concluded, laughing. I waited, hoping she’d say more, but she seemed to think that was enough and nudged Claudine with her elbow to get her to talk. ‘Claudine’s got a real story. She had a tough time growing up.’

“哎呀，我已经好几年没怎么想起我的家人了！我偶尔会见到我姐姐，但从来不见我哥哥或爸爸。我哥哥住在阿曼。至于我爸爸嘛，他真是个怪人。我觉得他不想见我，我也不想见他。我们彼此都不想见他！”她笑着总结道。我等着她继续说下去，希望她能说更多，但她似乎觉得够了，便用胳膊肘轻轻碰了碰克劳迪娜，示意她继续说下去。“克劳迪娜的故事很感人。她小时候过得很艰难。”

Claudine was no more forthcoming than Pippa but reluctantly she told me she’d been in and out of care during her childhood, until, at 12, she was fostered and then adopted by Delia, who she now thought of as her mum. She’d not seen or heard from either of her blood parents for years but when Milly was born, she’d got in contact with her biological mother.

克劳迪娜和皮帕一样，都不太愿意透露太多，但她还是勉强告诉我，她童年时期一直在不同的寄养家庭辗转，直到12岁那年，她被德莉娅收养，现在她把德莉娅当成自己的妈妈。她已经很多年没见过或联系过自己的亲生父母了，但米莉出生后，她联系上了亲生母亲。

‘It was a mistake. I thought maybe she’d be older, wiser, more up for being a grandma or something. But she’s just not someone I want anything to do with now.’

“这是个错误。我以为她年纪更大一些，更成熟一些，更适合当奶奶什么的。但现在我根本不想和她有任何瓜葛。”

‘Why were you taken into care, Claudine? Do you know?’ I asked, wondering what she’d suffered as a child.

“克劳迪娜，你为什么会被送去福利院？你知道吗？”我问道，想知道她小时候遭受过什么苦难。

‘I’ve been told that I was about one, the first time I went into care. My mum was using heroin and she was still with my dad.’ She paused, pressing her lips firmly together and, like Pippa, it was clear she wanted to leave it there, so I didn’t push her.

“我听说我大概一岁的时候第一次被送去福利院。我妈妈当时在吸食海洛因，而且她还和我爸爸在一起。”她停顿了一下，紧紧地抿着嘴唇，和皮帕一样，很明显她想就此打住，所以我没有追问。

After they left, I made my way upstairs. The day was turning out colder than I’d thought and I needed to retrieve a cardigan before I saw my next patient. I put on the cardigan and went to the mirror and, as I stood by it, near the open window, I could hear a loud voice in the street below. Looking out, I saw Pippa and Claudine standing by a beaten-up old green Fiat across the road. Pippa’s voice was raised and though I couldn’t hear her words, I could hear the tone and I could see from Claudine’s shrunken and slumped profile that she was in receipt of a serious telling-off.

他们走后，我上了楼。天气比我想象的要冷，我得在见下一位病人之前去拿件开衫。我穿上开衫，走到镜子前，站在敞开的窗户旁，听到楼下街上传来大声的说话声。我向外望去，看到皮帕和克劳迪娜站在马路对面一辆破旧的绿色菲亚特旁边。皮帕提高了嗓门，虽然我听不清她说了什么，但我能听出她的语气，而且从克劳迪娜蜷缩着身子、佝偻着的侧脸来看，她显然是被狠狠地训了一顿。

As we went on with the therapy, the little bit of their childhood history they’d shared began to help me make sense of their intense and lopsided relationship. It was evident that Claudine behaved in many ways like a child. Even now, though she claimed to have stopped abusing drugs for nearly six months, Pippa would bring her breakfast in bed. Claudine, who was a freelance editor, had begun to take on projects again but she struggled to complete and finish the work. Then Pippa would step in to help her and Claudine would immediately step back and allow her to do so. Claudine clearly wanted – needed, perhaps – for Pippa to mummy her and being helpless triggered that attention. Her drug abuse had tamped down painful feelings and collapsed her into a dependent, childlike state, secure in the knowledge that Pippa would be there to catch her.

随着治疗的进行，她们共同经历的那点童年往事开始帮助我理解她们之间那种强烈而又不对等的关系。很明显，克劳迪娜在很多方面都像个孩子。即使现在，尽管她声称已经戒毒近六个月了，皮帕还是会给她送早餐到床上。克劳迪娜是一名自由编辑，她开始重新接手一些项目，但却难以完成。这时，皮帕就会介入帮助她，而克劳迪娜则会立刻退到一边，任由皮帕去做。克劳迪娜显然渴望——或许是需要——皮帕像妈妈一样照顾她，而她的无助恰恰激发了这种渴望。毒品让她压抑了痛苦的情感，使她陷入一种依赖的、孩子气的状态，她深信皮帕会在那里接住她。

One Tuesday morning, the air cold but the sky bright, Pippa arrived on her own. Claudine, it seemed, wouldn’t get out of bed to come to the session. I felt irritated with Claudine and that irritation increased as I heard how Pippa had tried to rouse her, had taken her breakfast, had dropped Milly at school, had gone back and brought her a cup of coffee – but all to no avail. Claudine wasn’t getting out of bed.

一个星期二的早晨，空气寒冷，但天空晴朗，皮帕独自一人来了。克劳迪娜似乎赖在床上不肯来上课。我有点儿生克劳迪娜的气，后来听说皮帕如何努力叫醒她，给她吃了早饭，送米莉去上学，又回去给她带了杯咖啡——但这一切都无济于事——我的气就更重了。克劳迪娜就是不肯起床。

‘Do you think she’s been using?’ I asked.

“你觉得她是不是吸毒了？”我问。

‘I don’t think so. No. She wouldn’t do that. I’m sure she wouldn’t,’ Pippa said, shaking her head. There was a silence between us and I watched as Pippa took in my question properly.

“我不这么认为。不，她不会那样做的。我肯定她不会。”皮帕摇了摇头说道。我们之间沉默了一会儿，我看着皮帕认真地听着我的问题。

‘Why would you say that?’ Her voice was querulous.

“你为什么这么说？”她语气中带着责备。

‘Well, I might ask why you haven’t considered that?’

“那么，我倒想问问你为什么没有考虑过这一点呢？”

‘I don’t think you understand what’s been going on. There’s no way Claud would use now. She knows it would break my heart.’

“我觉得你根本不明白发生了什么。克劳德现在绝对不会用这招。她知道这会让我心碎。”

I sat silently. I knew that she had to find her own way to her doubt.

我静静地坐着。我知道她必须自己找到消除疑虑的方法。

‘I don’t know. I don’t know what to say. What d’you want me to say?’ she said angrily.

“我不知道。我不知道该说什么。你想让我说什么？”她生气地说。

‘I don’t want you to say anything, Pippa, but I do notice that it seems difficult for you to acknowledge or even allow yourself to feel any frustration or anger with Claudine. It seems easier to direct it at me. And I do wonder why that might be?’

“皮帕，我不想让你说什么，但我注意到你似乎很难承认，甚至很难允许自己对克劳迪娜产生任何不满或愤怒。你似乎更容易把这些情绪发泄在我身上。我很好奇这是为什么呢？”

‘She’s trying and you don’t seem to get how hard it is for her.’

“她一直在努力，但你似乎不明白这对她来说有多难。”

‘I understand it’s incredibly hard for her. My question is why you ignore how hard it is, and how hard it’s been, for you ?’

“我知道这对她来说非常艰难。我的问题是，为什么你无视这对你来说有多艰难，以及你一直以来承受的痛苦？”

She bowed her head and we sat there in silence. I looked at her and thought how tired and sad she looked. Her greying black hair was scraped back into a ponytail and her hands, which were folded in her lap, looked red and sore, the fingernails bitten to the quick.

她低下了头，我们静静地坐着。我看着她，心想她看起来多么疲惫，多么悲伤。她灰白的黑发随意地扎成马尾，放在膝上的双手红肿疼痛，指甲都咬破了。

‘You’ve never really told me much about your childhood or your family Pippa.’

“皮帕，你从来没跟我说过多少关于你的童年或你的家庭的事情。”

‘Mine? I did tell you.’

“我的？我跟你说过。”

‘Not really. Just that you don’t really see them.’

“倒也不是。只是你平时看不到他们而已。”

She sighed and shrugged her shoulders. ‘Well, it wasn’t great, if that’s what you’re thinking. My dad was, is , a complete loser. Did I tell you my mum died when I was 12? I’ve been thinking she might have been an alcoholic, though, frankly, being married to him I don’t blame her …’

她叹了口气，耸了耸肩。“嗯，如果你是这么想的话，那可就糟了。我爸过去是，现在也是，一个彻头彻尾的失败者。我跟你说过我妈在我12岁的时候就去世了吗？我一直在想她是不是酗酒，不过说实话，嫁给他之后，我也不怪她……”

It took time but, over the session, she was able to give me a graphic picture of a childhood in which, as the oldest of four, she’d habitually stepped in as ‘little mother’. Her father, though a steady earner, had never behaved like an adult; he was funny and playful but would come and go erratically and seemed incapable of taking any responsibility.

虽然花了一些时间，但在咨询过程中，她逐渐向我描绘出一幅生动的童年图景：作为四个孩子中的老大，她从小就习惯性地扮演“小妈妈”的角色。她的父亲虽然收入稳定，却从未像个成年人那样行事；他风趣幽默，但行踪不定，似乎完全没有责任感。

‘And your mother?’ I asked.

“那你母亲呢？”我问。

‘I loved my mum,’ Pippa said simply. ‘She could be really fun. Sometimes she was frightening, though.’

“我爱我的妈妈，”皮帕简单地说。“她很有趣。不过，有时候她也很吓人。”

‘Frightening?’

“可怕吗？”

‘Yeah. She’d … well, lose it and then, oh, you wanted to get out of her way.’

“是啊。她会……嗯，情绪失控，然后，哦，你就只想赶紧躲开她。”

‘I wonder if you spent a lot of time trying to make sure she didn’t lose it?’ Pippa looked at me, puzzled. ‘By taking over, by mummying her. By soothing her ?’ I suggested.

“我想知道你是不是花了很多时间确保她不会崩溃？”皮帕疑惑地看着我。“通过接管一切，像妈妈一样照顾她，安抚她？”我问道。

Pippa nodded. ‘Yeah. That’s right. Spot on. I’d do anything to keep her calm. I remember once she got really raging about the ants in the kitchen. She was jumping up and down and chucking boiling water all the over the place.’ Pippa laughed.

皮帕点点头。“是啊，没错，说得对。我什么都愿意做，只要能让她冷静下来。我记得有一次她因为厨房里的蚂蚁大发雷霆，又蹦又跳，还把开水泼得到处都是。”皮帕笑了。

‘It sounds more scary than funny,’ I said, smiling ruefully.

“听起来与其说是好笑，不如说是可怕，”我苦笑着说。

‘Yeah, true. My brother got burnt. I told the ambulance man it was me … with the boiling water.’ She shrugged.

“是啊，没错。我哥哥被烫伤了。我跟救护人员说是我……用开水烫伤的。”她耸了耸肩。

As the session went on, she told me that her mother had died quite suddenly from blood poisoning. She’d gone to the doctor with a bad pain in her arm but was told it was a pulled muscle strain. Three days later, she died in hospital of sepsis. After that, 12-year-old Pippa became the ‘little mother’ of the family. Her father absented himself, leaving her in charge of her siblings. She became a little soldier mummy protecting her ‘brood’.

随着谈话的进行，她告诉我她的母亲因败血症突然去世。她母亲当时手臂剧痛，去看医生，但医生说是肌肉拉伤。三天后，她因败血症在医院去世。之后，12岁的皮帕成了家里的“小妈妈”。她的父亲不在家，把照顾弟弟妹妹的责任都留给了她。她就像个小战士妈妈，守护着她的“孩子们”。

‘When you told the ambulance man it was you who’d burnt your brother, I think you were trying to protect your mother. And perhaps trying to keep her as a “good” mummy in your mind. I think you do the same thing with Claudine. You try to protect her and you try to keep her as a “good” wife in your mind.’

“当你告诉救护人员是你烧伤了你的弟弟时，我认为你是在保护你的母亲。或许你也想在心里把她当作一个‘好’妈妈。我认为你对待克劳迪娜也是一样。你想保护她，想在心里把她当作一个‘好’妻子。”

‘She is good, Susanna. She’s just …’ She searched for a word. ‘Damaged.’

“她很好，苏珊娜。她只是……”她斟酌着措辞。“受过伤害。”

Was Pippa repeating her childhood with Claudine, falling into a pattern of behaviour that felt familiar and known? I’ve never found the idea of repetition compulsion, in which a person keeps repeating something because it’s familiar, a satisfactory theory. Surely natural selection would have evolved that habit out of us? But at the heart of all my work is a recognition that people do seem to choose partners whose experience in childhood almost always in some way echoes their own. Why would this be so? Why would Pippa choose Claudine – someone, though lovable in many ways, who required just the kind of devotion and attention that Pippa’s mother demanded? Surely Pippa should have run a mile? Surely Pippa should have found someone who’d look after her ?

皮帕是否在和克劳迪娜重蹈覆辙，重复着她童年的经历，陷入一种似曾相识的行为模式？我一直觉得“重复强迫症”——即一个人因为熟悉而不断重复某种行为——的理论难以令人信服。自然选择难道不应该早已让我们摆脱这种习惯吗？但我所有研究的核心都在于认识到，人们似乎总是倾向于选择那些童年经历与自己几乎总是有某种共鸣的伴侣。为什么会这样？为什么皮帕会选择克劳迪娜——一个虽然在很多方面都很可爱，但却需要皮帕母亲所要求的那种奉献和关注的人？皮帕难道不应该赶紧逃离吗？难道她不应该找到一个能够照顾她的人吗？

Soon after this session, I managed to find a good colleague to work with Claudine. We’d been talking about how important it was that Claudine had some therapy on her own and now it seemed she was ready. She began to see her own therapist twice a week and it didn’t take long for that to shift things.

这次会谈后不久，我就找到了一位合适的同事来协助克劳迪娜。我们之前一直在讨论克劳迪娜接受个人心理治疗的重要性，现在看来她已经准备好了。她开始每周两次接受心理治疗，没过多久，情况就有所好转。

‘I’m finding these sessions aren’t really helping me anymore. I think we should stop coming,’ Claudine suddenly announced one autumn day as our session began.

“我觉得这些辅导课对我帮助不大。我想我们应该停止来了。”一天秋日，辅导课刚开始，克劳迪娜突然宣布道。

Pippa, still shrugging off her blue denim jacket, looked shocked. ‘You didn’t say that to me. You can’t just decide that on your own! I don’t want to stop coming, Claud.’

皮帕一边脱着蓝色牛仔外套，一边一脸震惊。“你没跟我说过这话。你不能自己做决定！我不想不来了，克劳德。”

‘Well, you continue with Susanna. I don’t have to. I’ve got my own therapist now.’

“那你就继续和苏珊娜治疗吧。我不用了。我现在有自己的心理医生了。”

‘Perhaps three sessions a week feels a little intense, Claudine?’ I asked gently, pushing down a flash of anger at her precipitous and high-handed decision.

“克劳迪娜，也许每周三次的训练强度有点大？”我轻声问道，努力压下心中对她草率而专横的决定的怒火。

Before Claudine could reply, Pippa, picking up my thread, jumped back in. ‘If it’s too much, sweetie, we can stop. I’m sorry. I don’t want you to feel under pressure from me. You’ve got a lot on your plate dealing with everything.’

克劳迪娜还没来得及回答，皮帕就接过话茬，插话道：“亲爱的，如果太难受了，我们可以停下来。对不起，我不想给你压力。你已经够忙的了，要处理这么多事。”

‘Why don’t you want to go on your own?’ Claudine asked.

“你为什么不想独自前往？”克劳迪娜问道。

Pippa cocked her head and looked at me and then back at Claudine, as though considering the idea. ‘I don’t think so. What for? Perhaps we should just stop. Or stop for a bit?’ And she looked at me again, checking my reaction.

皮帕歪着头看了看我，又看了看克劳迪娜，似乎在考虑这个提议。“我觉得不行。为什么要这么做？或许我们应该就此打住。或者至少停下来一会儿？”说着，她又看了看我，想看看我的反应。

‘Are you both saying that there isn’t a problem in the relationship anymore? Or that the problems have really been just Claudine’s problems?’

“你们俩的意思是说，这段关系已经没有问题了吗？还是说，之前的问题其实都只是克劳迪娜的问题？”

Pippa nodded but without any great enthusiasm.

皮帕点了点头，但并没有表现出多少热情。

‘We’ve discussed before, the way that Pippa has been a mother substitute to you, Claudine, but now you’ve started with your own therapist, perhaps it feels as though you’re getting enough of being mummied? And coming to see me is just one mummy too many?’

“我们之前讨论过，皮帕就像你的母亲一样照顾你，克劳迪娜，但现在你开始接受自己的心理治疗，也许你觉得被妈妈照顾得够多了？来见我，对你来说是不是多了一个妈妈？”

Claudine laughed and nodded her head. ‘Maybe, maybe. I just don’t always want to be the one who’s the centre of attention, you know.’

克劳迪娜笑着点了点头。“也许吧，也许吧。我只是不想总是成为众人瞩目的焦点，你知道的。”

After that, we explored what it meant to be the centre of attention both at home and in the therapy with me. Claudine acknowledged she liked Pippa taking care of her but she didn’t like the way Pippa didn’t take her seriously. She complained that Pippa bossed her around and then they skirmished around who made decisions about Milly. I listened carefully and remembered the scene that I’d witnessed outside my window; it seemed that Claudine had begun to recognise that there was a cost as well as a benefit to being a child in this relationship.

之后，我们探讨了在家里和我的治疗中，成为关注中心意味着什么。克劳迪娜承认她喜欢皮帕照顾她，但她不喜欢皮帕不把她当回事。她抱怨皮帕对她颐指气使，然后她们还就谁来做关于米莉的决定发生了争执。我仔细地听着，想起了我从窗外看到的一幕；克劳迪娜似乎开始意识到，在这段关系中，作为孩子既有好处也有坏处。

Eventually, I said that although it might seem as if sorting out Claudine would sort out their problems, I thought there was something important in the dynamic between them they needed to address.

最后，我说，虽然解决克劳迪娜的问题似乎就能解决他们的问题，但我认为他们之间还有一些重要的关系需要解决。

‘My therapist thinks Pippa’s got a lot of problems. Not just me. It feels like it’s always just me who’s got to do the changing. What about you, Pippa?’ Claudine said, glaring at me.

“我的心理咨询师觉得皮帕有很多问题。不只是我。感觉好像总是只有我一个人要改变。皮帕，你呢？”克劳迪娜怒视着我说道。

‘You think I’ve been part of making you the problem? Letting Pippa off the hook?’ I asked.

“你觉得我让你成为问题的一部分吗？放过皮帕？”我问道。

‘Well, you have. Sort of, yeah. I know you’re saying now about it being both of us but you haven’t been, not usually,’ Claudine said bluntly.

“嗯，你的确有过。某种程度上来说，是的。我知道你现在说是我们俩一起，但你以前并没有，通常情况下没有，”克劳迪娜直截了当地说。

I had to admit to myself there was probably some truth in this. I didn’t really like her – or rather, I didn’t approve of her. I knew this wasn’t right, that I wasn’t being even-handed or fair, but it was a struggle. She seemed so arrogant and selfish and Pippa, though avoidant in some ways, was so much easier to like.

我不得不承认，这话或许有些道理。我的确不喜欢她——或者更确切地说，我不认同她。我知道这样不对，我知道我不够公正，但我很难释怀。她看起来那么傲慢自私，而皮帕虽然有些疏离，却更容易让人喜欢。

We didn’t come to any conclusions that session and they left me with the understanding that they’d be back the following week to discuss it further. I felt irritated. That flash of anger at Claudine now felt directed at them both. It felt like they were washing their hands of the therapy and me, and that things would continue as before without any desire for any real change. I was struck how quickly Pippa had reverted to denying her own needs and jumped to protecting Claudine, even when she behaved like a spoilt and selfish child.

那次咨询我们没能达成任何结论，他们离开时告诉我下周会再来讨论。我感到很恼火。之前对克劳迪娜的那股怒气，现在感觉也指向了他们俩。感觉他们好像要放弃治疗，也放弃我，一切都会照旧，他们根本没有任何改变的意愿。我惊讶地发现，皮帕竟然这么快就又开始否认自己的需求，一心只想保护克劳迪娜，即便克劳迪娜的行为像个被宠坏的自私孩子。

Two days later, I got an email from Pippa:

两天后，我收到了皮帕的电子邮件：

Dear Susanna,

I hope you’re well. I’m just dropping you a line to say that we’ve decided to pause the therapy. I think you were spot on when you said it was feeling too much for Claud and so, for now, I think we should stop. Thank you so much for all the help you’ve given us at such a difficult time. We really appreciate it.

Pippa

亲爱的苏珊娜，希望你一切都好。我写这封信是想告诉你，我们决定暂停治疗。你说得对，这对克劳德来说负担太重了，所以，我觉得我们现在应该停止治疗。非常感谢你在这段艰难时期给予我们的帮助。我们真的非常感激。皮帕

Why is it that some couples will stick with therapy through hell and high water whilst others turn away? I could see that I’d probably focused too much on Claudine and her problems and unconsciously nominated her as the ‘ill’ patient with Pippa as her victim. It was understandable that she was fed up with feeling she was always in the doghouse but why did Pippa decide to back away too? Was it the thought of change? Was the therapy beginning to unravel the collusion between them and was it this that was being resisted? Whilst the burden of caring for Claudine was considerable, Pippa, in her grown-up role, got to feel in control and strong. Though her needs were put on hold, she could distance herself from her own childlike fragility by being a loving, if sometimes controlling and bossy, mummy.

为什么有些夫妻能坚持不懈地接受治疗，即使遭遇重重困难，而有些夫妻却选择放弃？我意识到自己可能过于关注克劳迪娜和她的问题，不知不觉地把她视为“病人”，而把皮帕视为受害者。克劳迪娜厌倦了总是被冷落的感觉，这可以理解，但皮帕为什么也决定退出呢？是因为害怕改变吗？治疗是否开始瓦解她们之间的默契，而这正是她们抗拒的？虽然照顾克劳迪娜的负担很重，但皮帕扮演着成年人的角色，让她感到自己能够掌控一切，变得强大。尽管她的需求被搁置，但她可以通过做一个充满爱心（尽管有时控制欲强、专横跋扈）的妈妈，来摆脱自己孩子般的脆弱。

As I contemplated this, I thought about the walk I’d taken the previous weekend with my nervous, rather urban friend in the countryside outside of London. We were chatting away when we reached a field full of cows. My friend demurred – she hated cows, was terrified of them, and proceeded to tell me that today’s cows were, because of breeding, far more dangerous than cows of the past. These weren’t docile, doe-eyed Daisies with a charming bell around their throats; these, she said, were anxious and unpredictable beasts and we must find another way through. But there was no other way through, no detour or alternative route. We either went through the field or we turned back and gave up on the rather nice pub lunch awaiting us at the end of the walk. Whilst I am no hero, not brave or athletic, her anxious pleading made me feel strong and determined. Gathering myself, I reassured her in an authoritative voice and we made our way through the field at a brisk pace and out the other side. I felt triumphant and fearless; all my own anxiety had evaporated, so firmly had I projected it into her.

我思索着这件事，想起了上周末和那位神经兮兮、略显都市化的朋友在伦敦郊外乡村散步的情景。我们一路聊着天，走到一片满是牛的田野。我的朋友犹豫了——她讨厌牛，害怕得要命，然后告诉我，现在的牛因为品种的原因，比以前的牛危险得多。她说，这些牛可不是以前那种温顺、眼神楚楚可怜、脖子上挂着铃铛的雏菊；它们是焦虑不安、难以捉摸的野兽，我们必须另寻他路。可是根本没有别的路，没有绕路，也没有其他路线。我们要么穿过这片田野，要么就只能原路返回，放弃在散步终点等着我们的那顿不错的酒吧午餐。虽然我不是什么英雄，既不勇敢也不擅长运动，但她焦急的恳求却让我感到自己变得坚强而果断。我定了定神，用不容置疑的语气安抚她，然后我们快步穿过田野，来到了另一边。我感到无比的胜利和无所畏惧；我所有的焦虑都烟消云散了，因为我把所有的焦虑都转移到了她身上。

Pippa’s own fragility was lodged in Claudine and by caring for her lover as if she was a small, helpless baby, she vicariously cared for herself too. But though we’d begun to understand the underlying causes of Claudine’s addictions and I had begun to explore Pippa’s part in the deception, I still wondered if Claudine’s lies were forgivable. And if they were, what would make true forgiveness possible? Claudine had allowed Pippa to fuss over her, to make doctor’s appointments, ignoring the pain and anxiety she was creating. Claudine had watched Pippa work herself to the bone to keep a roof over their heads, struggling to care for them all, whilst, all the time, she was secretly abusing drugs. And, in all the time she attended therapy, she never really said sorry.

皮帕自身的脆弱寄托在克劳迪娜身上，她像照顾一个弱小无助的婴儿一样照顾着自己的爱人，也间接地照顾着自己。尽管我们开始理解克劳迪娜成瘾的根本原因，我也开始探究皮帕在欺骗中所扮演的角色，但我仍然怀疑克劳迪娜的谎言是否可以被原谅。如果可以，又该如何才能真正原谅她呢？克劳迪娜任由皮帕对她百般呵护，替她预约医生，却对皮帕给她带来的痛苦和焦虑视而不见。克劳迪娜眼睁睁地看着皮帕为了维持生计拼命工作，努力照顾所有人，而她自己却一直在暗中滥用药物。而且，在她接受治疗的那些日子里，她从未真正道过歉。

Psychotherapists are trained not to take moral stands; we need to remain curious and open even in the presence of grand immorality. That isn’t to say that psychoanalytic therapy is amoral; indeed, psychoanalysis aims to help patients confront their destructiveness head on and, in time, take responsibility for the damage done. I’d failed to help Claudine face the hurt she’d caused and failed to help Pippa stand her ground in expecting some repentance. I had the sense that Pippa would do her best to keep Claudine, whatever the consequences, but, as a result, they wouldn’t be any closer or trusting.

心理治疗师接受的训练是不去评判道德立场；即使面对极其不道德的行为，我们也需要保持好奇心和开放的心态。但这并不意味着精神分析疗法本身是无道德的；事实上，精神分析旨在帮助患者直面自身的破坏性行为，并最终承担起造成伤害的责任。我没能帮助克劳迪娜面对她所造成的伤害，也没能帮助皮帕坚持她期待克劳迪娜悔改的立场。我感觉皮帕会竭尽全力留住克劳迪娜，不计后果，但结果却是她们之间的关系更加疏远，彼此之间也更加不信任。

How do couples recover well from great betrayals? Is it possible and is it wise? First and foremost, there needs to be the recognition that there has been a betrayal and that there is an accompanying sense of remorse about it. Say sorry. Then say sorry again and mean it. I have seen couples where the betrayal has been revealed and lies exposed but the betrayer continues to deny it. They cannot face and own their guilt, so they leave their partner not only with the trauma of having been let down but the further pain of that trauma not being recognised. In this situation, the hurt cannot heal and the couple cannot regain any sense of trust. Restoring trust takes time; a partner needs months and years of good experiences with their lover to gradually rub down the sharp edge of doubt and uncertainty. They need to believe that the betrayal won’t be repeated, that it is in the past or was a one-time thing. The restoration of a good sex life also helps because, of course, a less than satisfactory sex life is a very common reason for an affair in the first place. Finally, I’ve noticed that the couples who do best after a betrayal are those who, together, develop a narrative around the ‘why’. These couples take shared ownership of the root causes of the betrayal, acknowledging that the relationship was in a shaky state even before the duplicity and come to an understanding that the affair was a symptom of those problems.

伴侣如何才能从严重的背叛中恢复过来？这有可能吗？这样做明智吗？首先，也是最重要的，双方都需要意识到背叛的存在，并为此感到懊悔。道歉。然后再次道歉，并且要真心实意。我见过一些伴侣，背叛已被揭露，谎言也被揭穿，但背叛者仍然矢口否认。他们无法面对和承担自己的罪责，因此不仅让伴侣承受被辜负的创伤，还让他们承受这种创伤未被理解的痛苦。在这种情况下，伤痛无法愈合，伴侣也无法重建信任。重建信任需要时间；伴侣需要与爱人经历数月甚至数年的美好时光，才能逐渐抚平心中的疑虑和不安。他们需要相信背叛不会重演，它已经成为过去，或者只是一次偶然事件。恢复良好的性生活也大有裨益，因为性生活不和谐本身就是婚外情的一个常见原因。最后，我注意到，在经历背叛后关系恢复最好的伴侣，往往是那些共同探讨“为什么”的伴侣。这些伴侣共同承担背叛的根源责任，承认即使在背叛发生之前，这段关系就已经摇摇欲坠，并最终理解婚外情只是这些问题的征兆。

Part Three

第三部分

FLESH AND BLOOD

骨肉

Come away, O human child!
来吧，人类的孩子！
To the waters and the wild
去往水边和荒野，
With a faery, hand in hand,
与仙女手牵手，
For the world’s more full of weeping than you can understand.

—W. B. Yeats, ‘The Stolen Child’, The Wanderings of Oisin and Other Poems


因为这世间充满了你无法理解的悲伤。——叶芝，《被偷走的孩子》，选自《奥辛的漫游及其他诗歌》

Flesh and blood is gory – just like family life. Family life begins after the fairy tale ends. Though many couples will live happily, they will not live happily always . There is no ‘ever after’ about it.

血肉之躯终究是残酷的——就像家庭生活一样。家庭生活始于童话故事结束后。虽然许多夫妻会过上幸福的生活，但他们不会永远幸福。生活没有“从此幸福快乐地生活在一起”的结局。

The arrival or non-arrival of children is most usually the problem. They are wanted, needed, but they are so dependent and for so, so long. Having children is the most challenging part of being a couple because being a good-enough parent means sacrifice; it means budging up and letting someone else in. It means meeting parts of yourself long buried in infancy and childhood – how else would we know what our children feel? What our children need?

孩子的到来或不来通常是最大的问题。我们渴望孩子，需要他们，但他们依赖性太强，而且这种依赖性持续很久很久。为人父母是夫妻关系中最具挑战性的部分，因为做一个合格的父母意味着牺牲；意味着要做出让步，接纳另一个人。这意味着要面对自己内心深处那些被埋藏在婴儿期和童年期的部分——否则我们又怎能了解孩子的感受？了解孩子的需求呢？

And families? It seems we need them to flourish. They ground us, give us a place to belong and form our identities. Family links our past with our present and family holds the key to our future. Family is the place where we can try and rework that past and repair our pain, and all the pain and struggle of our ancestors, in an endless sequence of generations.

那么，家庭呢？我们似乎都需要家庭才能茁壮成长。家庭让我们脚踏实地，给予我们归属感，塑造我们的身份认同。家庭连接着我们的过去与现在，也掌握着我们未来的钥匙。家庭是我们尝试重塑过去、疗愈自身伤痛，以及世世代代祖先所承受的痛苦与磨难的地方。

# ↩

Bina and Shapiro Conjure up a Baby

比娜和夏皮罗变出了一个婴儿

The email from Bina asking for couple therapy was particularly polite. In every correspondence, she managed to convey that she was a thoughtful, respectful person. She was very understanding when I said I was currently full and seemed perfectly happy to wait for an appointment. She signed off her emails with Warmest Wishes, Bina . The heart seemed overkill but, nonetheless, I was looking forward to meeting Bina and her husband Shapiro.

比娜发来的咨询夫妻治疗的邮件格外礼貌。每次邮件往来，她都展现出体贴周到、尊重他人的品质。当我表示自己目前时间已满时，她非常理解，并表示很乐意等待预约。邮件末尾她会写上“致以最诚挚的问候，比娜 ”。虽然附上爱心图案略显夸张，但我仍然很期待见到比娜和她的丈夫夏皮罗。

They arrived promptly, an attractive couple, well dressed and well spoken, who smiled warmly when I gestured for them to come into my office. When I asked them to tell me a little about why they’d come, they smiled again and turned to each other to agree who’d start.

他们准时到达，是一对相貌堂堂、衣着得体、谈吐优雅的夫妇。我示意他们进办公室时，他们面带微笑。我请他们简单介绍一下此行的目的，他们再次微笑，然后互相交换了一下意见，商量由谁先开口。

‘Good question,’ Shapiro said approvingly, pointing his finger at me. ‘Let me put it in a nutshell. I think there are three points we need to address.’ He looked at Bina, who nodded agreement. ‘One,’ he raised his thumb. ‘How and when are we going to start a family? Two,’ he raised his forefinger, ‘What do we mean by quality time and how do we get to a mutual agreement around that? And three, how do we negotiate the financial and homemaking balance between us once we’ve started our family? In other words, Susanna, we need you to help us get to a “Version 2.0” of this relationship and we need some quick wins. We don’t want to boil the ocean over this, we’ve done some work already on getting the questions right. We just need you to set us off in the right direction. Right, hon?’ Shapiro stopped and checked in with Bina, who, again, smiled and nodded. Then Shapiro, neatly dressed in his grey suit and matching greying hair, sat back and waited for me to come up with a plan.

“问得好，”沙皮罗赞许地说，同时用手指着我。“我简单概括一下。我认为我们需要解决三个问题。”他看向比娜，比娜点头表示同意。“第一，”他竖起大拇指，“我们什么时候以及如何组建家庭？第二，”他竖起食指，“我们所说的‘高质量陪伴时间’是什么意思？我们如何才能就此达成共识？第三，组建家庭后，我们如何在经济和家务方面进行平衡？换句话说，苏珊娜，我们需要你帮助我们把这段关系升级到‘2.0版’，而且我们需要一些快速见效的方法。我们不想为此大动干戈，我们已经在确定问题上做了一些工作。我们只需要你指引我们走向正确的方向。好吗，亲爱的？”沙皮罗停顿了一下，向比娜确认，比娜再次微笑点头。然后，身着整齐灰色西装、头发也逐渐灰白的沙皮罗向后靠去，等着我想出一个计划。

It’s unusual for me to be lost for words but I have to admit Shapiro had succeeded in striking me dumb. My heart sank and I had little idea what he was talking about. All I could feel was the powerful wish in them for a quick solution, something I knew I wasn’t able to give.

我很少会语塞，但不得不承认，沙皮罗的话让我哑口无言。我心头一沉，完全不明白他在说什么。我只感受到他们迫切希望找到一个快速的解决方案，而我知道自己无能为力。

‘You seem to be saying that you’re both on the same page about what you want from coming to see me and I think I hear that some of this is about a life transition you’re wanting to make? You want to start a family?’

“你们似乎在说，你们对于来找我的目的达成了一致，我感觉你们好像想做出一些人生转变？你们想组建家庭？”

They both nodded.

他们俩都点了点头。

‘Could you tell me a little more about what’s been going on between you recently? Have you been at odds? Are there things you don’t agree on? Might this be the reason you decided to come and see me?’

“你能跟我说说你们最近发生了什么事吗？你们之间是不是闹矛盾了？是不是有什么事情你们意见不合？这会不会是你决定来见我的原因？”

Again, they looked at each other to see who might take my question and I had the sudden peculiar feeling that I was in a conference room and they, the speakers, were taking questions from me, the audience.

他们再次互相看了看，看看谁会回答我的问题，我突然有种奇怪的感觉，仿佛我身处一个会议室，而他们，也就是演讲者，正在接受我，也就是听众的提问。

‘I think we’ve sought you out because of your reputation. We went into this very carefully and your name kept coming up. We tried one other therapist but she was full, so you were second on our list.’ Shapiro beamed at me, as though congratulating me on my success. ‘We don’t want to mess around here. We want to get things sorted and some agreements on the table … if that’s OK with you?’

“我想我们找你是因为你的名声。我们做了很多调查，你的名字总是被提及。我们试过另一位治疗师，但她预约满了，所以你是我们的第二选择。” 沙皮罗对我露出灿烂的笑容，仿佛在祝贺我成功。“我们不想在这件事上浪费时间。我们想把事情理顺，达成一些协议……你觉得可以吗？”

I felt floored. This felt like a difficult mix of flattery and control that I wasn’t sure how to address. I said nothing and I could see that Bina was beginning to find that uncomfortable, as she looked nervously from me to Shapiro, as though expecting trouble.

我当时感觉不知所措。这种感觉既像是奉承又像是控制，我不知该如何应对。我什么也没说，但我看得出比娜开始觉得不自在，她紧张地看看我，又看看夏皮罗，好像在担心出什么事。

‘Is it hard to “negotiate” things in your relationship, Bina?’ I addressed her directly.

“比娜，你们的关系中是不是很难‘协商’？”我直接问她。

And then Bina began to speak, haltingly at first, but gradually she explained that Shapiro wanted them to have a baby but she wasn’t sure that this was the right time for her. She’d just moved jobs and been promoted and was now poised to make a big acquisition; she needed this deal to go through before she took time off. She didn’t think she’d be able to get pregnant before next March.

然后比娜开始说话，起初有些结巴，但渐渐地，她解释说，夏皮罗想要个孩子，但她不确定现在是不是合适的时机。她刚刚换了工作，升职了，现在正准备进行一项大型收购；她需要先完成这笔交易才能休假。她觉得明年三月之前自己不太可能怀孕。

‘I’ve told you, hon, next March won’t work. We’ll be opening the New York office then and I won’t be available. If we get going now, it works much better for me and hopefully you’ll be able to get the deal sewn up by Christmas. Which would mean the baby would arrive in May and I’ll have the New York office up and running and you’ll be able to take time off during the summer.’

“亲爱的，我跟你说过，明年三月不行。那时候我们要在纽约开办事处，我没空。如果我们现在就开始，对我来说更方便，希望你能在圣诞节前把这笔交易敲定。这样一来，宝宝五月份就能出生，纽约办事处也能顺利运营，你夏天也能好好休息了。”

I listened in astonishment. Both Bina and Shapiro seemed under the illusion that a baby could be timed exactly, like boiling an egg.

我听得十分惊讶。比娜和夏皮罗似乎都误以为生孩子可以像煮鸡蛋一样精确地把握时机。

‘It seems that thinking about having a baby is filled with complications and challenges for you both. And I’m wondering if this scheduling you’re doing is a way to manage the uncertainty of trying for a baby?’

“看来你们俩在考虑要孩子这件事上遇到了很多困难和挑战。我想知道你们现在这样安排是不是为了应对备孕过程中的不确定性？”

They both looked at me perplexed. ‘We haven’t actually started trying yet,’ Bina responded. ‘But I got pregnant last year by accident so we know we can.’

她们俩一脸困惑地看着我。“我们还没开始备孕呢，”比娜回答说，“不过我去年意外怀孕了，所以我们知道我们能怀上。”

‘Yep. No problems to report there!’ Shapiro said brightly.

“没错，那边一切正常！”夏皮罗兴高采烈地说。

‘You terminated the pregnancy?’ I asked gently.

“你终止了妊娠？”我轻声问道。

‘Yes. Tricky. But the right decision at the right time,’ Shapiro said, and didn’t elaborate further.

“是的，很棘手。但这是适时做出的正确决定。”沙皮罗说道，并未进一步解释。

Neither of them seemed to have consciously considered that getting pregnant might not be straightforward, so over the rest of the session, I tried to understand their worries about becoming parents, giving them some space to explore their feelings about this and the abortion they’d had the previous year. It was like pushing sand uphill and I sensed that Shapiro found my questions not only demanding but annoying. He wanted me to get on board with ‘negotiating an agreement’ between them and didn’t at all see the point of exploring their pasts or their feelings about it. By the end of the session, all my attempts to get the couple to think and feel had been rebuffed. I didn’t expect to see them again. I felt I’d gone from second best therapist to the bottom of the pile – from magic to tragic in their estimation.

他们俩似乎都没意识到怀孕可能并非易事，所以在接下来的咨询中，我试图理解他们对为人父母的担忧，并给他们一些空间去探讨他们对此的感受，以及他们去年堕胎的经历。但这就像推沙子上山一样徒劳无功，我感觉沙皮罗不仅觉得我的问题咄咄逼人，而且还觉得很烦。他想让我参与到他们之间的“协商”中，完全不明白探究他们的过去或他们对此的感受有何意义。咨询结束时，我所有试图引导这对夫妇思考和感受的努力都遭到了拒绝。我并不指望还能再见到他们。我觉得自己从二流的咨询师跌落到了谷底——在他们眼里，我从“神奇”变成了“悲剧”。

But the next morning I received the following email:

但第二天早上我收到了以下邮件：

Hi Susanna,

We just loved the session yesterday and we would like to meet you for five sessions. Our only problem is that next week I’m in the US and the following week Shapiro is in Paris. So, we’d like to start in three weeks and can we meet at 5.30pm instead of 5pm? Finally, if we book for five sessions do you give a discount?

Great working with you.

Bina

嗨，苏珊娜，我们非常喜欢昨天的课程，想和你一起上五节课。我们唯一的问题是，下周我要去美国，再下周夏皮罗要在巴黎。所以，我们想三周后开始，可以把时间改成下午5:30而不是5点吗？另外，如果我们预订五节课，你会给折扣吗？很高兴能和你合作。比娜

I wrote back firmly but politely explaining that I couldn’t see them at 5.30pm, that I didn’t work to a specific number of sessions or give discounts but that I could hold the session for them for two weeks. I was beginning to get a picture of this couple that made me curious. They clearly really liked to feel that they had everything nailed down and controlled. Would they be able to settle into therapy with me? I doubted it. But could I help them to become a little less action-orientated and more thoughtful, maybe?

我语气坚定但礼貌地回复说，下午5点半我无法接待他们，我的咨询次数没有固定限制，也不提供折扣，但我可以为他们保留两周的咨询时间。我开始对这对夫妇有了些许了解，这让我很好奇。他们显然很喜欢一切尽在掌握的感觉。他们能适应我的咨询吗？我对此表示怀疑。但我或许可以帮助他们减少一些行动导向，变得更加深思熟虑呢？

Three weeks later, they were back. Once again, there were broad smiles as they entered and Shapiro offered his hand to shake in greeting. I took it briefly and waited for them to settle themselves on the couch. Bina looked very groomed; her lustrous jet-black hair shone as though she’d just walked out of the hairdresser’s and her deep brown skin looked as though it had been polished. She was as slim as a pin and her hands were expertly manicured and varnished, two diamond bands decorating her ring finger.

三周后，他们又来了。他们进门时，脸上依旧洋溢着灿烂的笑容，沙皮罗伸出手来打招呼。我简单地握了握，等着他们在沙发上坐下。比娜看起来打扮得非常精致；她乌黑亮丽的头发闪闪发亮，仿佛刚从理发店出来一样，深棕色的皮肤也像抛光过一样光滑。她身材纤细，双手修剪得一丝不苟，涂着指甲油，无名指上戴着两枚钻石戒指。

They looked at me expectantly as though I was about to bring out a bag of magic tricks to conjure with but as we went on, our conversation seemed to falter – every avenue I tried to explore was shut down and every thought I offered was wrong. The sweet politeness they’d shown in the first session seemed to have evaporated. Eventually, I said, ‘Maybe it feels uncomfortable for you to be needing my help … any help, actually. My guess is that you’re used to managing things yourselves, getting on with it, sorting things and moving on. But perhaps this – your relationship – is something different? Something that needs a different kind of approach. One that involves talking about things you usually avoid and feeling things you don’t usually allow yourselves to feel?’

他们满怀期待地看着我，仿佛我要拿出百宝箱变出什么神奇的魔术来。但随着谈话的进行，我们的对话似乎陷入了僵局——我尝试探讨的每一个方向都被否决，我提出的每一个想法都被认为是错误的。他们在第一次咨询时表现出的那种亲切礼貌似乎消失殆尽。最终，我说：“也许你们觉得需要我的帮助……任何帮助——都让你们感到不自在。我猜你们习惯了自己处理事情，继续前进，解决问题，然后继续生活。但也许你们的关系有所不同？需要一种不同的方法。一种需要谈论你们通常会回避的事情，以及感受你们通常不允许自己感受的情绪的方法？”

Almost before I finished speaking, Shapiro interrupted. ‘I think you’re right, Susanna. Maybe we do need to do a deep dive here.’

我话还没说完，沙皮罗就打断了我。“我想你是对的，苏珊娜。或许我们真的需要深入研究一下这个问题。”

I tried to ignore his business jargon – maybe he was acknowledging in his own way that they were blocking any exploration. Then I noticed that tears were silently running down Bina’s face.

我努力不去理会他那些商业术语——或许他是在用自己的方式承认，这些术语阻碍了任何探索。然后我注意到，比娜的脸上正悄无声息地流着泪。

Shapiro leaned over and reached for the tissue box, which he waved in her direction for her to take. She was oblivious to him, lost in her own thoughts, so he rested the tissues precariously on the couch next to her. He looked awkward and upset. We waited.

沙皮罗俯身去拿纸巾盒，朝她挥了挥，示意她接过。她浑然不觉，沉浸在自己的思绪中，于是他小心翼翼地把纸巾放在她身旁的沙发上。他看起来有些尴尬和沮丧。我们等着。

‘Sorry, sorry,’ Bina said, taking a tissue and blowing her nose. ‘I don’t know why I’m crying. I just think it’s because sometimes …’ she paused and looked intently at Shapiro, ‘… sometimes it just seems hopeless.’

“对不起，对不起，”比娜说着，拿起纸巾擤了擤鼻子。“我不知道我为什么哭。我只是觉得，有时候……”她停顿了一下，专注地看着夏皮罗，“……有时候，一切都显得那么绝望。”

‘Hopeless?’ I asked.

“没希望了吗？”我问。

‘I just don’t see how I’m going to make Shapiro happy. He seems so sure about everything and I don’t think I am. I want a baby … I think. But I’m not sure I’m cut out for doing mother stuff and working. My own mother didn’t work and she was always exhausted. And there was a lot of help in the house. I just can’t see how I’m going to manage it all.’

“我真不知道该怎么才能让沙皮罗满意。他好像对什么都信心满满，但我却没那么自信。我想要个孩子……我想是吧。但我不太确定自己能不能胜任母亲的角色，同时还能工作。我母亲没有工作，但她总是筋疲力尽。而且家里还有很多人帮忙。我真不知道自己该怎么兼顾这一切。”

‘We’ll have help, Bee, of course we’ll have help. We can have two nannies if you want. Help isn’t a problem. I know your career is the most important thing. Don’t sweat about that,’ Shapiro tried to reassure her.

“我们会有人帮忙的，比，当然会有人帮忙的。如果你愿意，我们可以请两个保姆。帮忙不是问题。我知道你的事业最重要，别担心。”夏皮罗试图安慰她。

Bina then started to talk at length about her career and what it meant to her. She was clearly both successful and driven, despite having left school at 17. As she described it, I had the sense that her entire life centred on her work. She talked about the years and years of slog to prove herself but now she knew she was extremely good at her job.

比娜随后开始滔滔不绝地讲述她的职业生涯以及这份工作对她的意义。尽管她17岁就辍学了，但她显然既成功又充满干劲。听她描述，我感觉她的整个生活都围绕着工作。她谈到自己为了证明自己而付出的多年艰辛努力，但现在她知道自己非常擅长这份工作。

I began to ponder if Bina and Shapiro were finding themselves at different stages in their development and whether this could spell danger for their relationship. It seemed that the two of them had had a shared culture, where hard work and the achievements that hard work brought had been paramount. They’d clearly invested a huge amount into their careers and Bina was now wondering whether that investment was being threatened. Shapiro, on the other hand, seemed to treat the baby ‘project’ almost like a kind of work challenge, driving ahead despite Bina’s uncertainties. I thought they were having a conversation that was clearly at cross purposes and their shared vision of their future was beginning to unravel.

我开始思考比娜和夏皮罗是否正处于人生发展的不同阶段，这是否会给他们的关系带来危险。他们似乎拥有共同的价值观，那就是努力工作以及努力工作带来的成就至关重要。他们显然在事业上投入了大量心血，而比娜现在担心这些投入是否会受到威胁。另一方面，夏皮罗似乎把怀孕这个“项目”当作一种工作挑战，尽管比娜心存疑虑，他仍然一意孤行。我觉得他们的对话明显偏离了方向，他们对未来的共同愿景也开始瓦解。

Differences in development are common reasons for couples to seek help and it can be extremely befuddling when your partner changes their feelings, wishes and ideas. If the interests, opinions and needs of one partner suddenly change, it can challenge the status quo. There are myriad things that can create this lopsided development but planning for and having children is frequently the biggest test a couple ever face. Pregnancy, birth, breastfeeding and the realities of parenthood set off physical, psychological and life changes that can put couples at odds with each other as they express their differing needs and expectations.

发展差异是夫妻寻求帮助的常见原因，当伴侣的感受、愿望和想法发生变化时，会让人感到非常困惑。如果一方的兴趣、观点和需求突然改变，就会挑战现状。造成这种发展失衡的原因有很多，但计划生育和生育子女往往是夫妻面临的最大考验。怀孕、分娩、哺乳以及为人父母的种种现实都会引发生理、心理和生活方式的改变，这些改变可能会使夫妻在表达各自不同的需求和期望时产生分歧。

As they left, Shapiro looked stricken and grumpy. I’d made a last comment that questioned whether they might want quite different things and I had the distinct feeling he hadn’t appreciated that at all. I liked Shapiro but, although he thought he was giving Bina everything she might desire, though he believed he was reassuring her that everything would be OK, I felt he wasn’t really listening.

他们离开时，沙皮罗看起来既沮丧又闷闷不乐。我最后提了一句，质疑他们想要的东西是否完全不同，我明显感觉他一点也不领情。我喜欢沙皮罗，虽然他认为自己已经给了比娜她想要的一切，虽然他相信自己已经让她安心，让她相信一切都会好起来，但我感觉他根本没在听。

Shapiro and Bina continued to turn up promptly for their sessions but, despite their diligent attendance, we still seemed to be getting nowhere. At times, I had a good feeling that I’d made a connection with Bina but then if I attempted to get any closer to her, she seemed to find a way to brush me off. It was becoming clearer to me that any kind of intimacy was a challenge and whenever I felt she was becoming more emotionally available, she’d suddenly turn thoroughly sarcastic or brusque.

沙皮罗和比娜每次都准时赴约，但尽管他们如此尽心尽力，我们的关系似乎仍然毫无进展。有时，我感觉自己和比娜建立了某种联系，但如果我试图更进一步，她总能找到办法把我拒之门外。我越来越清楚地意识到，任何形式的亲密关系都是一种挑战，每当我觉得她开始敞开心扉时，她就会突然变得冷嘲热讽或态度生硬。

In the first or second session, I always ask my patients to tell me a little about their childhoods. Often, however, it takes many months, even years, to get a real picture, as patients gradually begin to remember more, trust more and slowly face the links between the past and their current struggles. It was no different with Bina and Shapiro. I asked them to tell me about their early family life and they certainly complied but, strangely, I found myself unable to recall any of the details they’d told me. When I looked back at my notes, they were also vague. Oddly, I’d scribbled down in pencil rather than typing them up and my writing was indistinct and messy. I knew that they’d told me they’d happy childhoods with parents whose marriages had thrived. I knew they both had siblings, though I was unsure how many. I knew they’d both gone to boarding school but I hadn’t written at what age. In summary, despite meeting for six sessions, it felt that I didn’t really know them at all. Was this my fault? Had I not been paying attention? Or perhaps it reflected the lack of connection they made with themselves, each other and me? Their lives were busy but felt completely colourless. The faded pencil scribbles seemed to sum up how indistinct and empty it seemed.

在第一次或第二次咨询中，我总是会请我的病人简单谈谈他们的童年。然而，通常需要几个月甚至几年的时间，才能真正了解他们的经历，因为病人会逐渐回忆起更多，逐渐建立信任，并慢慢面对过去与当下困境之间的联系。比娜和夏皮罗的情况也不例外。我请他们讲述早年的家庭生活，他们也确实照做了，但奇怪的是，我发现自己完全记不起他们告诉我的任何细节。当我翻看笔记时，发现内容也十分模糊。奇怪的是，我当时是用铅笔潦草地记下来的，而不是用电脑打字，所以我的字迹潦草难辨。我知道他们告诉我，他们的童年很幸福，父母婚姻美满。我知道他们都有兄弟姐妹，但我不确定具体有几个。我知道他们都上过寄宿学校，但我没有记下他们上学校时的年龄。总之，尽管我们见了六次面，但我感觉自己对他们仍然一无所知。这是我的错吗？是我疏忽了吗？或许这反映了他们与自己、彼此以及我之间缺乏联系？他们的生活看似忙碌，却毫无色彩。褪色的铅笔涂鸦似乎恰如其分地概括了他们生活的模糊和空虚。

I did have some important knowledge that came from how they treated me and the work I was trying to help them do. I could feel they hated the kind of therapy I was offering. They were uncomfortable with my belief that we needed to keep things open and exploratory rather than having a specific goal or aim. It wasn’t like the meetings they were used to – there was no agenda and no action points – and I could see they found this both frustrating and confusing. What kind of childhood experience, I wondered, had led to this fearful rigidity? It felt as though they’d been schooled to mistrust the world of emotions and discouraged from taking their feelings seriously. As a result, they maintained an emotional distance from me, from each other and, it seemed, even from themselves. As the sessions went on, I knew, though they didn’t tell me directly, that they were increasingly distrustful of my approach. They wanted to be free of me and their need of me.

我确实从他们对待我的方式以及我试图帮助他们完成的工作中获得了一些重要的信息。我能感觉到他们讨厌我提供的这种疗法。他们不认同我认为我们需要保持开放和探索的态度，而不是设定具体的目标或目的。这和他们以往的会面截然不同——没有议程，也没有行动要点——我能看出他们对此感到既沮丧又困惑。我不禁思考，究竟是怎样的童年经历导致了他们这种恐惧和僵化的性格？感觉他们似乎从小就被教育要怀疑情感世界，并且不被鼓励认真对待自己的感受。结果，他们与我、彼此之间，甚至似乎与他们自己都保持着情感上的距离。随着疗程的进行，我知道，尽管他们没有直接告诉我，但他们越来越不信任我的方法。他们想要摆脱我，摆脱对我的依赖。

Session six arrived and I wondered what would happen next? It seemed to me increasingly likely that they’d stick to their original plan to have just six sessions, even though I felt they needed so much more. Because they were usually very prompt, I was concerned when the big hand slid past the hour on my clock and by the time it reached ten past, I felt sure that they weren’t coming back. I sat there, quite disappointed; it’d been hard work to engage them and they’d resisted all my attempts to get them to open up but I felt warm towards them and still thought that there was useful work we could do together. However, I had a strong sense of how uncomfortable the sessions had been for them, so it was unsurprising that they’d dropped out. It was strange that they hadn’t written to tell me, though; they always seemed so polite and businesslike. Was there a confusion? Did they think that they’d had the full course of sessions and that the therapy then just stopped? I thought we were on session six but perhaps they thought last week was session six? I was pondering all this as I began to compose an email, when the buzzer sounded, startling me out of my reverie.

第六次疗程到了，我不禁琢磨接下来会发生什么。我越来越觉得他们很可能会坚持原计划，只做六次疗程，尽管我觉得他们需要的远不止这些。因为他们通常都很准时，所以当时钟上的大指针滑过整点时，我有些担心。到了十点，我确信他们不会再来了。我坐在那里，相当失望；和他们交流很费劲，他们也一直抗拒我让他们敞开心扉的尝试，但我对他们仍然抱有好感，也仍然觉得我们可以一起做一些有益的工作。然而，我能强烈地感觉到这些疗程对他们来说有多么不自在，所以他们中途退出也并不意外。奇怪的是，他们没有写信告诉我；他们总是那么礼貌，那么公事公办。是不是有什么误会？他们是不是以为疗程已经结束了，治疗就此终止了？我以为我们才第六次，但也许他们以为上周才是第六次？我一边思考着这一切，一边开始写电子邮件，这时蜂鸣器响了，把我从沉思中惊醒过来。

Seconds later, Shapiro came through my door. ‘Just me, hope that’s OK?’ he said as he took off his coat. ‘I don’t think Bee’s coming. I waited for her at the end of the road, she’s never late. I’ve tried ringing her … and texting,’ he explained, looking anxiously at his phone.

几秒钟后，沙皮罗推门进来。“就我一个人，可以吗？”他一边脱外套一边说。“我觉得比不会来了。我在路尽头等了她，她从来不迟到。我试着给她打电话……也发短信了，”他解释道，焦急地看着手机。

‘You were expecting her, then?’ I asked.

“那你当时在等她吗？”我问。

‘Mmm. Not sure. She has a big presentation tomorrow; she’s probably stuck at work. And, to be brutally honest, she wasn’t keen to come. She said there was no point coming to the last session. Nothing’s gonna change.’ He shrugged and looked again at his phone and then it beeped as a message came in. ‘She says she’s not coming,’ he said, lifting his head. ‘Perhaps I should go too? Not much point in me being here without her, is there?’ I heard this as an appeal to me, I felt he was indicating he didn’t really want to go and did want to talk.

“嗯……不太确定。她明天有个重要的演讲，可能工作上耽搁了。而且，说实话，她不太想来。她说上次的会议来也没用，什么都不会改变。”他耸了耸肩，又看了看手机，这时手机响了一声，有条信息进来了。“她说她不来了，”他抬起头说，“也许我也应该去？她不来，我待在这里也没什么意义，对吧？”我听出了他是在向我求情，感觉他是在暗示他其实并不想去，只是想和我聊聊。

‘Perhaps there are things you’d like to talk about on your own?’ I asked.

“或许有些事情你想单独谈谈？”我问道。

In response, Shapiro leant back on the couch, making himself more comfortable. ‘I did want to ask you something,’ he said.

沙皮罗听后向后靠在沙发上，让自己更舒服些。“我确实想问你件事，”他说。

I waited patiently, watching the uncertainty flicker across his face. After a little while and following some general comments, he began to talk about his previous relationships. He reminded me that he was nine years older than Bina and that whilst she’d never been in a serious relationship before, he’d previously been married. He was worried that history was repeating itself but in reverse. When I looked puzzled, he explained that his first marriage had ended because she’d wanted children and he didn’t. They’d fought about it for months and then, despite his reluctance, she got pregnant. At first, he’d been angry and upset, but he was just getting used to the idea when, at 13 weeks, she miscarried. After that, everything seemed wrong between them and they decided to go their separate ways. She was married now to an old school friend of his and had lots of children. He joked about her trying for a rugby team and tried to laugh but he looked rueful and regretful as he recounted this tale. We sat in silence for a little while and I felt sad and sorry that I hadn’t helped him talk about this before. This was the first glimpse of something more real and vulnerable. Was it safer to tell me this without Bina’s presence? Was it easier to be more open given this was the last session?

我耐心地等着，看着他脸上闪过一丝不安。过了一会儿，我们闲聊了几句之后，他开始谈起自己之前的感情经历。他提醒我，他比比娜大九岁，比娜之前从未谈过恋爱，而他却结过婚。他担心历史会重演，只不过方向相反。我一脸疑惑，他解释说，他的第一次婚姻破裂是因为她想要孩子，而他不想。他们为此争吵了好几个月，然后，尽管他很不情愿，她还是怀孕了。起初，他很生气也很沮丧，但还没来得及接受这个事实，13周的时候，她就流产了。之后，他们之间的一切都变了，最终决定分道扬镳。现在，她嫁给了他的一位老同学，并且有很多孩子。他开玩笑说她以前想加入橄榄球队，努力让自己笑出来，但讲述这段往事时，他脸上却满是懊悔和遗憾。我们沉默地坐了一会儿，我感到难过和懊悔，之前没能帮他谈谈这件事。这是我第一次看到他内心更真实、更脆弱的一面。没有比娜在场，跟我说这些会不会更安全？考虑到这是最后一次咨询，是不是更容易敞开心扉？

‘It’s striking we haven’t talked about this before, it’s obviously very important. Does Bina know about this?’ I asked.

“令人惊讶的是，我们之前从未谈论过这件事，这显然非常重要。比娜知道这件事吗？”我问道。

‘Yeah, yeah, absolutely. I mean, we discussed how neither of us was keen on children right at the beginning of the relationship. But then, well, we both changed our minds … or, at least, I thought we’d both changed our minds.’ He trailed off, looking depressed. ‘Do you think I should give up? On having kids, I mean. I don’t want us to break up over it. I think I may’ve pushed Bee a bit too hard. Time to put on the brakes. Row back?’ he asked.

“是啊，是啊，当然。我的意思是，我们一开始就讨论过，我们俩都不太想生孩子。但是后来，嗯，我们都改变了主意……或者至少，我以为我们都改变了主意。”他声音渐渐低了下去，看起来很沮丧。“你觉得我应该放弃吗？我是说，放弃要孩子这件事。我不想因为这个分手。我觉得我可能对Bee有点太逼了。是时候踩刹车了。回头看看？”他问道。

‘And what would you do about the bit of you that really wants to have a child, Shapiro?’ I asked.

“那么，沙皮罗，你内心深处真的很想有个孩子，你会怎么做呢？”我问道。

He looked uncertain.

他看上去有些犹豫。

‘What I do notice, Shapiro, and I’ve said this to you before, is that it seems you really don’t like uncertainty. You always push to make a decision, to act, to decide … when perhaps it’s still a time for thinking?’

“我注意到一点，沙皮罗，而且我以前也跟你说过，你似乎真的很不喜欢不确定性。你总是急于做决定、采取行动、做出决定……但也许现在正是思考的时候？”

He nodded in agreement and then began to talk about his work and how his love of a solution had, at times, got him into trouble. He was beginning to realise that, as a boss, it was sometimes best to do nothing.

他点头表示同意，然后开始谈论他的工作，以及他那种追求完美解决问题的执着有时会给他带来麻烦。他开始意识到，作为老板，有时最好的办法就是什么都不做。

‘I’ve got this guy who’s working for me, running this big IT project we’re doing. He comes into my office at least once a day and just rabbits on about what’s broken or what doesn’t work or who’s not doing their job or … well, it’s one problem after another and it’s been really getting to me. I’ve been working my arse off to solve these issues and then, next day, BOOM! It’s all sorted but not in the way I suggested, it’s just got sorted. And I’ve realised this last couple of weeks – he doesn’t need me to do anything, to sort it out for him, he just needs me to … listen.’

“我手下有个家伙，负责我们正在做的这个大型IT项目。他每天至少来我办公室一次，喋喋不休地抱怨哪里坏了，哪里出了问题，谁没做好本职工作……总之，问题一个接一个，真是让我心烦意乱。我拼命地解决这些问题，结果第二天，砰！一切都搞定了，但不是按我预想的方式，就这么莫名其妙地解决了。过去几周我意识到——他不需要我帮他做任何事，不需要我帮他解决问题，他只需要我……听他倾诉。”

‘Perhaps, you’re also talking about what you need from me, from this therapy? Not a solution, but a place to sort out your thoughts and feelings … for me to listen?’

“或许，你也是在说你需要我，需要从这次治疗中得到什么？不是解决方案，而是一个可以梳理你的想法和感受的地方……让我倾听？”

My comment seemed to free him up because for the rest of the session he talked without pause, as though a dam had broken and he could, at last, explore all the worries and concerns about his relationship with Bina. As we came to a close, I suggested that perhaps they needed more time to explore all these things together and that we should go on.

我的话似乎让他如释重负，因为在接下来的谈话中，他滔滔不绝，仿佛堤坝决堤，终于可以畅所欲言地探讨他和比娜关系中的种种担忧和顾虑。谈话临近尾声时，我建议他们或许需要更多时间共同探讨这些问题，并提议我们继续进行下去。

‘I’d very much like to, Susanna, but I’m not sure I’ll be able to persuade Bee.’

“我很想去，苏珊娜，但我不太确定我能不能说服比。”

‘Well, I’ll write to her and suggest that we do, and I’ll expect to see you both next week unless I hear otherwise?’ Shapiro nodded but I could see the doubt in his face.

“嗯，我会写信给她，建议我们这么做，除非另有安排，否则我希望下周能见到你们俩。” 沙皮罗点了点头，但我能看出他脸上的疑虑。

I didn’t feel very confident that they’d be back the following week. I’d come to the conclusion that their reluctance to get settled in a deeper psychotherapy was linked to their anxiety about opening up painful feelings that made them feel vulnerable, but I hoped my session with Shapiro would have reduced his anxiety and raised his curiosity enough to enable him to persuade her to come back.

我不太确定他们下周是否会再来。我得出的结论是，他们不愿接受更深入的心理治疗，是因为他们害怕敞开心扉，袒露那些让他们感到脆弱的痛苦感受。但我希望我和夏皮罗的会面能够减轻他的焦虑，并激发他的好奇心，让他能够说服她再次前来。

I was wrong.

我错了。

I received a brief email response from Bina saying thank you, but they didn’t feel any more sessions would be useful. She didn’t add the heart.

我收到比娜的一封简短邮件回复，她说谢谢，但他们觉得再进行任何疗程都没有意义了。她没有加上爱心。

It was nearly a year later when I received the following email from Shapiro:

将近一年后，我收到了沙皮罗发来的以下邮件：

Hi Susanna,

Hope you’re well? Bee and I wondered if you might have time to see us again for a session? Bee’s pregnant and would like to discuss a couple of issues with you.

Cheers,

Shappy

嗨，苏珊娜，希望你一切都好？我和比想问问你是否有时间再来见我们一次？比怀孕了，想和你讨论一些问题。祝好，莎皮

I actually didn’t have any time but I wanted to see how they were getting on, so I emailed back suggesting an appointment two weeks ahead.

我其实没时间，但我想看看他们的进展如何，所以我回复邮件建议两周后预约。

Hi Susanna,

Thank you so much for returning my email. Any chance we could pop in to see you this week? It’s a bit urgent.

Cheers,

Shappy

嗨，苏珊娜，非常感谢你回复我的邮件。我们这周能不能去拜访你一下？事情有点紧急。谢谢，莎皮

I was curious and a bit concerned. I thought something quite serious must be afoot for him to make a demand like that. I emailed them back, offering to see them on Friday, a day I didn’t usually see patients.

我当时既好奇又有点担心。我觉得他提出这样的要求，肯定是有什么很严重的事情要发生。我给他们回了邮件，提出周五可以见他们，而我通常周五不接诊病人。

I’d pressed the buzzer to let them in some minutes earlier and I was standing outside my consulting room wondering where they’d got to when I heard Bina’s voice on the stairs below.

几分钟前我按了门铃让他们进来，当时我正站在诊室外，纳闷他们去了哪里，这时我听到比娜的声音从楼下的楼梯上传来。

‘God, these stairs,’ she groaned.

“天哪，这楼梯！”她呻吟道。

‘One more floor,’ Shapiro said encouragingly.

“再上一层吧，”沙皮罗鼓励道。

Bina was flushed and sweaty, looking quite different from the polished woman I’d encountered the previous year. She was wearing a block print kaftan and leggings; her low-heeled brown sandals showed her swollen ankles. Her hair, which was stuck to her forehead, was piled into a messy bun with a large purple clip. She looked uncomfortable and unhappy.

比娜满脸通红，汗流浃背，与我去年遇到的那位光鲜亮丽的女士判若两人。她穿着一件印花长袍和紧身裤，脚上穿着棕色低跟凉鞋，露出了肿胀的脚踝。她的头发贴在额头上，随意地挽成一个发髻，用一个紫色的大发夹固定着。她看起来很不自在，也很不开心。

They sat down on the couch, drawing water from their bags and drinking deeply. Bina asked if I could open the window and Shapiro got up to do it. There was something heavy in the air; I knew something was very wrong.

他们坐在沙发上，从包里掏出水来，咕咚咕咚地喝了起来。比娜问我能不能开窗，沙皮罗起身去开窗。空气中弥漫着沉重的气氛；我知道出大事了。

‘Thanks so much for seeing us today. Shall I fill you in?’ Shapiro looked at Bina to confirm that he should start and she nodded dismissively without looking at him.

“非常感谢你们今天来看我们。要我给你们讲讲吗？” 沙皮罗看向比娜，确认他可以开始讲了，比娜没有看他，只是漫不经心地点了点头。

‘OK. First, we need to tell you that the previous sessions with you hit the bullseye. Totally helpful. Both of us felt it really made a difference. Right, hon?’

“好的。首先，我们需要告诉你，之前几次咨询效果非常好，真的很有帮助。我们俩都觉得真的很有效果，对吧，亲爱的？”

Bina didn’t respond.

比娜没有回应。

‘We started trying right after ending the sessions. First month, no luck. Second month, boom! And here we are! Baby’s due in five weeks!’ Shapiro looked at me expectantly but I wasn’t sure what to say. It all seemed so unreal; his enthusiastic bonhomie felt deeply fake.

“疗程结束后我们就开始备孕。第一个月没怀上。第二个月，就成功了！瞧，宝宝还有五周就要出生了！” 沙皮罗满怀期待地看着我，但我不知道该说什么。这一切都太不真实了；他那热情洋溢的亲切劲儿让我觉得很做作。

‘But the pregnancy has been a bit tricky. Bee’s been …’ He searched for the word. ‘A bit down. Maybe depressed?’ He glanced furtively at Bina, who sat motionless and unresponsive.

“不过，这次怀孕有点儿棘手。比伊一直……”他斟酌着措辞。“情绪有点低落。或许是抑郁了？”他偷偷瞥了一眼比娜，她一动不动地坐在那里，毫无反应。

There was a silence. I looked at Bina, hoping she’d say something herself, but her head was down and she seemed, at that moment, quite unreachable.

一片沉默。我看向比娜，希望她能开口说话，但她低着头，那一刻，她似乎遥不可及。

I waited. And waited. I sensed strongly that if I tried to quiz Bina, she’d withdraw further. She needed to feel that it was her choice to open up to me, that it was in her power to speak or not.

我等啊等。我强烈地感觉到，如果我试图追问比娜，她会更加封闭自己。她需要感受到，是否向我敞开心扉是她自己的选择，是她有权选择说或不说。

So I waited some more, drifting off into my own thoughts as we sat together in silence, until Bina’s voice brought me back into the present. It flashed across my mind as she began to speak that my disconnection had mirrored hers.

于是我又等了一会儿，我们静静地坐在一起，我的思绪渐渐飘向远方，直到比娜的声音把我拉回现实。她开口说话的那一刻，我突然意识到，我的恍惚状态和她的如出一辙。

‘I don’t know what you all want me to say,’ Bina said flatly.

“我不知道你们想让我说什么，”比娜冷冷地说。

‘Just explain to Susanna how you’ve been, how you’re feeling,’ Shapiro instructed and I nodded encouragingly too.

“你就跟苏珊娜解释一下你最近怎么样，你的感受如何，”夏皮罗指示道，我也鼓励地点了点头。

‘Fat. That’s how I’m feeling. Disgusting. Fat.’

“胖。我就是这种感觉。真恶心。胖。”

It took a lot of prompting and patience for Bina to share what was going on. She’d never told anyone her feelings about her body and her struggle with eating. She said she felt gross, ugly and out of control and her old routine of restricting her diet and obsessive exercise just wasn’t possible now. She was veering between starving herself and then bingeing, prompted by an aching hunger like she’d never experienced before. She felt as though she couldn’t go on, that she hated herself, wanted to obliterate herself. She didn’t want to live if she had to live like this.

比娜费了好大劲才开口倾诉自己的遭遇。她从未向任何人提起过自己对身材的感受以及与饮食的斗争。她说自己感觉糟糕透顶，丑陋不堪，完全失控，以前那种节食和疯狂运动的习惯现在根本行不通了。她一会儿节食挨饿，一会儿暴饮暴食，这种前所未有的饥饿感让她难以承受。她觉得自己活不下去了，恨透了自己，想要彻底毁灭自己。如果必须这样活下去，她宁愿不要。

I asked Bina, as gently as possible, if she’d thought about hurting herself or even made plans to do so.

我尽可能温和地问比娜，她有没有想过伤害自己，甚至有没有制定过伤害自己的计划。

‘No. I wouldn’t hurt the baby.’

“不，我不会伤害孩子。”

She looked stricken. As though the reality of the baby had just dawned on her. I felt more present with her than I’d ever been and I had a strong impulse to get up and hug her; there was something so lonely and tragic in her voice. I’d never really seen this part of Bina before; it had been so carefully hidden behind her glossy façade. But now it felt she could, at last, acknowledge the mess she was in and the need she had to be cared for and to be understood. And in doing that, she brought me closer to her.

她看上去心力交瘁，仿佛刚刚才意识到自己有了孩子。我感觉自己比以往任何时候都更能感受到她的存在，我强烈地想要起身拥抱她；她声音里透着一股孤独和悲伤。我以前从未真正见过比娜的这一面；它一直被她光鲜亮丽的外表小心翼翼地隐藏着。但现在，她似乎终于能够正视自己身处的困境，以及她渴望被关爱和理解的迫切需要。而正是这一点，拉近了我和她的距离。

‘It’s really good you’re talking to Susanna, hon,’ Shapiro said, turning to me. ‘I’ve been really worried. Bee’s just not been her old self at all. I’m really glad she’s told you what’s been going on. What do you think Bee needs to do?’

“亲爱的，你跟苏珊娜谈这件事真是太好了，”夏皮罗转向我说。“我一直很担心。比伊完全不像以前那样了。我很高兴她把事情都告诉你了。你觉得比伊需要怎么做？”

‘I’m not sure it’s about doing , Shapiro. Maybe first it’s about listening?’

“我不确定关键不在于行动，沙皮罗。也许首先应该在于倾听？”

‘Oh, absolutely. I want to listen. But should Bina see a psychiatrist? What do you think?’

“哦，当然。我很想听听。但是比娜应该去看精神科医生吗？你觉得呢？”

‘Perhaps but let’s have a bit of a think first though.’

“或许吧，不过我们先仔细考虑一下。”

By the end of the session, I think Shapiro felt relieved and I could see why he’d pushed to see me urgently. I suggested I should write to Bina’s GP and that she might need some individual help alongside the couple work. They listened carefully. I consulted my diary and we agreed they’d come back on Wednesday at 8am; the only time I could offer.

会谈结束时，我觉得沙皮罗松了口气，我也明白了他为什么急着要见我。我建议我给比娜的家庭医生写信，说她可能除了夫妻咨询之外，还需要一些个人辅导。他们认真听取了我的建议。我查看了一下日程安排，我们约好周三早上八点再来；这是我唯一能安排的时间。

I spoke to her doctor and emailed a colleague who specialised in eating disorders to see if she had a space for Bina and, by Wednesday, I felt I’d begun to put the care that was going to be needed around this young family.

我跟她的医生谈过，并给一位专门治疗饮食失调症的同事发了邮件，询问她是否能收治比娜。到了周三，我觉得我已经开始为这个年轻的家庭提供所需的关怀了。

On Wednesday, I arrived at Queen Anne Street sweaty and thirsty; the Tube had been pulsing with the previous day’s heat. There was no time to pop to the café to get a coffee and a bottle of water so I opened the windows, put out a new box of tissues, checked the bathroom for loo paper and sat down to wait.

星期三，我抵达皇后街地铁站时，又热又渴；地铁里人头攒动，显然是前一天酷暑的体现。我没时间去咖啡馆买杯咖啡和一瓶水，于是打开窗户，拿出一盒新的纸巾，检查了洗手间有没有卫生纸，然后坐下来等车。

They didn’t come. They didn’t phone or text. I checked my email to no avail. At 8.45am, I dashed out to the café to get my coffee and added a croissant to my order as compensation for being dicked about.

他们没来。他们既没打电话也没发短信。我查看了邮件，但一无所获。早上8点45分，我冲到咖啡馆去买咖啡，还加了一个羊角面包，算是对他们怠慢的补偿。

The day passed uneventfully. I checked my phone between sessions but there was nothing from either Shapiro or Bina. On the way home, I checked again and wrote a brief email to them both, hoping that everything was OK and suggesting they be in touch.

这一天平静地过去了。课间休息时我查看了手机，但沙皮罗和比娜都没有发来任何消息。回家路上，我又查看了一遍，然后给他们俩分别写了一封简短的邮件，希望一切安好，并建议他们保持联系。

The week passed quickly and, like the pencil scribbles, my interest began to fade. I’d done my best; I’d let the GP know and I’d connected Bina up with an outstanding psychotherapist. There was nothing more I could do.

一周很快就过去了，就像铅笔的涂鸦一样，我的兴趣也开始消退。我已经尽力了；我告诉了家庭医生，也帮比娜联系了一位非常优秀的心理治疗师。我再也做不了什么了。

Psychotherapists often have to bear rejection. Many patients, fearful of the depth of their need, slap the offered hand away. Most times, the psychotherapist has to offer it again, and sometimes again and again and again – session after session. Bina’s secret eating disorder was, in some ways, completely unsurprising. She hated her neediness so much that she fought against the reality of her body’s requirement for food. She wanted to control that part of her, the hunger that left her feeling out of control. Through their response to my offers of help, I felt I’d begun to understand their fears, but understanding was useless if they wouldn’t come.

心理治疗师常常要承受拒绝。许多患者因为害怕自己需求的深度，会一把甩开伸出的援手。大多数时候，心理治疗师不得不再次伸出援手，有时甚至要一次又一次地重复——一次又一次的治疗。比娜的秘密饮食障碍，在某种程度上，完全在意料之中。她如此憎恨自己的依赖性，以至于她抗拒身体对食物的需求这一现实。她想要控制自己身体的这一部分——那种让她感到失控的饥饿感。通过他们对我的帮助的回应，我感觉自己开始理解他们的恐惧，但如果他们不愿接受帮助，理解就毫无意义。

It was November, nearly five months later, when I heard from them again. And once more, it was Shapiro who reached out, leaving a friendly message on my phone. There was no apology and little information, just a polite request to be seen. I mulled over whether I wanted to see them again. Was I resentful? Was it a waste of time? But my concern (and curiosity) overrode my reluctance and I offered them a Zoom session the following week. It was all I had.

将近五个月后，到了十一月，我再次收到了他们的消息。这次又是沙皮罗联系我，在我的手机上留了一条友好的留言。没有道歉，也没有提供太多信息，只是礼貌地请求见面。我犹豫着是否要再次见面。我是否心怀怨恨？这是否只是浪费时间？但出于关心（和好奇），我的顾虑最终战胜了犹豫，我提出下周和他们进行一次Zoom视频通话。这是我唯一能做的。

A week later, I sat in my office at home and started the Zoom meeting just a minute before the session was due to begin. I looked at myself on the screen and, noting the tiredness around my eyes, I reached for the cheering lipstick on my desk. Then, ping, there they were. I could see that they were sitting on a large green velvet sofa and behind them was a striking abstract painting. Everything looked comfortable and organised and there seemed to be no sign of a baby in the view I had.

一周后，我坐在家里的办公室里，在会议开始前一分钟启动了Zoom会议。我看着屏幕上的自己，注意到眼角的疲惫，便伸手去拿桌上那支提亮肤色的口红。这时，屏幕上出现了他们。我看到他们正坐在一个宽大的绿色丝绒沙发上，身后是一幅引人注目的抽象画。一切看起来都很舒适整洁，从我的视野来看，似乎并没有婴儿的身影。

I smiled at them and commented that it was some time since we’d met. They smiled back and there was a little flurry between them whilst they decided who would start.

我朝他们笑了笑，说我们好久不见了。他们也回以微笑，然后两人之间短暂地争论了一番，决定谁先开始。

‘Well, we have a son! Darsh. Four months!’ Shapiro said, his voice slightly strained. ‘It’s been … challenging but we’re doing OK, I think.’ And he glanced nervously at Bina who was sitting passively beside him.

“嗯，我们有儿子了！达什。四个月大了！”沙皮罗的声音有些沙哑。“这……挺不容易的，不过我想我们还算可以。”说着，他紧张地瞥了一眼坐在身旁、无精打采的比娜。

She looked drained. Her hair was glossy and down around her face but her skin looked sallow and pinched, and I could see her collarbones jutting out from the neck of her cream jumper.

她看上去很疲惫。她的头发光泽亮丽地披散在脸颊旁，但皮肤却显得蜡黄憔悴，我能看到她米色套头衫领口下凸出的锁骨。

‘Congratulations. How have you both been?’ I asked, directing my gaze at Bina.

“恭喜你们。你们俩最近怎么样？”我问道，目光转向比娜。

‘Not so good,’ she replied. ‘The birth was very tough, long. I had to have a Caesarean in the end. I was in labour for 22 hours and then they were concerned about his heart rate, so they took me in for an emergency Caesar and then I had an infection, so I haven’t really done very well at breastfeeding him. I got mastitis when I got home, so they put me on antibiotics and then I had a reaction to the antibiotics, which meant I had to go back to hospital without Darsh. He’s a lovely boy but he doesn’t sleep so … I’m exhausted to be honest.’ Bina spoke without pause, the words breathlessly tumbling out of her. I thought she looked shell-shocked, as though she couldn’t make sense of all that had happened and was happening to her.

“不太好，”她回答说。“生产过程非常艰难，耗时很长。最后我不得不剖腹产。我经历了22个小时的产程，后来他们担心宝宝的心率，所以给我做了紧急剖腹产。之后我又感染了，所以母乳喂养不太顺利。回家后我又得了乳腺炎，他们给我开了抗生素，结果我对抗生素产生了不良反应，这意味着我不得不独自回医院。他是个很可爱的孩子，但他不怎么睡觉……说实话，我筋疲力尽。”比娜一口气说完，声音急促而清晰。我觉得她看起来像是受到了惊吓，仿佛无法理解所有发生在她身上的事情。

The rest of the session was spent unpacking all this. It seemed the pregnancy, the birth and the first months felt to Bina like a trauma. Her usual ways of managing her feelings and her body had all been thrown into disarray and she was trying hard, and failing, to find a new equilibrium.

剩下的时间都用来梳理这一切。对比娜来说，怀孕、生产和最初的几个月似乎都像是一场创伤。她以往应对情绪和身体状况的方式都被打乱了，她努力想要找到新的平衡，却徒劳无功。

This time there was no prevarication, no wish to limit the number of sessions. They jumped into the therapy with both feet and I was a lifeboat to a pair of drowning children. After a couple of weeks of Zoom sessions, a regular appointment at my office became available and we agreed they should come in person.

这一次，他们没有丝毫犹豫，也没有限制疗程次数的意愿。他们全身心地投入到治疗中，而我就像一艘救生艇，救起了两个溺水的孩子。经过几周的Zoom治疗后，我的办公室终于有了常规的预约名额，我们一致同意他们应该亲自来诊所。

It was a truly horrid winter day. Bitterly cold, icy and dark. I didn’t feel like leaving home myself so I was doubtful that Shapiro and Bina would brave the elements but at 4pm the buzzer buzzed and, moments later, Bina, wearing a baby, arrived in my office.

那真是个糟糕的冬日。寒风刺骨，冰天雪地，天色昏暗。我自己都不想出门，所以也怀疑沙皮罗和比娜会不会冒着严寒出门。但下午四点，门铃响了，片刻之后，比娜抱着一个婴儿来到了我的办公室。

‘Just me today, I’m afraid. Shapiro had to go up to Leeds for work. Sorry,’ she said, as she unwrapped Darsh from his sling and then unwrapped herself from the many layers of clothing she was wearing to keep out the cold. She didn’t mention the presence of the baby or why she’d brought him and so neither did I.

“恐怕今天只有我一个人。沙皮罗得去利兹出差了。抱歉。”她说着，从背带里解开达什，然后脱掉自己为了御寒而穿的多层衣服。她没提孩子在身边，也没说为什么带他来，所以我也没问。

Darsh sat on her lap passively facing me, his dark shock of hair standing upright as she pulled off his woolly blue hat. He looked at me intently with large brown eyes and bunched his small fist into his mouth. I smiled at him, and he frowned.

达什被动地坐在她腿上，面对着我，她摘下他那顶蓝色的羊毛帽时，他浓密的黑发直直地竖了起来。他用那双棕色的大眼睛专注地看着我，把小拳头攥进嘴里。我朝他笑了笑，他却皱起了眉头。

‘I thought you’d like to meet him,’ Bina explained. Darsh grumbled, whimpering a little and arching his back and immediately a look of panic spread over Bina’s face.

“我想你会想见见他，”比娜解释道。达什咕哝了一声，低声呜咽着，弓起了背，比娜脸上立刻浮现出惊恐的神色。

‘I don’t know what’s the matter,’ she said, frowning. ‘I just fed him before we walked here.’

“我不知道怎么回事，”她皱着眉头说，“我们来之前我刚喂过他。”

She pulled on his little tracksuit bottoms and said, ‘No poo. Shall I feed him again?’

她给他穿上小运动裤，问道：“没有便便。要不要再喂他一顿？”

‘Perhaps today you’d like me to take care of you and him?’ I said.

“或许今天你想让我照顾你和他？”我说。

‘That’d be nice,’ she responded smiling. ‘I’m exhausted.’

“那太好了，”她笑着回答，“我累坏了。”

Darsh whimpered again and his face crumpled in displeasure.

达什又呜咽了一声，脸上露出不满的神色。

‘What is it Darsh? What do you want?’ Her voice was slightly despairing. ‘I don’t seem to ever know what he wants.’ But, before she could elaborate on her thought, Darsh’s grumbling descended into a full-scale complaint and he began to cry.

“怎么了，达什？你想要什么？”她的声音里带着一丝绝望。“我好像永远也搞不清楚他想要什么。”但还没等她细说，达什的抱怨就变成了彻底的抱怨，他哭了起来。

Bina looked stumped. She lifted Darsh up and scrambled to her feet where she stood awkwardly jiggling him up and down. It was excruciating to watch – to see how helpless Bina felt and how lost Darsh was without a mother who could soothe him. His cries grew louder and her desperation grew larger and she looked at me with such misery that I felt tears prick my eyes. It felt so pitiful, I wanted to take them both into my arms.

比娜一脸茫然。她抱起达什，慌忙站起身，笨拙地上下摇晃着他。看着这一切，真是令人心痛——比娜如此无助，达什失去了母亲的安抚，多么迷茫无助。他的哭声越来越大，比娜的绝望也越来越强烈，她用那种悲惨的眼神看着我，我的眼眶也湿润了。这场景太可怜了，我真想把他们俩都拥入怀中。

It goes without saying that a psychotherapist must be able to empathise with people. In that moment, as I observed the crisis that was unfolding between Darsh and Bina, I felt empathy for them both. Darsh’s frantic cries pierced into me with urgent need and Bina’s forlorn desperation touched me too. A baby’s cry hits us in the gut. It’s designed that way – we’re hardwired to respond to that helplessness, an infant’s survival depends on that we do. But I’ve also been a mother and I know how daunting that can be; how tough mothering is and how painful it is to feel helpless in the face of desperate crying.

毋庸置疑，心理治疗师必须具备同理心。那一刻，当我目睹达什和比娜之间发生的危机时，我对他们两人都感同身受。达什焦急的哭声让我感到无比迫切，比娜的绝望也深深触动了我。婴儿的哭声直击人心。这是与生俱来的——我们天生就会对这种无助感做出反应，婴儿的生存依赖于我们的这种反应。但我同时也是一位母亲，我知道这有多么令人畏惧；我知道为人母有多么艰难，也知道面对孩子绝望的哭声时那种无助感有多么痛苦。

The Italian neuroscientist Vittorio Gallese has discovered that when we empathise with someone, identical neural systems in both brains fire up. It’s as though our brain is working to replicate the feelings of another person. In these experiences of empathic identification, we connect to an emotion that we may have had in the past but which is not our own in the present. For a moment, we allow ourselves to feel the other’s despair, fear, rage or joy. But if we lose ourselves in someone else’s feelings, or we find those feelings too overwhelming, we can’t help them – we need to fall into the feelings, connect and then separate our emotions from theirs, all in the twinkling of an eye. If we fail to empathise like this with our children or our partners, they feel misunderstood. And whilst that seems a little thing, being misunderstood by those we love is a painful, alienating experience.

意大利神经科学家维托里奥·加莱塞发现，当我们与他人共情时，双方大脑中相同的神经系统都会被激活。这就像我们的大脑在努力复制他人的感受。在这些共情体验中，我们会与一种我们过去可能经历过但此刻并不属于我们自身的情绪建立联系。那一刻，我们允许自己感受他人的绝望、恐惧、愤怒或喜悦。但如果我们沉浸于他人的感受之中，或者发现这些感受过于强烈，我们就无能为力——我们需要进入这些感受，建立联系，然后在瞬间将自己的情绪与他人的情绪区分开来。如果我们无法以这种方式与孩子或伴侣共情，他们会感到不被理解。虽然这看似一件小事，但被我们所爱的人误解却是一种痛苦而疏离的体验。

That afternoon, was I witnessing Bina’s trouble with empathising with Darsh? I think she knew he was uncomfortable and unhappy but it seemed she didn’t feel she could help him cope with it. It wasn’t that she couldn’t empathise with him, it was that she felt too much like him? Desperate and helpless.

那天下午，我是否目睹了比娜难以理解达什的感受？我想她知道他很不自在，很不开心，但她似乎觉得自己无力帮助他走出困境。并非她无法理解他，而是她觉得自己和他太像了——绝望而无助。

Darsh kept crying and Bina kept on jiggling. Eventually, I stood up and put out my arms to take him. He wriggled frantically and arched his back but I held him firmly against my shoulder and he began to quieten. Bina sat down and stared, her mouth slightly open, her face vacant.

达什不停地哭，比娜不停地扭动。最后，我站起身，张开双臂抱起他。他拼命地扭动着，弓起背，但我紧紧地把他搂在肩上，他渐渐安静下来。比娜坐了下来，呆呆地望着我，嘴巴微微张开，脸上毫无表情。

‘He likes you,’ she said weakly.

“他喜欢你，”她虚弱地说。

‘You must be very tired,’ I said and she nodded. Darsh was quiet now and I handed him back to Bina.

“你一定很累了，”我说，她点了点头。达什安静下来后，我把他还给了比娜。

‘Do you mind if I feed him? Is that OK?’

“我可以喂他吗？可以吗？”

She lifted her sweater and I saw Darsh shiver with excitement and root for her breast, attaching himself firmly with loud sucky noises.

她撩起毛衣，我看到达什兴奋得浑身颤抖，拼命地寻找她的乳房，发出响亮的吮吸声，牢牢地吸吮着。

‘At least the feeding seems to be going better now. I nearly gave up but the midwife said I should keep at it,’ Bina said.

“至少现在喂奶情况好多了。我差点就放弃了，但助产士说我应该坚持下去，”比娜说。

As Darsh sucked rhythmically, we also seemed to get into a rhythm. She talked and I listened. She told me her worries about her nipples, how she thought they were the wrong shape. How she worried that Shapiro wouldn’t find her body attractive, how they hadn’t even tried to have sex. She said her mother seemed fearful of helping with Darsh and she talked about how disappointed she felt about that. Her mum couldn’t understand how hard she was finding it and kept suggesting she should get a nanny. But though she didn’t want a nanny, she couldn’t really understand why. She talked and I listened and whilst we talked, Darsh slept, unmoving at her breast.

达什有节奏地吮吸着，我们似乎也找到了节奏。她说话，我倾听。她告诉我她对自己乳头的担忧，她觉得乳头的形状不对。她担心夏皮罗不会觉得她的身材有吸引力，他们甚至还没尝试过性生活。她说她妈妈似乎害怕帮忙照顾达什，她对此感到非常失望。她妈妈无法理解她有多难过，一直建议她请个保姆。虽然她不想请保姆，但她真的不明白为什么。她说话，我倾听，在我们交谈的时候，达什在她胸前一动不动地睡着了。

Most of the change that therapy brings is through these ordinary conversations – week in, week out. Patients talk about their lives, couples discuss who fills the fridge, who empties the bin. If people change, become more loving, more open to each other or themselves, it’s because someone has listened. Someone has listened who can bear to hear it all, the good, the bad and, indeed, the ugly.

治疗带来的改变大多源于这些日常对话——日复一日，周复一周。患者们谈论着自己的生活，伴侣们讨论着谁负责填满冰箱，谁负责倒垃圾。如果人们有所改变，变得更加友爱，更加坦诚地面对彼此或自己，那是因为有人倾听了他们。有人倾听了他们的一切，好的、坏的，甚至是丑陋的。

I don’t think anyone had really listened to Shapiro or Bina before; their brittle defences were the result of childhoods that hadn’t provided the understanding that children need to flourish. They’d been brought up to prize achievement above everything else and they had bought into that and created a shared culture within their marriage that put feelings and relationships way down the list of priorities. But babies have a way of changing things. They pull us back to our own infancy, stirring feelings often long repressed. Babies make us remember, so that in remembering, we can listen to the messages in their cries.

我想之前没人真正听过夏皮罗和比娜的话；她们脆弱的防御机制源于她们的童年经历，她们从小就没有接受过孩子健康成长所需的教育。她们从小就被教育要把成就看得高于一切，她们也接受了这种观念，并在婚姻中营造了一种将情感和人际关系置于次要地位的共同文化。但婴儿有一种改变一切的力量。他们把我们拉回自己的婴儿时期，唤醒那些常常被压抑已久的情感。婴儿让我们回忆起往事，在回忆的过程中，我们才能倾听他们哭声中传递的信息。
