Many couples pull themselves away from these feelings; mothers ignore the tingling in their breasts as their milk lets down on the way to the office. Fathers drop the baby at nursery and slog on to work to pay the bills. Most parents have no choice. Of course, sometimes it’s a relief to get away from the raw needs of a child but does it also mean shutting down and disconnecting from these raw needs? How else do you hand over the most precious thing in your life to someone else, for eight or nine hours a day?

许多夫妻会刻意回避这些感受；母亲们在上班路上会忽略乳房涌起的乳汁分泌感；父亲们会把孩子送到托儿所，然后继续埋头苦干，挣钱养家。大多数父母别无选择。当然，有时远离孩子最迫切的需求确实是一种解脱，但这是否也意味着要封闭自己，与这些需求脱节呢？否则，你又该如何将生命中最珍贵的东西，每天八九个小时，托付给别人呢？

We’ve structured a world in which the care of children seems to come way down the list of our priorities. Governments want workers and women rightly protest the disadvantage that full-time motherhood brings. But who advocates for the baby, who advocates for the importance of parents being able to be parents? We now know how critical the early years are, how the experiences that children have between birth and three can shape all of their lives. Do long hours in nursery care provide an optimal experience for most children? Do most parents of young children want to spend more time at work than with their infants? Why can’t we allow new parents to work less? Why don’t we value the time they spend caring for their family as much as the time spent in the office?

我们构建的世界里，儿童保育似乎被远远地抛在了次要位置。政府希望员工就业，女性也理所当然地抗议全职母亲所面临的不利处境。但是，谁来为婴儿发声？谁来倡导父母履行父母职责的重要性？我们现在知道，幼儿时期至关重要，孩子从出生到三岁的经历会如何影响他们的一生。长时间待在托儿所真的能为大多数孩子提供最佳体验吗？大多数年轻父母真的希望把更多的时间花在工作上而不是陪伴孩子上吗？为什么我们不能允许新手父母减少工作时间？为什么我们不把他们照顾家庭的时间看得比在办公室的时间更重要？

As a psychotherapist, it’s not my job to judge or to recommend a particular way of living. But psychotherapy is political because its manifesto values the importance of human relationships much more than money or success. It’s also true to say that a good therapy often resets the values of our patients, altering their priorities.

作为一名心理治疗师，我的职责并非评判或推荐某种特定的生活方式。但心理治疗本身具有政治性，因为它的理念是人际关系远比金钱或成功更重要。同样不可否认的是，一次成功的治疗往往能够重塑患者的价值观，改变他们的优先事项。

I think the therapy with Bina and Shapiro helped them. Everything about them softened and they didn’t hire the two nannies after all. Bina never went back to her old job and when Darsh was one, Shapiro left his job too. They wanted a different future for themselves and something different to their own childhoods for Darsh. By the time they finished the therapy, Bina was pregnant again and they’d started their own business and this time, it was going to be a family business.

我认为比娜和夏皮罗的心理治疗对他们很有帮助。他们性格变得温和了许多，最终也没有再雇佣那两个保姆。比娜再也没有回到原来的工作岗位，达什一岁时，夏皮罗也辞去了工作。他们想要一个不一样的未来，也希望达什能拥有一个与他们自己截然不同的童年。治疗结束后，比娜再次怀孕，他们也开始了自己的事业，这一次，他们打算把它发展成家族企业。

# ↩

Gabrielle and Johannes Blow the Straw House down and Then Do Some Rebuilding

加布里埃尔和约翰内斯把稻草屋吹倒，然后开始重建。

I’m dreaming about a boat. It sails, tacking back and forth in the gentlest of winds, luffing more than actually moving. The boat is a sickly yellow and I’m trying desperately to steer it through rock-strewn waters. I’m scared I’m going to run aground and there’s a nagging worry about what’s below deck and whether it can get out. Is there a hole in the hull? Then I wake, sweating, my nose dry and my throat raw.

我梦见一艘船。它在微风中摇曳，来回穿梭，与其说是前进，不如说是颠簸。船身是病态的黄色，我拼命地想把它驶过布满礁石的水域。我害怕搁浅，心里一直惦记着甲板下的东西，担心它们能不能逃出去。船体是不是有个洞？然后我醒了过来，浑身是汗，鼻子干涩，喉咙嘶哑。

It was my fifth day of being ill. The coronavirus had come on suddenly. I’d cooked lunch for friends and we’d had the back door open in celebration of spring, which was just poking its nose through the grey, wet weather. It was convivial; we’d bumped elbows and reassured each other that we’d still have a summer. Plans were made for meeting in Suffolk as we drank our way through a long, lazy lunch. Later, I felt hot. ‘I’ve got that coronavirus thing,’ I told my husband. He scoffed but frowned when I showed him the thermometer.

这是我生病的第五天。新冠病毒来得猝不及防。我为朋友们做了午饭，为了庆祝春天的到来——尽管春天刚刚从阴雨绵绵的天气里探出头来——我们打开了后门。气氛很融洽；我们碰碰胳膊肘，互相安慰说夏天依然会到来。我们一边悠闲地享用着午餐，一边喝酒聊天，还计划着在萨福克郡见面。后来，我感觉有点发烧。“我得了新冠病毒，”我告诉丈夫。他嗤之以鼻，但当我给他看体温计时，他皱起了眉头。

I’d upgraded my Zoom account the previous week – it was obvious that trotting off to Queen Anne Street to see my patients wasn’t going to be sustainable. We’d bought the hand sanitiser and I’d taken to wiping down the doorknobs between sessions but by mid-March the virus had got out of the pen and was rampaging through central London. There were conversations amongst my colleagues about Zoom, Skype and Microsoft Teams, and hastily convened meetings to share know-how and concerns about moving – sometimes very vulnerable patients – online. And then I became ill and my patients had to wait.

前一周我升级了Zoom账号——很明显，每天跑到皇后街去看望病人已经行不通了。我们买了洗手液，我也开始在每次诊疗间隙擦拭门把手，但到了三月中旬，病毒已经扩散开来，在伦敦市中心肆虐。我的同事们开始讨论Zoom、Skype和Microsoft Teams，并紧急召开会议，分享经验，探讨如何将一些非常脆弱的病人转移到线上诊疗。然后，我也病倒了，我的病人只能继续等待。

Two weeks later, I was sufficiently recovered to restart my practice in this new and rather unsettling world. I’d taken care to buy myself a new camera to upgrade the one on my old laptop and I’d rearranged my home office with an easy chair from my downstairs consulting room. I placed the laptop on my office chair so I could adjust the height and strapped myself into Zoom. It felt very strange and, still exhausted from the virus, I wasn’t looking forward to the day.

两周后，我身体恢复得差不多了，可以在这个令人不安的新世界里重新开始我的工作。我特意买了个新摄像头来替换旧笔记本电脑上的，还把楼下诊室的椅子搬到了家里的办公室。我把笔记本电脑放在办公椅上，调整好高度，然后打开了Zoom。感觉很陌生，而且因为感染病毒仍然很疲惫，我并不期待这一天的到来。

I was due to see Johannes and Gabrielle, who consulted me from time to time. When they first came, acrimony and distrust suffused every word they spoke. Back then, I had needed all my authority to quell the accusations and counter-accusations that were being flung about my office like grenades. They’d been in and out of court for a year and the judge, fed up with them, had wearily suggested they seek therapy. Neither wanted to be sitting with each other in my consulting room but they’d run out of road with their fantasy that they could win the battle and avoid compromise. Gradually, they’d made progress and been able to co-operate a little more around their two children. But the peace was fragile and when it broke down, they came to see me.

我原本约好要见约翰内斯和加布里埃尔，他们时不时会来咨询我。他们第一次来的时候，每句话都充满了怨恨和不信任。那时，我得使出浑身解数才能平息他们互相指责、互相反驳的局面，那些指责和反驳像手榴弹一样在我办公室里乱飞。他们一年来一直在法庭上进进出出，法官对他们感到厌烦，无奈地建议他们接受心理治疗。他们俩都不想坐在我的咨询室里，但他们幻想自己能赢得这场争斗、避免妥协的幻想已经破灭了。渐渐地，他们取得了一些进展，在两个孩子的问题上也能稍微合作一些。但这种和平很脆弱，一旦破裂，他们就来找我了。

Both of them were fat. Not nicely rounded in a way that suggested just one too many trips to the fridge but so overweight that it seemed to suggest a sustained refusal to care for themselves. Was something desperate and destructive being expressed through their bodies, which was echoed in the anger that they vented on each other?

他们俩都很胖。不是那种因为吃得太多而显得圆润的胖，而是胖得仿佛长期拒绝照顾自己。是不是某种绝望而具有破坏性的情绪通过他们的身体表达出来，而这种情绪又在他们彼此发泄的愤怒中得到了呼应？

I like parenting consultations – they’re different from long, ongoing psychotherapy. I enjoy the work with couples who are finding it hard to adjust to being parents or who are suddenly really challenged by an adolescent revolt. I find satisfaction in supporting parents who are worried because their child is depressed, school refusing or in other kinds of trouble. I like it because I can use different parts of myself – I can be a kind of parenting coach; I can be a sympathetic ear; I can offer some reflections on the family dynamics and I can relate to parents from my own experience of parenting. Most important of all, I feel that I’m caring for the children too.

我喜欢育儿咨询——它不同于漫长的心理治疗。我乐于帮助那些难以适应为人父母的角色，或突然面临孩子青春期叛逆挑战的夫妇。我乐于支持那些因孩子抑郁、厌学或其他问题而忧心忡忡的父母。我喜欢这份工作，因为我可以运用自身的不同特质——我可以扮演育儿教练的角色；我可以倾听他们的心声；我可以就家庭动态提供一些思考；我还能凭借自身的育儿经验与父母产生共鸣。最重要的是，我觉得自己也在关心孩子们。

Every couple therapist is confronted with the challenges children present to a relationship and many couples who seek therapy argue a lot about parenting. What is clear from numerous studies across the globe is that marital satisfaction declines steeply when you have a baby. Google ‘marital satisfaction and having children’ and you will see a plethora of graphs showing a U-shaped curve. Happiness declines with the first child and having further children makes the decline deeper. Then, just as things seem to be getting easier, children reach the teenage years and couple contentment goes into a further deep dive. But stick it out because as the children begin to leave home, things gradually improve. I remember years ago showing these graphs during a training day for children’s centre managers and there was a shocked silence until one woman stood up in dismay, blurting, ‘Why did no one tell me this?!’

每位婚姻咨询师都会遇到孩子给夫妻关系带来的挑战，许多前来咨询的夫妻也经常因为育儿问题争吵。全球众多研究表明，有了孩子后，婚姻满意度会急剧下降。在谷歌上搜索“婚姻满意度与生育”，你会看到大量图表，它们都呈现出U型曲线。第一个孩子出生后，幸福感就开始下降，而随着孩子数量的增加，这种下降趋势会更加明显。正当一切似乎开始好转的时候，孩子进入青春期，夫妻的满意度又会进一步下滑。但请坚持下去，因为随着孩子陆续离家，情况会逐渐好转。我记得几年前，我在一次儿童中心经理的培训日上展示了这些图表，现场一片震惊的沉默，直到一位女士沮丧地站起来，脱口而出：“为什么没人告诉我这些？！”

This decline in relationship happiness frequently begins in the first year after the birth of a baby. The baby arrives and, for most couples, there is joy – grandparents coo, friends bring cakes, balloons, cards and flowers arrive with the postman and everything is mostly rosy for a while. But baby coming first eventually takes its toll and as time passes, parents come to realise that their needs have been overtaken by their children’s, which can evoke strong feelings of deprivation and neglect. These feelings may reactivate distress about similar feelings experienced earlier in their lives, adding an overlay from the past to the intensity of what is happening in the present. In response to these feelings, each partner may look to the other to fill the gap and to ameliorate these feelings of deprivation, which then provokes a competition of needs. Couples begin to argue about whose turn it is to change a nappy, whose turn is it to get up in the night or whose turn it is to have a night out with friends. In this situation, parents begin to ‘shift parent’, monitoring who’s clocked on and who’s having time off. Whilst this seems to be a kind of solution to the arguments, in time, this kind of parenting produces even further distance between the couple and pleasures derived from shared activities around the children are lost.

这种关系幸福感的下降通常始于孩子出生后的第一年。宝宝的到来，对大多数夫妻来说都是喜悦的——祖父母的咿呀声，朋友们带来的蛋糕、气球、贺卡和鲜花，一切都显得格外美好。然而，宝宝优先终究会带来压力。随着时间的推移，父母逐渐意识到自己的需求被孩子的需求所掩盖，这会引发强烈的被忽视和被冷落感。这些感受可能会重新唤起他们早年生活中类似的痛苦经历，让过去的阴影叠加在当下的困境之上。为了应对这些感受，夫妻双方可能会寻求对方来填补空缺，缓解这种被忽视的感觉，从而引发需求上的竞争。夫妻开始争吵，比如谁该换尿布，谁该在夜里起床照顾孩子，或者谁该和朋友出去玩。在这种情况下，父母开始“轮流照顾孩子”，密切关注谁在上班，谁在休息。虽然这看似能暂时缓解争吵，但久而久之，这种育儿方式反而会加剧夫妻间的疏离，让他们失去共同陪伴孩子所带来的乐趣。

The experience of mothers is often somewhat different from fathers. Mothers still undertake a greater proportion of domestic and child-rearing tasks than men, though there is evidence that this is beginning to change. Men often feel something of the outsider in the face of the intense breastfeeding dyad of mother and baby and this sense of exclusion leads some men to focus on their life outside the family, which in practice often means their work. On the other hand, rather than feeling excluded, mothers may have strong claustrophobic feelings as they spend all day with an infant in their arms or at their breast. These differing experiences can make having sex tricky. Men want sex to reclaim their partners, to reassure and be reassured that there is still time for adult love amid the love fest around the baby. But women may find their strongest urge is not for more cuddles but for more space and their partner’s wish for sex may be felt as a further encroachment on themselves.

母亲的经历通常与父亲有所不同。尽管有证据表明这种情况正在发生改变，但母亲仍然承担着比男性更多的家务和育儿工作。面对母亲和婴儿紧张的哺乳互动，男性常常感到自己像个局外人，这种被排斥感导致一些男性将注意力集中在家庭之外的生活上，而这在实践中通常意味着他们的工作。另一方面，母亲们并非感到被排斥，而是可能因为整天抱着婴儿或喂奶而感到强烈的幽闭恐惧。这些不同的经历会使性生活变得棘手。男性渴望性爱来重新掌控伴侣，来确认和寻求确认，在围绕婴儿的爱意满满的生活中，仍然有时间享受成人的爱。但女性可能发现她们最强烈的渴望并非更多的拥抱，而是更多的空间，伴侣对性爱的渴望可能会让她们感到被侵犯。

And then there are the in-laws. Up until a baby comes, the couple may have chosen to be quite insular from the wider family but suddenly grandparents and aunts and uncles appear. They may be helpful, and they certainly may be needed, but a renewed connection between one partner and their family of origin may require big adjustments and the need to redraw the boundaries around the relationship. Family culture – how you parent, make a Christmas, make a home and celebrate birthdays – is often derived from what we experienced in our own childhood. A new family has to work out what its new culture will be and this negotiation can bring about conflict when expectations of family life differ. Grandma and Mummy may have one view about how baby should be fed that may differ hugely from Daddy’s expectations derived from his own family.

还有姻亲的问题。在孩子出生之前，夫妻俩可能选择与大家庭保持相当的距离，但突然之间，祖父母、叔叔阿姨们就出现了。他们或许会提供帮助，而且肯定必不可少，但一方与原生家庭重新建立联系可能需要做出巨大的调整，并需要重新界定彼此关系的界限。家庭文化——如何养育子女、如何过圣诞节、如何营造家庭氛围以及如何庆祝生日——通常源于我们自身的童年经历。一个新家庭必须摸索出属于自己的新文化，而当对家庭生活的期望存在差异时，这种协商就可能引发冲突。祖父母对如何喂养婴儿可能有一套看法，而爸爸的期望可能源于他自己的家庭，两者之间可能存在巨大差异。

All the challenges I describe above can be usefully explored in couple therapy and it is a great shame that couples often leave it far too long to come and talk about these matters. Over recent years, successive governments have placed greater emphasis on early intervention for new parents, initiating pilot schemes to encourage them to focus on their relationship and as a result, some years ago, I and a colleague set up a co-parenting consultation service.

我上面提到的所有挑战都可以在伴侣治疗中得到有效探讨，但令人遗憾的是，很多伴侣往往拖延太久才来谈论这些问题。近年来，历届政府都更加重视对新手父母的早期干预，并启动试点项目鼓励他们关注彼此的关系。因此，几年前，我和一位同事创办了共同育儿咨询服务。

We expected concerned and anxious parents of teenage children and younger parents struggling with their babies and with collaborating over sleep training, feeding and childcare. To our surprise, none of these couples came. Instead, we saw broken couples who really didn’t want to co-operate, who’d much prefer it if their ex was dead or gone. We had lawyers sending us huge files containing the miserable details of bitter disputes. We had couples who literally wouldn’t sit together in the consulting room and, in one case, a woman insisting her scary-looking mother be present to ‘protect’ her from her ex.

我们原本以为会遇到一些忧心忡忡、焦虑不安的父母，他们的孩子正值青春期；还有一些年轻的父母，他们正为如何训练孩子睡眠、喂养和育儿而苦恼。但出乎意料的是，这些夫妇一个也没来。相反，我们看到的是一些关系破裂、根本不想合作的夫妻，他们宁愿对方已经去世或离开。律师们给我们发来了厚厚的文件，里面详细记录着双方痛苦的争执。有些夫妻甚至不愿意一起坐在咨询室里，还有一位女士坚持要她看起来很吓人的母亲在场，说是要“保护”她免受前夫的伤害。

This all came as a shock and we were, initially, quite unprepared. Gradually, however, we learnt to work with these separated couples and were often able to help. We were also naively shocked at how little provision there is for these parents who fall outside of the court system. How little, as a society, we have concerned ourselves with the plight of children caught between warring parents. Every study of separation and divorce concludes that unresolved and sustained conflict between parents is deeply harmful to children and yet extraordinarily little time and few resources are made available to help these families. Lawyers make money, judges make judgements and children are left to navigate that most complex territory of managing the relationship between combatant parents. Something I, after 35 years of working with couples, can barely manage myself.

这一切都让我们措手不及，起初我们完全没有准备。然而，我们逐渐学会了如何与这些分居夫妇相处，并且常常能够帮到他们。我们也天真地震惊于，对于那些无法通过司法系统解决的父母，社会提供的帮助竟然如此之少。作为一个社会，我们对夹在争吵不休的父母之间的孩子的困境关注甚少。每一项关于分居和离婚的研究都得出结论：父母之间未解决且持续的冲突对孩子造成了极大的伤害，然而，用于帮助这些家庭的时间和资源却少得可怜。律师赚钱，法官判决，而孩子们却不得不独自面对处理父母之间复杂关系的重重困境。即便是我，在从事夫妻咨询工作35年后，也几乎难以应对这种情况。

This kind of therapeutic work is often challenging and frustrating. Parents suddenly refuse to come to the sessions or they walk out midway. The therapist is copied in to email trails that list past slights and abuses. Accusations are made that can make your hair stand on end and sometimes demand a call to the GP or a social worker. And this was the case with Johannes and Gabrielle.

这种治疗工作往往充满挑战和挫折。家长们会突然拒绝参加治疗，或者中途离场。治疗师会收到记录着过去种种轻视和虐待行为的电子邮件。他们会提出一些令人毛骨悚然的指控，有时甚至需要联系家庭医生或社工。约翰内斯和加布里埃尔的遭遇正是如此。

They had two children who were the subject of their dispute. Nathan, aged four, who, just months before they separated, had been diagnosed as autistic, and Mia, who was 20 months. I never saw their children and, at first, neither Nathan nor Mia were talked about in any real way. The children were constantly referred to but it took a long time to get a picture of how they were doing. It felt, at times, that they were just commodities to be fought over.

他们有两个孩子，也是他们争执的焦点。四岁的内森，在他们分居前几个月被诊断出患有自闭症；还有20个月大的米娅。我从未见过他们的孩子，起初，他们也从未真正谈论过内森和米娅。虽然他们经常提到孩子，但要了解他们的近况却需要很长时间。有时，我感觉他们就像是争夺的物品。

The first session was a nightmare. They arrived separately. Gabrielle came first and objected to being asked to wait outside until Johannes arrived. I knew it would be fatal to begin without him; I didn’t want to start by creating any sense that she and I had established some rapport from which he was excluded. But at the time, I had no waiting room and it was a bitterly cold day outside. The minutes ticked by and I felt worse and worse for leaving Gabrielle in the street. Eventually, I heard footsteps and both tumbled down the stairs and into my office in a rush. I was startled by their size. They seemed to take up a lot of space and I suddenly felt a bit overwhelmed by their presence.

第一次咨询简直是一场噩梦。他们俩分别到的。加布里埃尔先到，她很不情愿被要求在外面等约翰内斯。我知道不等他就开始咨询会很糟糕；我不想一开始就给人留下我和她之间建立了某种默契，而他却被排除在外的印象。但当时我没有候诊室，外面又冷得刺骨。时间一分一秒地过去，我越来越后悔把加布里埃尔留在街上。最后，我听到了脚步声，他们俩赶紧冲下楼梯，跑进我的办公室。他们的体型吓了我一跳。他们似乎占据了很大的空间，我突然感到有些不知所措。

‘Shall we begin?’ I asked, as they settled in the two chairs that were furthest apart.

“我们开始吧？”我问道，他们则在两张距离最远的椅子上坐了下来。

Gabrielle shot me a hostile look and then, ignoring Johannes, said, ‘Why the fuck is he so late?’ Without waiting for an answer, she proceeded to tell me that it was pointless being here and that she was only doing it because her court appointed social worker said she must. She then added that I mustn’t believe anything Johannes said as he was a pathological liar.

加布里埃尔恶狠狠地瞪了我一眼，然后无视约翰内斯，问道：“他怎么这么晚才来？” 不等我回答，她就开始说来也白来一趟，她来这里只是因为法院指定的社工让她这么做。她还说，约翰内斯说的任何话都不要信，因为他是个病态的骗子。

This wasn’t a promising start. And worse, within minutes, the two of them were in meltdown and I was just an observer as Johannes accused Gabrielle of deliberately misleading him about the time of the appointment.

这并非一个好兆头。更糟糕的是，几分钟之内，两人就情绪崩溃，而我只能眼睁睁地看着约翰内斯指责加布里埃尔故意在预约时间上误导他。

I put up my hand, palm flat and outwards, and firmly told them that if they wanted to spend their money on this argument they certainly could but it was a pointless waste and, more importantly, wouldn’t in any way help their children. I can’t say that this was a turning point. In that first session, I must have raised my hand to stop them half a dozen times. But when I asked them to tell me about Nathan and Mia, when I enquired about Mia’s language development and how they felt about Nathan’s diagnosis of autism, they grew slightly more circumspect, at least for a while.

我举起手，掌心平放向外，坚定地告诉他们，如果他们想把钱花在这场争论上，当然可以，但这毫无意义，而且更重要的是，对他们的孩子没有任何帮助。我不能说这是一个转折点。在第一次咨询中，我至少举手阻止了他们六次。但当我请他们谈谈内森和米娅的情况，当我询问米娅的语言发展以及他们对内森被诊断为自闭症的看法时，他们的态度稍微谨慎了一些，至少暂时如此。

Four days after the first session, I had an email from Johannes saying that his contact with the children had been stopped because Gabrielle had accused him of being ‘inappropriate’ with Nathan. My heart sank, this was deeply worrying. I learnt that Nathan had apparently told his mother that he’d ‘played with’ Daddy’s penis in the bath and now social workers were investigating. Johannes was outraged, asserting that nothing had occurred beyond a four-year-old’s ordinary curiosity. I wasn’t surprised when they cancelled their session.

第一次面谈四天后，我收到约翰内斯的邮件，说他与孩子们的接触被中止了，因为加布里埃尔指控他对内森“行为不端”。我顿时心头一沉，这真是令人担忧。后来我得知，内森竟然告诉他妈妈，他在浴缸里“玩弄”了爸爸的生殖器，现在社工正在调查此事。约翰内斯对此非常愤怒，坚称这不过是一个四岁孩子正常的好奇心作祟。他们取消面谈，我一点也不感到意外。

Separating is hard; losing love and that sense of belonging to someone is disorientating and painful. Often, we erect such enormous barriers to mourning our losses that it can seem impossible to see over the top of them, towards a future. Some people mourn quietly; they retreat and hide themselves away. Others mourn a separation noisily, sharing their grief, their hurt and their worries with friends, therapists, colleagues and family. Many of us mourn angrily. We find ourselves furious at our losses, raging at the unfairness of it and incensed by the sense of powerlessness that loss engenders. And, furious, we look to blame and punish, which is a potent recipe for a court battle.

分离是痛苦的；失去爱和归属感会让人迷失方向，倍感痛苦。我们常常会筑起巨大的壁垒来逃避失去的痛苦，以至于看不到未来。有些人默默地哀悼，他们退缩，把自己封闭起来。有些人则大声地哀悼分离，与朋友、心理咨询师、同事和家人分享他们的悲伤、痛苦和担忧。我们中的许多人则愤怒地哀悼。我们发现自己对失去感到愤怒，对其中的不公感到愤慨，并对失去带来的无力感感到愤怒。愤怒之下，我们寻求指责和惩罚，这很容易引发一场官司。

Two months later, the couple asked for a further appointment. Johannes had emailed to tell me that an investigation had been conducted and social services reported no concerns. The children were able to resume their overnight stays with him but, he wrote, Gabrielle was still putting up barriers in the way of his contact with the children. I agreed to see them the following week, prepared for the session to be difficult.

两个月后，这对夫妇要求再次面谈。约翰内斯发邮件告诉我，社会服务部门已经进行了调查，并表示没有发现任何问题。孩子们可以恢复在他家过夜，但他写道，加布里埃尔仍然阻挠他与孩子们接触。我同意下周与他们见面，并做好了这次面谈会很艰难的准备。

Within minutes of arriving, Johannes broke down in angry tears as he described the child welfare investigation and the intrusion and the shame. He told me how scared he’d been, how fearful he was. Would he be charged with abuse? Would he lose the children? For over a month, he had no contact with either of the children and then he’d only been able to see them at a contact centre whilst a social worker observed him. As he spoke, Gabrielle sat there listening, seemingly chastened. But her silence didn’t last and it wasn’t long before they, hot with feeling, began to fight. Again, I focused relentlessly on how their children were being damaged by this fighting and it seemed, slowly, to be sinking in.

约翰内斯刚到没几分钟，就情绪崩溃，泪流满面地讲述着儿童福利调查、侵犯隐私和羞辱的经历。他告诉我他有多么害怕，多么恐惧。他会不会被指控虐待儿童？他会不会失去孩子的监护权？整整一个多月，他都无法联系到两个孩子，之后也只能在社工的监督下，在探视中心见他们。他说话的时候，加布里埃尔坐在那里听着，似乎有些羞愧。但她的沉默并没有持续多久，没过多久，两人就因为情绪激动而争吵起来。我再次强调，他们的争吵正在伤害他们的孩子，而加布里埃尔似乎慢慢地开始意识到这一点。

‘I know you really want to hurt each other, to pay each other back for the pain and distress you feel, but you need to realise there’s no such thing as a clean, clear shot here. There’s always collateral damage. Your children are getting hit by the shrapnel from your fights every day.’

我知道你们真的很想伤害对方，想报复对方所感受到的痛苦和折磨，但你们需要明白，这里没有干净利落的打击。总会有附带伤害。你们的孩子每天都在被你们争吵的碎片击中。

During this early period, I had several single sessions with them. I knew they were both still deeply wounded from what had occurred in their relationship and how it had ended and I believed these residual feelings were getting in the way of their parenting. They had told me that their relationship had always been intense, passionate and stormy and, though they were both resolved it was over, they were certainly having a hard time moving on. It seemed to me that they kept the previous intensity of their old relationship going by having these endless fights and even though they were now separated, they seemed to be just as involved with each other through these rows as they’d been when they were together. Were these fights a way of avoiding a real ending? Perhaps this lively combat was better than being faced with the desolate silence of mourning?

在这段初期，我分别和他们进行了几次单独咨询。我知道他们都还深深地被之前感情中发生的事情以及最终的结局所伤，而且我认为这些残留的伤痛正在影响他们为人父母的方式。他们告诉我，他们的感情一直都很激烈、充满激情，但也充满波折。虽然他们都明白这段感情已经结束了，但他们显然很难真正放下。在我看来，他们似乎通过无休止的争吵来维持过去感情中的那种强烈状态。即使现在他们已经分开，但这些争吵中他们似乎仍然像以前在一起时那样投入。这些争吵是不是他们逃避真正结束的一种方式？或许，这种激烈的争吵比面对悲伤的寂静要好得多？

Johannes, a writer of crime fiction, was a curious mix. He spoke fluently with a confident assurance that came from his stellar education and his career success and yet, despite his imposing size and voice, he conveyed an anxious vulnerability too. His mother had put him temporarily into care when he was a toddler, which led to periods with foster parents and stays in children’s homes. He would see his mother from time to time but she never seemed able to provide a permanent home for him, so, eventually, aged six, he was adopted. His adoptive parents, he told me, were loving but they were members of an evangelical church which meant that life was rather austere and very rule bound. Now, he hated rules or rigidity of any sort and, though he was reeling from losing his home and terrified that Gabrielle would take the children from him, he found it hard to go along with all the rules about when and how he could see them. Johannes had a quick intelligence and saw immediately when I pointed it out that the abandonment he’d experienced in his early childhood and the rigidity of his adoptive parents were affecting his responses to the current situation. But though he knew this intellectually, deep in his gut he felt an overwhelming sense of distrust and fear.

约翰内斯是一位犯罪小说作家，他的性格十分奇特。他说话流利，自信满满，这源于他卓越的教育背景和事业上的成功；然而，尽管他身材魁梧，嗓音洪亮，却也流露出一种焦虑和脆弱。他幼年时，母亲曾将他暂时送去寄养家庭，之后他辗转于不同的寄养家庭和儿童之家。他偶尔会见到母亲，但她似乎始终无法给他提供一个稳定的家，最终，在他六岁时，他被收养了。他告诉我，养父母很慈爱，但他们是福音派教会的成员，这意味着他们的生活相当简朴，规矩繁多。他生性厌恶任何形式的规矩和僵化，尽管他正因失去家园而痛苦不堪，也害怕加布里埃尔会把孩子们带走，但他还是很难接受那些关于何时以及如何探望孩子的种种规定。约翰内斯心思敏捷，我一指出他幼年时期被遗弃的经历以及养父母的严苛管教，他就立刻明白了，这些都影响着他对现状的反应。虽然他理智上明白这一点，但内心深处却涌起一股强烈的不信任感和恐惧。

Whilst Johannes wore his heart on his sleeve, Gabrielle was much more closed. Her grief was locked up inside her and she regarded me not as an ally but as someone who was judging her. She was startlingly pretty. Her rounded face had a luminous quality, with clear olive skin and rich dark brown straight hair. She spoke with a strong South African accent and often turned her face away from me, which combined to make me feel both dismissed and curious about her. Later, I began to see that she turned away to hide her feelings and that great shame was attached to any expression of vulnerability. She said little about her childhood except that her parents had divorced when she was four and that her mother had remarried a bullying, selfish man whom Gabrielle had hated. Her stepfather had died when she was 19 and Gabrielle’s indifference to his death had driven a permanent wedge between her and her mother.

约翰内斯喜怒形于色，而加布里埃尔则封闭得多。她将悲伤深埋心底，并不把我当成盟友，而是视我为评判者。她美得惊人。圆润的脸庞透着光彩，橄榄色的肌肤透亮，一头浓密的深棕色直发。她操着一口浓重的南非口音，常常把脸转向一边，这让我既感到被忽视，又对她充满好奇。后来，我渐渐明白，她转过脸去是为了掩饰自己的感受，任何流露出的脆弱都让她感到无比羞耻。她很少谈及自己的童年，只说父母在她四岁时离异，母亲改嫁给一个专横跋扈、自私自利的男人，加布里埃尔恨透了他。继父在她十九岁时去世，加布里埃尔对他的死漠不关心，这在她和母亲之间筑起了一道永远无法逾越的鸿沟。

It took nearly a year of fortnightly and then monthly sessions before things were calmer. And then, with some general agreements in place about care of the children and money issues, they ended therapy on the understanding they could come and see me from time to time if they wished. And they did. Every six months or so, they’d come and we’d discuss issues they were struggling with. Which nursery for Mia? What help for Nathan? Could Johannes’s new girlfriend meet the children?

在经历了近一年的两周一次、后来每月一次的会谈后，情况才逐渐平静下来。之后，双方就孩子的照料和经济问题达成了一些共识，并在同意他们可以随时来找我咨询的前提下结束了治疗。他们也确实这么做了。大约每六个月，他们都会来，我们一起讨论他们遇到的难题。比如，米娅该去哪家托儿所？内森需要什么帮助？约翰内斯的新女友能不能见见孩子们？

When working with separated couples, I often think of the ‘Judgement of Solomon’, a story from the Old Testament in which King Solomon of Israel rules between two women, both claiming to be the mother of a child. Unable to agree, Solomon tells the mothers that the solution is to cut the child in two, so that each of them can have a half. A sword is brought to the King to enact his judgement and then the real mother, unable to bear her son being killed, offers the child to the other woman to save the baby’s life, whilst the other agrees to the halving. In this way the false mother is exposed and King Solomon then restores the child to its real mother. Sometimes, in the work with Johannes and Gabrielle, I felt as if I was being asked to be a kind of Solomon, though I never recommended any chopping up of either Nathan or Mia!

在辅导分居夫妇时，我常常想起《旧约》中的“所罗门审判”故事。故事讲述的是以色列国王所罗门在两个女人之间争执，她们都声称自己是同一个孩子的母亲。由于无法达成一致，所罗门告诉她们，解决办法是将孩子劈成两半，一人一半。有人拿来一把剑，准备由国王执行审判。这时，真正的母亲不忍心让自己的儿子被杀，便将孩子交给另一个女人以保全孩子的性命，而另一个女人则同意将孩子劈成两半。就这样，假母亲的身份被揭穿，所罗门王将孩子归还给了真正的母亲。有时，在辅导约翰内斯和加布里埃尔的过程中，我感觉自己仿佛被要求扮演某种所罗门的角色，尽管我从未建议把内森或米娅也劈成两半！

I was proud of Johannes and Gabrielle and proud of my work. They might still squabble and cuss but, in the end, they’d decided not to damage their babies but to put them first, even if it meant at times giving in to each other.

我为约翰内斯和加布里埃尔感到骄傲，也为我的工作感到骄傲。他们或许还会争吵、咒骂，但最终，他们决定不伤害自己的孩子，而是把孩子放在第一位，即使这意味着有时需要向对方妥协。

But as lockdown kicked in, here they were again, arguing fiercely from the trenches of their respective living rooms. I wondered if Zoom was making it easier for them to let rip, that they felt safer chucking accusations via a computer rather than in person. It was as if all the work we’d done over the years now counted for nothing. I wondered if this was the result of three weeks of lockdown – schools and nurseries were closed and they were now both on their own with the children. Johannes looked desperate and his sense of desperation began to infect me as the intermittent message Johannes’s internet is unstable was accompanied by the loss of sound and vision. My head hurt as I tried to gather up what was going on but it was impossible to make much sense because I could only hear one word in three.

但随着封锁措施的实施，他们又开始在各自的客厅里激烈争吵。我不禁怀疑，Zoom 是否让他们更容易放纵自己，是不是他们觉得通过电脑互相指责比当面指责更安全。仿佛我们这些年来所做的一切努力都付诸东流。我琢磨着，这是否是三周封锁的后果——学校和幼儿园都关门了，他们现在只能独自照顾孩子。约翰内斯看起来很绝望，他的绝望也开始感染我，因为时不时会听到“约翰内斯的网络不稳定”的提示音，同时伴随着声音和画面的中断。我头痛欲裂，努力想弄明白发生了什么，但根本无法理解，因为我只能听清三分之一的字。

‘Susanna, can you hear me? Susanna, can I speak?’

“苏珊娜，你能听到我说话吗？苏珊娜，我可以说话吗？”

Gabrielle interrupted. ‘Why is your internet so shit Johannes? Can’t you do something about it? Turn off your video.’

加布里埃尔打断道：“约翰内斯，你的网怎么这么烂？你就不能解决一下吗？把视频关掉。”

Eventually, I learnt that the dispute was over where the children should reside during lockdown. Nathan and Mia were currently at Gabrielle’s in Hackney but, as the pandemic had hit, Johannes had fled from his flat by Victoria Park to his girlfriend’s cottage in Sussex. Gabrielle was adamant that the children shouldn’t travel to the countryside, that it was against the rules and wasn’t safe. If Johannes wanted to see them, he should come back to London.

最终，我了解到这场争执的焦点在于孩子们在封锁期间应该住在哪里。内森和米娅当时住在哈克尼的加布里埃尔家，但随着疫情爆发，约翰内斯从他在维多利亚公园附近的公寓逃到了他女友位于苏塞克斯的乡间小屋。加布里埃尔坚决认为孩子们不应该去乡下，因为这违反规定，而且不安全。如果约翰内斯想见他们，就应该回到伦敦。

‘There’s no way they’re going to Sussex. It’s not safe and I don’t want them that far from me. What if they’re ill? And actually, what if I get ill when they’re with me? I didn’t even know that he wasn’t at home until I called him on Tuesday with a migraine and he said he couldn’t come and pick them up. So, Susanna, I was left with them on my own, thinking I was going to be really ill with coronavirus. It’s such a complete betrayal of my trust … as usual, you’re just putting yourself first.’ She would have continued but I stopped her in mid-sentence.

“他们绝对不能去苏塞克斯。那里不安全，我不想让他们离我那么远。万一他们生病了怎么办？而且，万一我跟他们在一起的时候生病了怎么办？直到周二我偏头痛发作打电话给他，他才告诉我他不在家，他说他没法来接他们。所以，苏珊娜，我只能一个人带着他们，还担心自己会感染新冠病毒，病情会很严重。你完全背叛了我的信任……像往常一样，你只把自己放在第一位。”她本来想继续说下去，但我打断了她的话。

‘Johannes, I’m unclear why you’re in Sussex?’ I asked, hoping he could hear me across the flickering screen.

“约翰内斯，我不明白你为什么会在苏塞克斯？”我问道，希望他能透过闪烁的屏幕听到我的话。

‘I needed to be with Liz.’

“我需要和莉兹在一起。”

‘What the fuck does that mean?’ Gabrielle interrupted. ‘Why? Why do you need to be with her and not your children?’

“这他妈什么意思？”加布里埃尔打断道，“为什么？为什么你非要和她在一起，而不是和你的孩子们在一起？”

There was a silence.

一片寂静。

‘Are you still there, Johannes?’ I asked.

“约翰内斯，你还在吗？”我问道。

‘Yes, yes, I’m here. Look, Gabs, it seems obvious to get the kids out of London – London is where all the virus is. I think they would be safer here with me. It’s only for a few weeks, you don’t even have a garden and here they can have lots of space and enjoy the weather—’

“是啊，是啊，我在这儿。你看，盖布斯，把孩子们带离伦敦是显而易见的——病毒都集中在伦敦。我觉得他们跟我在一起更安全。就几个星期而已，你家连个花园都没有，而在这里他们有足够的空间，还能享受好天气——”

A storm erupted at these words – one that overtook the rest of the session and that I couldn’t calm. Both were angry. Johannes believed that Gabrielle was deliberately misunderstanding his intentions, whilst she was incandescent and, I suspected, very fearful that he would somehow win this argument. The only good thing that came from the session was the agreement to have another session three days later.

这些话犹如晴天霹雳，引发了一场轩然大波——这场风暴席卷了接下来的会谈，我根本无法平息。两人都非常愤怒。约翰内斯认为加布里埃尔故意误解了他的意图，而她则怒不可遏，我怀疑她非常害怕他会在这场争论中占上风。这次会谈唯一的好处就是他们约定三天后再进行一次会谈。

Things were calmer when we Zoomed again. Johannes had driven back to London after the previous session and for the last two nights the children had been with him at his London flat. They were now watching TV in the next room whilst I tried to help their parents come to some agreement about their care.

我们再次视频通话时，气氛平静了下来。约翰内斯上次通话结束后开车回了伦敦，孩子们过去两晚都和他待在他伦敦的公寓里。现在，孩子们正在隔壁房间看电视，而我则试图帮助他们的父母就孩子的监护问题达成一致。

‘Gabs, it just doesn’t make any sense for me to stay in London or for the children to. Liz has a lovely cottage, not far from the sea; they’ve got their own rooms and it’s much more sensible for the children. And safer. If you were putting the children first, and thinking about what was best for them, you’d be happy for them to go.’

“盖布斯，我和孩子们留在伦敦都毫无意义。莉兹有一栋漂亮的乡村小屋，离海边不远；他们有自己的房间，这对孩子们来说更合理，也更安全。如果你真的把孩子放在第一位，真心为他们着想，你就应该乐意让他们离开。”

He went on in this vein for several minutes and, despite the reasonableness of his tone, I could see that Gabrielle was getting more and more distressed at the thought of her children ensconced in this dream cottage with Johannes and Liz.

他这样说了好几分钟，尽管他的语气很合情理，但我能看出，一想到自己的孩子和约翰内斯、莉兹一起住在这间梦幻小屋里，加布里埃尔就越来越焦虑不安。

Her voice was clipped and deliberate when she spoke. ‘J, you know, I’ve known you forever. This isn’t about the children – you know it and I know it.’ Then she addressed me. ‘It’s because he can’t be away from his bloody girlfriend. And that’s fine but we’re in the middle of a fucking pandemic for fuck’s sake. Can’t you just do without your daily fuck for a few weeks?!’

她说话时语气简短而坚定。“J，你知道，我认识你很久了。这跟孩子没关系——你我都清楚。”然后她转向我。“是因为他离不开他那该死的女朋友。这没问题，但我们现在他妈的正处于疫情期间。你就不能停几周，别天天跟她上床吗？！”

The next few minutes were a storm of accusations and insults as they shouted and bitched at each other like in the bad old days – the intensity of their anger seemed greater than ever, as though the screen protected them and they could really let rip. I leant forward into the camera. ‘OK. OK! Let’s just calm down. Johannes! Gabrielle! Please!’ But Gabrielle was in full flight and wouldn’t be stopped.

接下来的几分钟，他们像以前那样互相指责、谩骂，简直像一场风暴——他们的愤怒似乎比以往任何时候都更加强烈，仿佛屏幕保护了他们，让他们可以肆无忌惮地发泄。我凑近镜头说：“好了好了！冷静点！约翰内斯！加布里埃尔！拜托！”但加布里埃尔已经完全爆发了，根本停不下来。

I felt helpless. If they’d been in the room with me, I would, I knew, be able to shut them up. The force of my authority and their sense of propriety would have brought some order but here on Zoom, I just couldn’t get through. I sat back in my chair, defeated.

我感到无能为力。我知道，如果他们和我身处同一房间，我一定能让他们闭嘴。我的权威和他们的礼仪本可以带来一些秩序，但在这里通过Zoom，我却无能为力。我颓然地靠在椅背上。

‘And if I get ill, who’ll look after the children? Who’s going to help me with the children if you’ve swanned off to Suffolk with her?’

“如果我生病了，谁来照顾孩子？如果你和她一起溜到萨福克去了，谁来帮我照顾孩子？”

‘Not Suffolk! Sussex! Are you deaf as well as stupid?’

“不是萨福克！是苏塞克斯！你又聋又蠢吗？”

And it went around and around. All my usual compromises weren’t, in this situation, going to work. The Covid restrictions forbade travelling but Johannes was determined to go back to Sussex the following day and he continued to threaten to take the children with him. We were getting nowhere and I found myself uncertain about what was best. Everyone knew that London was at the epicentre of the coronavirus and was Gabrielle’s small, gardenless flat going to be the best option? Perhaps they would be better off in the countryside? I could see that the rural idyll he was describing could be good for the children but I also knew that Mia and Nathan would find it very difficult to be separated from their mother for weeks on end. I felt torn and I still couldn’t quite understand why Johannes was so determined to break lockdown to go to Liz’s.

事情就这样反反复复地纠缠下去。我平时那些妥协的办法，在这种情况下都不管用了。新冠疫情的限制措施禁止出行，但约翰内斯执意第二天就要回苏塞克斯，他还不断威胁要带孩子们一起走。我们毫无进展，我开始犹豫不决，不知道什么才是最好的选择。大家都知道伦敦是新冠疫情的中心，加布里埃尔那间没有花园的小公寓真的是最佳选择吗？或许他们搬到乡下会更好？我能理解他描述的田园生活对孩子们有好处，但我也知道米娅和内森要和妈妈分开好几个星期会非常难熬。我左右为难，仍然不明白约翰内斯为什么如此执意要违反封锁规定去莉兹家。

The session ended with a tenuous agreement from Johannes that he would stay put for the next week but he wouldn’t give any assurances beyond that.

会议结束时，约翰内斯勉强同意下周留守，但除此之外，他没有做出任何保证。

It was a long day of Zoom sessions before I finally shut my laptop to head downstairs to make dinner. I was pouring myself a large gin and tonic when my phone dinged – it was a text from Johannes.

一整天都在开Zoom会议，直到我终于关掉笔记本电脑下楼做晚饭。我正给自己倒了一大杯金汤力，这时手机响了——是约翰内斯发来的短信。

Hi Susanna, sorry to bother you but could I call you tomorrow? I HAVE to get back to Sussex – Liz is five months pregnant and not doing very well. I need to find a way to be straight about it with Gabs. J

嗨，苏珊娜，不好意思打扰你，但我明天可以给你打电话吗？我必须回苏塞克斯——莉兹怀孕五个月了，身体状况不太好。我得想个办法跟盖布坦白这件事。J

Now it made sense. I put on some water for the pasta and peeled onions and thought about what to do next. Both Johannes and Gabrielle had their fragilities and were easily triggered by fears of losing the children and being controlled by each other. It was a toxic mix of feelings that produced storms of overwhelming emotion, where neither could think calmly. A new baby in the middle of a pandemic wasn’t going to make things any easier. Gabrielle was going to test Johannes on his loyalty to her and the children; the danger was that, rather than reassuring her, he would feel oppressed by this and get angry. Gabrielle’s own childhood was also likely to compound the already tense situation, I knew she liked Liz but the idea of her children now being part of a brand new family, from which she was excluded, was going to echo her own experience and make it hard for her to cope with. As I crushed garlic and sipped my drink, I began to feel quite pessimistic that they’d get through lockdown without another falling-out.

现在我明白了。我烧了些水准备煮意面，剥了洋葱，琢磨着下一步该怎么办。约翰内斯和加布里埃尔都有各自的弱点，都很容易被失去孩子和被对方控制的恐惧所激怒。这种复杂的情绪交织在一起，如同风暴般席卷而来，令两人都无法冷静思考。疫情期间又添了个新生儿，更是雪上加霜。加布里埃尔肯定会考验约翰内斯对她和孩子们的忠诚；危险在于，他非但不会安抚她，反而会因此感到压抑和愤怒。加布里埃尔的童年经历也可能加剧本已紧张的局面。我知道她喜欢莉兹，但想到孩子们现在要加入一个全新的家庭，而她却被排除在外，这会让她想起自己的童年，让她难以承受。我一边捣碎大蒜，一边啜饮着饮料，开始感到悲观，觉得他们恐怕很难在封锁期间避免再次争吵。

New partners and new babies are extremely challenging events for separated parents, activating competitive feeling states that can make empathy and concern almost impossible. As infants, we are hardwired to protest when there is any potential threat that might come between us and our parent, and that protest is often louder when a child already has a feeling of insecurity. That’s why children nearly always have ambivalent feelings when a new sibling arrives, uncertain whether this is a delightful new playmate or someone who will steal the food of parental love from their mouths. Human parenting is equally instinctive, often driven by biological impulses. If we feel our children are threatened or our connection to them is at risk, we react strongly. If our own childhood was insecure, we may be particularly alert to these threats and when we feel there is jeopardy, our emotional responses may be more reactive than considered. I knew all this but how would I help Gabrielle and Johannes through this storm?

对于离异父母来说，新的伴侣和新生儿都是极具挑战性的事件，会激发他们内心的竞争情绪，使他们几乎无法产生同理心和关怀。婴儿时期，我们天生就会对任何可能阻碍我们与父母关系的潜在威胁做出抗议，而当孩子本身就缺乏安全感时，这种抗议往往会更加强烈。这就是为什么当新弟弟妹妹到来时，孩子们几乎总是会感到矛盾，他们不确定这究竟是令人愉快的玩伴，还是会抢走父母爱的“食物”。人类的养育行为同样出于本能，常常受到生物本能的驱使。如果我们感到孩子受到威胁，或者我们与孩子之间的联系面临风险，我们就会做出强烈的反应。如果我们自己的童年缺乏安全感，我们可能会对这些威胁格外敏感，一旦感到危险，我们的情绪反应可能会过于冲动，而缺乏深思熟虑。我明白这一切，但我该如何帮助加布里埃尔和约翰内斯度过这场风暴呢？

I feared they would fight as if their lives depended on it. Gabrielle would hold the children close and Johannes would react to this by becoming controlling and aggressive, which would then confirm Gabrielle’s worst fears. I’d seen them play out this dynamic on numerous occasions and here it was again. They were gridlocked in lockdown and it was going to take time and work to unlock all these entangled feelings.

我担心他们会像拼命一样争吵。加布里埃尔会紧紧抱着孩子们，而约翰内斯则会变得控制欲强、咄咄逼人，这只会印证加布里埃尔最担心的事。我见过他们无数次上演这种局面，而现在又重演了。他们被困在封锁之中，想要解开这些纠缠不清的情感，需要时间和努力。

I was having trouble with my back and I blamed Zoom. There was something about staring into a screen that was creating problems in my neck, probably because I was constantly craning forward to get closer to my patients. Sessions with Johannes and Gabrielle had continued intermittently through the early summer and I felt grumbly and frustrated with how regressed they both seemed – petty and vindictive. Gabrielle had taken Liz’s pregnancy quite well on the surface but now a row had broken out about whether Nathan should start school in September or not.

我的背一直不舒服，我把这归咎于Zoom。盯着屏幕看似乎让我的脖子很不舒服，可能是因为我总是向前倾着身子想靠近我的病人。初夏时节，我和约翰内斯以及加布里埃尔的会诊断断续续地进行着，他们俩的态度都让我感到很沮丧和恼火——他们显得斤斤计较，还心怀怨恨。加布里埃尔表面上对莉兹怀孕这件事表现得还算平静，但现在却因为内森九月份是否应该上学而爆发了争吵。

‘Nathan won’t cope with starting school under these circumstances; it’s selfish of you to want to send him. Once again, Gabs, this is all about you and what you want and not about him. How is a little boy with his needs going to cope with teachers in masks and parents who aren’t allowed into the school? The whole thing is fucking ridiculous.’ Johannes was on a roll and I raised a hand and my voice to stop him.

“在这种情况下，内森根本无法适应上学；你想送他去上学真是太自私了。加布斯，你又一次只顾着自己，只想着自己，根本不考虑他。一个有特殊需求的小男孩，怎么可能适应老师戴着口罩、家长又不能进校的情况？这简直太荒谬了！”约翰内斯滔滔不绝地说着，我抬起手，大声制止了他。

‘You don’t believe in him anymore,’ Gabrielle said, shaking her head in disgust. ‘You’re treating him with no respect. He wants to go. He’s been looking forward to this for a long, long time. I, I …’ she struggled for words. ‘I think you’ve written him off, as though because he’s autistic it doesn’t really matter if he goes to school at all. I’ve sorted everything out. Got Islington to ensure he’s got a helper; spoken to his class teacher; Zoomed the head three times. What the fuck have you done? And now, you want to stop him going … Fuck YOU!’

“你不再相信他了，”加布里埃尔厌恶地摇着头说，“你对他一点都不尊重。他想去上学。他盼这一天盼了很久很久了。我，我……”她一时语塞，“我觉得你已经放弃他了，好像因为他是自闭症患者，他去不去上学都无所谓似的。我已经安排好了一切。我让伊斯灵顿学区确保给他安排了辅导员；我跟他的班主任谈过了；我还跟校长视频通话了三次。你到底做了什么？现在，你竟然想阻止他去上学……去你的！”

It went on like this, session after session. Moments of accord wouldn’t hold and I feared that they were heading back to court – though over what exactly wasn’t clear. Then, two weeks later, there was a breakthrough. And it was all down to Mia.

事情就这样一轮又一轮地持续下去。短暂的和解总是无法维持，我担心他们又要对簿公堂——尽管究竟是什么事还不清楚。两周后，事情有了突破性进展。而这一切都要归功于米娅。

They’d been doing a handover of the children in Highgate Wood and they’d begun to argue. Meanwhile, Mia had fallen over in the toddler playground. Neither of them noticed and another parent had picked her up and, unaware of who she belonged to, carried her crying and bleeding to the café to find the park keepers. Finally noticing Mia had vanished, Johannes and Gabrielle had become frantic and ran about the woods dragging Nathan with them. By the time they located her, Mia was in such a state that it took hours to soothe her. And now Mia, who’d recently come out of nappies, had regressed and was peeing and pooing her pants, which alarmed them both.

他们当时正在海格特伍德公园交接孩子，结果开始争吵。与此同时，米娅在幼儿游乐场摔倒了。他们俩都没注意到，另一位家长抱起了她，却不知道她是谁的，就抱着哭闹流血的米娅去了咖啡馆找公园管理员。约翰内斯和加布里埃尔终于发现米娅不见了，顿时慌了神，拉着内森在树林里四处寻找。等他们找到米娅时，她已经哭闹不止，花了几个小时才安抚好她。而现在，米娅——她最近才摆脱尿布——又出现了退步，开始尿裤子拉裤子，这让他们俩都非常担心。

‘I can see you both still feel very shocked and upset. It must have been dreadful. Really frightening.’ Shame and guilt animated their faces but I didn’t want to name it. I wanted them to.

“我看得出来你们俩仍然很震惊，也很难过。那一定很可怕，非常吓人。”他们的脸上写满了羞愧和内疚，但我不想说出来，我想让他们自己说出来。

They both nodded. And it was silent for some time. Then Gabrielle spoke.

两人都点了点头。沉默了一会儿。然后加布里埃尔开口说话了。

‘It’s got to stop. I know we’ve got to stop. I don’t want to hurt the kids. That’s why I’ve kept agreeing to sessions with you, Susanna. Look Jo, whatever you want. If you don’t want Nathan to start in September. Fine. Whatever. We just have to be on the same page. I can’t go on with these arguments anymore. It’s killing me and we’re letting them down.’

“必须停止了。我知道我们必须停止。我不想伤害孩子们。所以我才一直答应和你一起上课，苏珊娜。听着，乔，你想怎样都行。如果你不想让内森九月份开始上课，那也行。随便你。我们必须达成共识。我不能再这样争吵下去了。这让我很痛苦，我们也让他们失望了。”

I saw then that Johannes looked tearful and tormented. And then I felt tearful. Gabrielle had moved me; her passion and regret seeped through Zoom and right into my body. Then Johannes began to speak, slowly, haltingly.

我看到约翰内斯眼含泪水，痛苦万分。我也跟着热泪盈眶。加布里埃尔的话深深打动了我；她的热情和悔恨透过Zoom屏幕，直抵我的内心。然后，约翰内斯开始说话，声音缓慢而断断续续。

‘It’s not been you, Gabs; it’s been … mostly me. I’ve been angry with you. Fucked up about Nathan. And about us. About leaving. I’m sorry. I’m sorry.’

“不是你的错，盖布斯；主要是……我的错。我一直生你的气。因为内森的事，也因为我们俩的事，还有离开的事，我都感到很沮丧。对不起，对不起。”

And then both of them were crying.

然后他们俩都哭了。

‘You’ve both been feeling so guilty about the break-up for so long,’ I began, ‘and it’s been painful to own this guilt. Perhaps because it stems, I think, from a feeling that you’ve done something very destructive by separating. And then you’ve both tried to get rid of that awful feeling of guilt by pushing it away and forcing the blame onto each other. Perhaps now it can stop? Perhaps now you can try to bear your own guilt. Own it, work it through and stop blaming.’ I paused. ‘If you don’t, then the feelings of guilt will escalate because the anger between you creates a sense that you are destructive. The anger makes you, as we’ve just been hearing, forget the children’s needs. Guilt, anger, blame. Guilt, anger, blame. It’s a cycle – and I think you’re ready to make it stop.’

“你们俩都为分手这件事感到内疚很久了，”我开口说道，“承认这种内疚感很痛苦。我想，这或许是因为你们都觉得分手是一件非常伤人的事。然后你们都试图摆脱这种可怕的内疚感，把它推开，互相指责。也许现在一切都可以结束了？也许现在你们可以试着承担自己的内疚。正视它，努力克服它，停止互相指责。”我停顿了一下。“如果你们不这样做，内疚感就会加剧，因为你们之间的愤怒会让人觉得你们都是在伤害对方。正如我们刚才听到的，愤怒会让你们忘记孩子的需求。内疚、愤怒、指责。内疚、愤怒、指责。这是一个恶性循环——我想你们已经准备好打破这个循环了。”

I was quiet then and they were quiet, and it felt, for the first time in a long time, peaceful.

那时我很安静，他们也很安静，很久以来第一次感到如此平静。

# ↩

Kelly Anne Becomes a Wicked Stepmother

凯莉·安妮变成了恶毒的继母

In those early weeks of the first lockdown, every Zoom session confirmed how anxious people were. Even those who said they felt a new kind of freedom away from work, sequestered at home, seemed to me to be somehow disconnected from reality. One man, who said he was ‘loving lockdown’, dreamt he was riding a horse – but its legs came off and he found himself stuck in quicksand. Another patient dreamt of an oven that was frozen inside. And I, still disturbed by my illness, also felt disconnected and confused. All my moorings were gone and I felt I couldn’t connect with my patients across the wavering, uncertain screen. And then along came Darryl and Kelly Anne.

在第一次封城的最初几周，每一次Zoom会议都印证了人们的焦虑。即使是那些声称在家隔离、远离工作、感受到一种全新自由的人，在我看来也似乎与现实脱节。一位自称“喜欢封城”的男士梦见自己骑着马——但马腿断了，他发现自己陷入了流沙。另一位病人梦见烤箱里冻住了。而我，仍然饱受疾病的折磨，也感到与世隔绝、迷茫困惑。所有的依靠都消失了，我感觉无法隔着摇晃不定、充满不确定性的屏幕与我的病人建立联系。就在这时，达里尔和凯莉·安妮出现了。

A central tenet of being a couple therapist is even-handedness and I work hard to manage that tension and to avoid coming down on one side or another. This balance is essential to build trust and I’ve long learnt that although it can look like one partner is much more to blame for the troubles, in reality, couples ‘cook up’ their misery together. But when it came to Darryl and Kelly Anne, I not only found myself taking sides but also acting as jury, judge and executioner.

作为一名婚姻咨询师，我的核心原则之一是保持公正，我努力控制这种紧张关系，避免偏袒任何一方。这种平衡对于建立信任至关重要，我早就明白，虽然表面上看起来一方似乎要为问题承担更多责任，但实际上，夫妻双方共同“炮制”了痛苦。然而，在达里尔和凯莉·安的案例中，我发现自己不仅偏袒一方，还扮演了陪审团、法官和刽子手的角色。

They requested an appointment just as the first lockdown was coming to an end and I postponed beginning with them until early July so I could meet them face to face, back in my central London consulting room. I made extensive preparations, bought disinfectant sprays and gels and shifted the furniture about to get the two-metre distance. Despite now being in possession of coronavirus antibodies, I was returning to Queen Anne Street with some trepidation.

他们预约的时候，正值第一次封城即将结束之际。为了能回到位于伦敦市中心的诊室与他们面对面交流，我把他们的初诊推迟到了七月初。我做了充分的准备，购买了消毒喷雾和凝胶，并重新布置了家具，以确保两米的社交距离。尽管我现在已经拥有了新冠病毒抗体，但回到安妮女王街的诊室，我仍然有些忐忑不安。

Kelly Anne was in her late twenties. She spoke with a strong American twang and was pretty in a slightly plastic, shiny kind of way with short auburn hair and a deep tan. Darryl, in his mid-forties with overgrown, ginger curls and a sandy freckled complexion, spoke in a soft Scottish accent; if it hadn’t been for the wild, lockdown hair, he would have been very handsome. After many weeks of Zoom meetings, it was striking what an impact being body to body in my office felt like. I felt suddenly more alive than I had for months and delighted to be meeting a couple in person.

凯莉·安妮二十七八岁，操着一口浓重的美国腔，长相甜美却略显矫揉造作，一头红棕色的短发，晒成了黝黑的古铜色。达里尔四十多岁，一头姜黄色的卷发蓬乱不堪，肤色呈沙色，还带着些许雀斑，说着一口柔和的苏格兰口音；如果不是因为疫情封锁期间那蓬乱的头发，他本该非常英俊。经过数周的Zoom会议，在办公室里与人面对面交流的感觉真是令人震撼。我突然感觉自己比几个月以来都更有活力，也很高兴能见到这对夫妇本人。

They’d been introduced to each other just over two years ago by a rather exclusive dating agency, set up to service the wealthy in search of love. Their first date took them to Heston Blumenthal’s exclusive restaurant at the Mandarin Oriental in Knightsbridge and that glamorous evening was followed by expensive trips to Paris, Barbados and New York. Both were bruised from failed relationships and they quickly sought comfort from each other and confirmation that their ex-partners were brutes and bullies.

两年前，他们通过一家颇为高端的婚介机构相识，这家机构专门服务于寻求爱情的富豪阶层。他们的第一次约会是在骑士桥文华东方酒店，地点是赫斯顿·布卢门塔尔 (Heston Blumenthal) 的高级餐厅。在那之后，他们又开始了前往巴黎、巴巴多斯和纽约的奢华之旅。两人都曾经历过失败的恋情，伤痕累累，因此他们很快在彼此身上寻求慰藉，并互相确认对方的前任都是些粗暴无礼的恶霸。

This was Darryl’s third marriage. First to Abiba, who now lived in South Africa with their 20-year-old son, and more recently to Breda, with whom he’d had two daughters, Natalie who was eleven and Catherine, eight. In that first consultation, they recounted how awful and mad Breda was and how she was a ‘very bad mother’. Darryl, Kelly Anne explained, had been subject to Breda’s erratic and controlling behaviour for years and, eventually, he’d cracked two years ago and left. It was clear from his stumbling account that he’d found the divorce and financial settlement brutal and, I thought, he was still deeply preoccupied and scarred by the experience.

这是达里尔的第三次婚姻。第一任妻子是阿比芭，她现在和他们20岁的儿子住在南非；最近一次是和布雷达，他们育有两个女儿，分别是11岁的娜塔莉和8岁的凯瑟琳。在第一次咨询中，他们讲述了布雷达有多么可怕、多么疯狂，以及她是一个多么糟糕的母亲。凯莉·安妮解释说，达里尔多年来一直忍受着布雷达反复无常且控制欲极强的行为，最终，两年前他崩溃了，离开了她。从他断断续续的叙述中可以明显看出，他觉得离婚和财产分割非常残酷，而且我认为，他仍然深受这段经历的困扰，伤痕累累。

Then Kelly Anne told me her story, which had many echoes of Darryl’s. She’d been in a relationship with Kyle for three years and, from her graphic account, this man had been a bully, a cheat and a liar.

然后凯莉·安妮跟我讲述了她的故事，其中有很多地方与达里尔的经历相似。她和凯尔交往了三年，从她生动的描述来看，这个男人是个恶霸、骗子和说谎者。

‘I can’t imagine how Kelly Anne stayed with that man for that long,’ Darryl told me, taking over her narrative. ‘Frankly, he robbed her blind, refused to leave her apartment and stole her car.’

“我真无法想象凯莉·安是怎么跟那个男人待那么久的，”达里尔接过凯莉·安的叙述告诉我，“说实话，他把她洗劫一空，拒绝离开她的公寓，还偷了她的车。”

It appeared that when they’d met, Kelly Anne had been in serious financial difficulties and Darryl had come to the rescue, employing, on her behalf, the best legal team to extricate her ex-partner from her life and her apartment as swiftly as possible. As he spoke, I got a strong sense of how important it was to Darryl that he felt himself to be a kind of hero. I said that it sounded like he’d been a knight in shining armour for Kelly Anne and they both giggled – I could see that this idea appealed to them.

看来他们相遇时，凯莉·安正面临严重的经济困境，达里尔挺身而出，为她聘请了最好的律师团队，尽快将她的前伴侣从她的生活和公寓中驱逐出去。听他讲述，我强烈地感受到达里尔非常在意自己是否觉得自己是个英雄。我说，听起来他就像凯莉·安的白马王子，他们俩都咯咯地笑了起来——我看得出来，他们很喜欢这个比喻。

They’d bonded over their difficulties, sharing their outrage at the legal shenanigans of their respective exes. Darryl’s decree absolute had arrived in July, and they wasted no time planning for their wedding. They’d married late summer at the Villa Cimbrone in Ravello, a place I knew fleetingly from my own travels to be both wildly romantic and wildly expensive.

他们因共同的困境而惺惺相惜，共同愤慨于各自前任的法律伎俩。达里尔的离婚判决书在七月送达，他们立即着手筹备婚礼。他们在夏末于拉韦洛的辛布罗内别墅举行了婚礼。我曾在旅行中匆匆路过那里，只觉得那里既浪漫至极，又极其昂贵。

As the minutes ticked past, I began to wonder why they’d come. Everything I was hearing seemed to suggest that whilst their previous partners had been the source of much trouble for them, they were golden. And they’d been married less than a year.

随着时间一分一秒地过去，我开始琢磨他们来干什么。我听到的一切都表明，虽然他们之前的伴侣给他们带来了很多麻烦，但他们现在过得非常幸福。而且他们结婚还不到一年。

Kelly Anne looked at Darryl. ‘Tell her why we’ve come – you explain,’ she instructed. He lifted his hands and spread them in a gesture of helplessness and resignation.

凯莉·安妮看着达里尔。“告诉她我们为什么来——你来解释，”她吩咐道。他举起双手，摊开，做出无助和无奈的姿态。

‘Well, you know, er, what with lockdown and everything, my wife, I mean my ex-wife, wasn’t coping er … so, er … well, she said that er … Natalie and Cathy needed to come and stay with us …’ He paused and glanced anxiously at Kelly Anne. ‘And, erm … Kelly Anne felt that Cathy was fine but Natalie …’

“嗯，你知道，呃，因为封城什么的，我老婆，我是说我前妻，有点应付不来……呃……所以，呃……她说……娜塔莉和凯茜需要过来和我们住一段时间……”他停顿了一下，焦虑地看了凯莉·安一眼。“而且，呃……凯莉·安觉得凯茜没事，但是娜塔莉……”

He ground to a halt and Kelly Anne shot him an angry look. ‘It wasn’t me who said that. I didn’t say she couldn’t come. She doesn’t want to come. She hates me!’ she concluded emphatically.

他猛地停住脚步，凯莉·安妮怒视着他。“那话不是我说的。我没说她不能来。是她不想来。她恨我！”她斩钉截铁地说道。

I had a sense, then, of where the problem was and how tricky this was going to be. Darryl flinched at Kelly Anne’s tone and looked down, waiting for her to finish.

那时我就隐约感觉到问题出在哪里，也意识到这件事有多么棘手。达里尔被凯莉·安的语气吓了一跳，低下头，等着她说完。

‘She hates you?’ I asked, picking up her last words and hoping to hear more. But both were quiet now and I felt they were telling me that this topic was just too dangerous to explore.

“她恨你？”我问道，回想起她最后说的话，希望能听到更多。但两人都沉默了，我感觉她们在告诉我，这个话题太过危险，不宜深究。

‘I can see this is very distressing to talk about. It’s hard to come up against such a difficulty between you, so soon after getting married.’

“我知道这件事让你很难过。结婚不久就遇到这样的问题，确实令人难过。”

Both nodded but somehow the rest of the session passed without any further discussion of Darryl’s daughters and soon they were leaving my office and I was still none the wiser.

两人都点了点头，但不知何故，接下来的会议时间里，他们再也没有讨论过达里尔的女儿们，很快他们就离开了我的办公室，而我仍然一无所知。

It was late July before I saw them again, I’d taken a much-needed short break in Cornwall. Despite the crowds let loose from lockdown, it was revitalising and I returned to Queen Anne Street with a growing sense that things were getting back to normal. Most of my patients, however, were still on Zoom, reluctant to make the journey into central London, so I looked forward to having an in-person session with Darryl and Kelly Anne – it would be a welcome change.

直到七月下旬我才再次见到他们，之前我在康沃尔郡度过了一段急需的短暂假期。尽管疫情封锁结束后人潮涌动，但那里的氛围令人精神焕发，我回到安妮女王街时，越来越觉得一切都在慢慢恢复正常。然而，我的大多数病人仍然通过Zoom进行线上问诊，不愿前往伦敦市中心，所以我很期待能和达里尔以及凯莉·安妮进行一次面对面的会诊——这将是一个令人欣喜的改变。

They arrived with a great flurry. Kelly Anne had been shopping and was toting several chic, glossy carrier bags, which Darryl relieved her of, placing them like a barrier on the carpet between us. They looked uncomfortable on my plastic-covered sofa and I noticed they’d sat further apart from each other today. After some chit-chat they fell silent but it took only a gentle prompting from me for them to pour out the bitter and disappointed feelings that had emerged between them. I’ve worked with many blended families before so it was no surprise to me that the children and Kelly Anne were struggling to build a relationship, but it was a shock to hear the way Kelly Anne talked about Natalie, a girl of just 11 who was, no doubt, still coming to terms with her parents’ divorce. It was very hard not to feel judgemental.

他们匆匆赶来。凯莉·安妮刚买完东西，拎着好几个时髦亮面的购物袋，达里尔帮她接过，把它们像屏障一样放在我们之间的地毯上。他们坐在我那铺着塑料布的沙发上显得很不自在，我注意到他们今天坐得比平时更远了。寒暄了几句后，他们就沉默了，但我稍加引导，他们便倾诉了彼此之间积压的苦涩和失望。我以前接触过很多重组家庭，所以孩子们和凯莉·安妮难以建立关系并不让我感到意外，但听到凯莉·安妮谈论娜塔莉的方式，我还是感到震惊。娜塔莉才11岁，无疑还在努力接受父母离婚的事实。我很难不去评判他们。

In most families, alliances shift and change as the years pass. Brothers and sisters who were close in young childhood find themselves at odds in the teenage years; fathers and sons who were best pals find themselves competing for attention and power. These changes are natural and normal, though often painful, but they come about because of ordinary processes of development within the individuals in the family, as each matures and experiments with new identities. But divorce disrupts these processes and blended families even more so.

在大多数家庭中，随着岁月的流逝，人际关系会发生转变。童年时期亲密无间的兄弟姐妹，到了青少年时期可能会产生矛盾；曾经形影不离的父子，也会为了争夺关注和权力而反目成仇。这些变化虽然往往令人痛苦，但却是自然而然的，也是家庭中个体成长发育的正常过程，每个人都在逐渐成熟，并尝试新的身份认同。然而，离婚会扰乱这些过程，重组家庭的情况则更为严重。

‘She doesn’t like me and I don’t like her,’ she said in a clipped, defensive tone. ‘I won’t be treated with disrespect – it’s not fair on me. And Darryl knows it. I don’t want her coming round, giving me those sly looks and trying to get her daddy on her side. She’s got to learn that things have changed. She can’t have everything her own way.’ Kelly Anne, now in full flow, enumerated all the terrible slights that young Natalie had inflicted on her. She’d never worn the dress that Kelly Anne had bought her; she didn’t help the maid carry the dishes through to the kitchen. And so it went on … and on.

“她不喜欢我，我也不喜欢她，”她语气生硬而防备地说。“我不能容忍这种不尊重——这对我不公平。达里尔也知道这一点。我不想让她再来，用那种狡黠的眼神看着我，想方设法拉拢她爸爸。她必须明白，时代变了。她不能事事都随心所欲。”凯莉·安滔滔不绝地列举了小娜塔莉对她种种恶劣的冒犯。她从来没穿过凯莉·安给她买的裙子；她也没有帮女佣把碗碟端到厨房。诸如此类，没完没了。

‘The trouble is, she can twist Darryl round her little finger and he just never says no. I see her manipulating you, honey. You can’t see it but I can! And I don’t understand why you let her dress like that! Breda doesn’t teach her that you just can’t wear a dirty crop top and some torn old leggings out to dinner. I do feel quite sorry for Natalie, it’s not all her fault. If no one tells her how to behave then it’s no surprise she’s so spoilt.’

“问题是，她能把达里尔玩弄于股掌之间，他从来不会拒绝。亲爱的，我看得出来她在操纵你。你看不出来，但我看得出来！我不明白你为什么让她那样穿！布雷达没教过她，穿脏兮兮的露脐上衣和破旧的打底裤去吃饭是不对的。我挺同情娜塔莉的，这也不能全怪她。如果没人教她该怎么做，她被宠坏也就不奇怪了。”

I expected Darryl to remonstrate with her, to defend his little girl and explain her vulnerability to Kelly Anne. But he didn’t, and he seemed more concerned to pacify Kelly Anne, joining her in her criticism of Natalie.

我原以为达里尔会劝阻她，维护自己的小女儿，并向凯莉·安解释她为何如此脆弱。但他没有，反而似乎更关心安抚凯莉·安，甚至和她一起批评娜塔莉。

‘Don’t blame me, darling. I know she’s difficult. I have as much trouble with her as you. She is very ungrateful. She’s very like her mother and no one can expect you to make it right – but, darling, it’s really not fair to blame me and if you say we can’t have Natalie over then Breda won’t allow poor Cathy to come and we want Cathy to come, don’t we sweetie?’

“别怪我，亲爱的。我知道她很难搞。我跟你一样也觉得她很麻烦。她很忘恩负义。她跟她妈妈很像，谁也不能指望你能把一切都安排妥当——但是，亲爱的，怪我真的很不公平。如果你说我们不能让娜塔莉过来，那布雷达就不会让可怜的凯茜来了，而我们想让凯茜来，对吧，宝贝？”

As I listened to this, my mind went to a piece of research that I had heard several years before at a lecture by two brilliant, married American psychologists, Philip and Carolyn Cowan, both professors at the University of California, Berkeley. In their research, they’d noticed that where a couple were unhappy together, fathers seemed less close to their daughters. The implications were that fathers’ negative feelings about their wives spilled into their relationship with their daughters, as though fathers confused these two relationships in their minds. Was this what was going on with Darryl? Was this why he seemed so down on Natalie?

听着这些，我的思绪回到了几年前在一次讲座上听到的一项研究。当时两位才华横溢的美国心理学家夫妇——菲利普·考恩和卡罗琳·考恩——正在加州大学伯克利分校任教。他们的研究发现，如果夫妻关系不幸福，父亲与女儿的关系似乎也会疏远。这意味着父亲对妻子的负面情绪会蔓延到他们与女儿的关系中，仿佛父亲们把这两种关系混淆了。达里尔的情况是不是就是这样？是不是这就是他为什么对娜塔莉如此冷淡的原因？

As they left, I palmed my face; I felt a strong sense of distaste. This couple seemed so unfeeling and self-centred, and I felt no inclination at all to ask myself why they were like this. I only wanted to protect poor Natalie. They were due to come back next week and I felt relieved that I’d have time to consult with colleagues. I knew I needed help if I was going to be able to work with them.

他们离开时，我捂住了脸，感到一阵强烈的厌恶。这对夫妇看起来如此冷漠自私，我丝毫没有想要探究他们为何如此的念头。我只想保护可怜的娜塔莉。他们下周还要来，我松了口气，终于有时间咨询同事了。我知道，如果想和他们一起工作，我需要帮助。

But I didn’t have time to speak to colleagues. Later that day, I picked up the phone to Kelly Anne who was on the other end, sobbing and screaming simultaneously. I managed to glean through the tears that Darryl had left her and gone back to Breda. She was hysterical and desperate. What should she do? They’d had a big fight, they’d thrown things, she’d pushed him and then walked out, and when she came back home an hour later, he’d left.

但我没时间跟同事们说话。那天晚些时候，我拿起电话，凯莉·安妮在电话那头又哭又叫。我好不容易才从她的泪水中听出，达里尔离开了她，回到了布雷达。她歇斯底里，绝望极了。她该怎么办？他们大吵了一架，摔东西，她推了他一把就走了，一个小时后她回到家，他却已经走了。

‘Why do you think he’s at Breda’s, Kelly Anne?’ I asked and was met with a wail. She didn’t know for sure he was, she’d just assumed. So I suggested to her that perhaps he wasn’t with Breda but simply licking his wounds somewhere. I told her I would see her next week, attempting to instil some sense of a boundary and calm.

“凯莉·安，你觉得他为什么会在布雷达家？”我问，她却嚎啕大哭起来。她并不确定他是否真的在那里，只是猜测而已。于是我建议她，也许他不是在布雷达家，只是在某个地方疗伤。我告诉她下周再见，试图让她明白一些界限，并让她平静下来。

But it was to no avail. I was bombarded by calls and texts all weekend, with Darryl now joining in to tell me his side of the story. He hadn’t gone to Breda at all, he’d been in a hotel around the corner from where they lived in St John’s Wood. She’d attacked him. She’d broken his heart. I could see how hard they were working to have me take sides and, truthfully, I still felt more on his side than hers. Anyone who spoke about an 11-year-old like that must be to blame. I felt caught in the middle between them, so I sent them a joint email and then determined not to respond to any more texts or calls.

但这一切都无济于事。整个周末我都被电话和短信轰炸，达里尔也加入了进来，跟我讲述他的版本。他说他根本没去布雷达，而是在圣约翰伍德他们家附近的一家酒店里。是她袭击了他，伤透了他的心。我能看出他们费尽心思想让我选边站，说实话，我仍然更倾向于他。任何这样谈论一个11岁孩子的人都难辞其咎。我感觉自己夹在他们中间左右为难，于是我给他们发了一封联名邮件，然后决定不再回复任何短信或电话。

Dear Darryl and Kelly Anne,

I’m sorry you’ve been having a difficult time. I will see you at 2.15pm on Tuesday when we can think together about the situation.

Best wishes,

Susanna

亲爱的达里尔和凯莉·安妮，很抱歉你们最近遇到了困难。周二下午2点15分我会和你们见面，到时候我们可以一起想想办法。祝好，苏珊娜

I was thinking about Kelly Anne and Darryl as I walked down Marylebone High Street on the Tuesday, reflecting on my own feelings about them, as all psychoanalytic therapists are trained to do. I knew intellectually that the emotions they stirred up in me could probably help me better understand their inner worlds but I couldn’t get beyond feeling simply irritated and dismissive. I felt a particular distaste for Kelly Anne. How could she be so rejecting of this little girl? There was something unnatural in her lack of maternal feeling for this child. Then I thought how judgemental I was being and how little I really knew about Kelly Anne. Or Darryl, for that matter. Why should Kelly Anne particularly like Natalie? Did I expect her, because she was a woman, to be particularly nurturing? Was my judgement infected by a gender bias?

星期二，我沿着马里波恩大街走着，脑海里浮现出凯莉·安妮和达里尔的身影，反思着自己对他们的感受——就像所有精神分析治疗师受过训练的那样。理智上我知道，他们激起的情绪或许能帮助我更好地理解他们的内心世界，但我却始终无法摆脱那种恼怒和不屑的感觉。我尤其反感凯莉·安妮。她怎么能如此排斥这个小女孩？她对这个孩子缺乏母爱，这很不自然。然后我意识到自己是多么武断，我对凯莉·安妮又是多么的无知。达里尔也是如此。凯莉·安妮为什么会特别喜欢娜塔莉？难道仅仅因为她是女性，我就期望她格外温柔体贴吗？我的判断是否受到了性别偏见的影响？

Musing on this, I realised that their whole thing seemed to be all about taking sides; all about goodies and baddies. Cathy was good. Natalie was bad. Their exes were both clearly unbelievably bad and apparently completely to blame for everything that had gone wrong in their previous relationships. And when it came to them, the same kind of black-and-white, polarised mindset was evident. One minute, Darryl and Kelly Anne were in idealised bliss, then the next it was all over and they were in hell. Was I also guilty of taking sides? I seemed to be treating Darryl as though he was the long-suffering goody, doing his best, whilst I felt Kelly Anne behaved just like a spoilt child.

仔细想想，我意识到他们之间的一切都围绕着站队；一切都围绕着好人和坏人。凯茜是好人，娜塔莉是坏人。他们的前任显然都坏得令人难以置信，而且显然要为之前感情中所有的问题负全责。而当轮到他们自己时，这种非黑即白、极端对立的思维模式也同样明显。前一秒，达里尔和凯莉·安还沉浸在理想化的幸福中，下一秒一切就都结束了，他们仿佛坠入了地狱。我是不是也犯了站队的错误？我似乎把达里尔当成了那个默默忍受、尽力而为的好人，而我觉得凯莉·安就像个被宠坏的孩子。

This kind of splitting into good and bad was something I’d encountered many times before and I knew that behind this way of being, there was probably a lot of suffering inside both of them. As I reached Queen Anne Street, I didn’t like them any better but I’d begun to become a little more curious about them. It would have to do.

这种将人分成好与坏的二元论，我以前也遇到过很多次，我知道在这种表象之下，他们内心深处可能都藏着许多痛苦。走到安妮女王街时，我对他们的好感并没有丝毫减退，但我开始对他们产生了一些好奇。就这样吧。

They seemed a little sheepish as they settled themselves on the crackly plastic of my sofa. Kelly Anne carefully removed her mask, unclipped her handbag and applied lipstick as Darryl began to speak.

他们似乎有些不好意思，在我那张吱吱作响的塑料沙发上坐了下来。达里尔开始说话时，凯莉·安妮小心翼翼地摘下口罩，解开手提包，涂上口红。

‘Well. It’s been a bit up and down since we last saw you.’ He smiled but through the jollity I could see he was uncomfortable. ‘All sorted now though, Susanna. I’m sorry if we put you through it a bit,’ he laughed. ‘We’ve kissed and made up!’

“嗯，自从上次见面以来，我们之间有点波折。”他笑着说，但透过笑容，我看得出他并不自在。“不过现在都解决了，苏珊娜。如果我们让你操心了，我很抱歉。”他笑着说，“我们已经和好如初了！”

I waited but neither of them spoke. Eventually, I said, ‘It seems your relationship can feel absolutely blissful and absolutely unbearable. I imagine these swings of feeling might be quite difficult to cope with.’

我等了一会儿，但他们俩都没说话。最后，我说：“看来你们的关系有时幸福无比，有时又痛苦不堪。我想这种情绪的剧烈波动对你们来说一定很难应对。”

They looked at one another. Kelly Anne shrugged and said, ‘I hate it, it’s like we’re driving each other crazy and Darryl never admits it’s down to him too. He says it’s all me, all my fault. I’m getting all the blame, but he provokes me … Yesterday, when we were supposed to be making dinner together, he spent over an hour on the phone to Natalie, sweet-talking her because she was having a hissy fit. I could hear him promising to take her out on Saturday, when we already have plans to play tennis with friends and …’ She was in full flow now and the more she talked, the angrier she seemed to get. I watched as Darryl became increasingly agitated. His previous jollity evaporated, he frowned and looked away. I could see they were about to descend into something even more destructive, which would get us nowhere, so I interrupted her flow.

他们互相看了看。凯莉·安妮耸了耸肩说：“我讨厌这样，感觉我们俩都快要疯了，达里尔从来不承认他也有错。他说都是我的错，都是我的错。所有的责怪都落在我身上，可是明明是他挑衅我……昨天，我们本来应该一起做晚饭的，他却花了超过一个小时跟娜塔莉打电话，哄她开心，因为她当时正在大发脾气。我都能听到他答应周六带她出去，可我们本来就计划和朋友们一起打网球……”她现在滔滔不绝地说个不停，说得越多，似乎就越生气。我看着达里尔越来越烦躁。他之前的兴致消失殆尽，皱着眉头，把目光移开。我知道他们马上就要陷入更糟糕的境地，那样只会让我们一事无成，所以我打断了她的话。

‘Perhaps it would be helpful to widen the lens,’ I suggested. They looked at me, not understanding. ‘I’ve heard a bit about the current difficulties you’re having but I don’t feel I know much about either of you – I know how you met and a little about your previous relationships but nothing about your family backgrounds. We might be able to think together about what’s at the heart of these upsetting feelings if we understand more about how you grew up?’

“或许拓宽一下视野会有帮助，”我建议道。他们看着我，一脸茫然。“我听说了你们目前遇到的一些困难，但我感觉对你们俩了解不多——我知道你们是怎么认识的，也略知你们之前的感情经历，但对你们的家庭背景却一无所知。如果我们能更多地了解你们的成长经历，或许就能一起思考这些令人难过的情绪究竟源于何处？”

I knew that without more insight into their families I would continue to be lost at sea. I needed to get a sense of what they might be repeating and trying to resolve from their pasts if I was to begin to help them. I thought they might be reluctant to tell me much but Kelly Anne jumped in, saying, ‘I’ll go first.’

我知道，如果不能更深入地了解他们的家庭情况，我将继续迷失方向。如果我想帮助他们，就必须了解他们可能正在重复哪些过往的经历，以及他们试图解决哪些问题。我原以为他们可能不愿多说，但凯莉·安妮却抢先说道：“我先说。”

She told me that when she was small, she’d lived with her mother and grandmother in Kentucky, but at seven, she moved east with her mother, her mother’s new boyfriend and his three children. She liked her stepbrother and kept in touch with him and his wife but she’d never got on with her stepsisters and she’d missed her grandmother a lot.

她告诉我，她小时候和母亲、祖母住在肯塔基州，但七岁时，她和母亲、母亲的新男友以及他的三个孩子搬到了东部。她喜欢她的继兄，并一直和他及他的妻子保持联系，但她和继姐妹们一直相处不来，而且她非常想念祖母。

‘My stepfather was a dictator, a complete control freak. We argued a lot. I left as soon as I could. At 17, I went back to Kentucky to live with my gramma and I went to college. I never went back home. My mom and stepdad were toxic together – they got divorced about ten years ago.’

“我的继父是个独裁者，控制欲极强。我们经常吵架。我一有机会就离开了。17岁那年，我回到肯塔基州和奶奶一起生活，然后上了大学。我再也没回过家。我妈妈和继父的关系很糟糕——他们大约十年前离婚了。”

‘Toxic? In what way?’ I asked. And then she told me that her stepfather had been quite weird. He was ‘phobic’ about everything and when she hit her teenage years, he got more odd and ‘weird’ with her. I looked at her questioningly but it was clear she didn’t want to say any more.

“有毒？哪方面？”我问。然后她告诉我，她的继父很古怪。他对什么都“恐惧”，等她到了青春期，他对她变得更加古怪，更加“怪异”。我疑惑地看着她，但很明显她不想再说下去了。

‘My real dad, he still lives near my gramma’s house and I used to see him on the sidewalk from time to time – he’d wave at me. He was always in a bar and once we had a chat but I think it was mainly so I’d buy him a drink.’ She grunted and sighed and made a dismissive gesture with her hand.

“我的亲生父亲，他现在还住在奶奶家附近，我以前时不时会在人行道上看到他——他会朝我挥手。他总是泡在酒吧里，有一次我们聊了一会儿，但我觉得主要是因为我请他喝酒。”她哼了一声，叹了口气，不耐烦地挥了挥手。

‘You had a lot of disruptions in your childhood, Kelly Anne. It sounds like leaving your grandma was really painful?’

“凯莉·安，你的童年经历了很多波折。听起来离开奶奶对你来说真的很痛苦？”

‘Yeah. She’s the only one of my family I’ve ever really been close to. She’s 90 this year and in a retirement home and since I’ve been in London and what with Covid, I haven’t seen her, not even once …’ And she began to cry, tears slowly sliding down her cheeks. Darryl took her hand; she leant into him and he held her quietly for a moment.

“是啊。她是我家里唯一一个我真正亲近的人。她今年90岁了，住在养老院。自从我来到伦敦，再加上疫情，我就没见过她，一次也没有……”说着说着，她开始哭泣，泪水缓缓滑落脸颊。达里尔握住她的手；她靠向他，他静静地抱着她一会儿。

I didn’t say anything more then but I could sense my feelings towards her shifting because now I could relate to the child part of Kelly Anne and feel how complicated her life had been. As I entered her experience in my mind, I felt myself come alive with connections. How challenging it must have been to go from having your mum and grandma to yourself to suddenly losing one of the most important people in your life. And how hard it must have been for Kelly Anne to share her mum with her new stepfather and three other children. I began to feel more sympathy towards her difficulties with Natalie; maybe sharing Darryl with his children was just too much like a repeat of what she’d had to do in her childhood? We sat in silence as Kelly Anne recovered herself and then I turned to Darryl.

我当时没再说什么，但我能感觉到自己对她的感觉在转变，因为我现在能理解凯莉·安童年时的感受，也能体会到她人生的复杂。当我设身处地地感受她的经历时，我仿佛被某种情感唤醒。从拥有自己的母亲和祖母，到突然失去生命中最重要的人之一，这该是多么艰难的转变啊！凯莉·安要和她的继父以及另外三个孩子分享母亲，这又是多么痛苦。我开始对她和娜塔莉之间的矛盾感同身受；或许，和达里尔的孩子们分享母亲，对她来说就像是重蹈覆辙，让她再次经历童年的痛苦？我们静静地坐着，凯莉·安缓过神来，然后我转向了达里尔。

‘And your family? Can you tell me a little?’

“你的家人呢？能跟我说说吗？”

‘What do you want to know?’ Darryl asked. But I didn’t get a chance to reply because he launched into the story of his life and there was no stopping him. He told me that he’d grown up in Inverness, that his father was a vet and his mother, a nurse. They were very religious and family life revolved round the Church. His mother favoured his older brother who was a star athlete and brilliant at school. His father, on the other hand, had favoured his younger sister, who’d also become a vet and taken over his father’s practice. He said that he always knew that he wasn’t going to get the attention that his brother and sister had but it was OK because he got a lot of freedom. They didn’t really seem to expect much of him and hadn’t complained when he decided to leave school at 16 and join the navy. He talked at length about what a great experience the navy was, how it had helped him to grow up and get the confidence he needed to start a business. Then he launched into his career and detailed his various achievements – the businesses he’d started and sold. He described the clever idea behind his present enterprise and where he was planning to take it. Gradually, I realised that what was happening in the room seemed to mirror the way he’d dealt with his past.

“你想知道什么？”达里尔问道。但我还没来得及回答，他就滔滔不绝地讲述了自己的故事，根本停不下来。他告诉我，他是在因弗内斯长大的，父亲是兽医，母亲是护士。他们非常虔诚，家庭生活也围绕着教会展开。他的母亲更偏爱哥哥，哥哥是运动健将，学习成绩也十分优异。而他的父亲则更宠爱妹妹，妹妹后来也成为了一名兽医，并接管了父亲的诊所。他说，他一直都知道自己不会像哥哥姐姐那样受人瞩目，但这没关系，因为他拥有很大的自由。他们似乎对他并没有抱太大的期望，所以当他16岁辍学参军时，他们也没有抱怨。他详细地讲述了在海军的经历，以及这段经历如何帮助他成长，并让他获得了创业所需的自信。然后他开始讲述自己的职业生涯，详细列举了他取得的各项成就——他创办和出售的公司。他描述了他目前这家公司背后的巧妙构思，以及他计划如何发展这家公司。渐渐地，我意识到房间里发生的一切似乎与他处理过去的方式如出一辙。

‘I notice, Darryl, that you’ve skimmed over your childhood and quickly moved onto when you left home. It sounds that, like Kelly Anne, you had some quite challenging issues in your family and, like Kelly Anne, you got away from them as fast and as soon as you could. And now, here, talking to me, you’ve got away from thinking about the past as quickly as possible.’

“达里尔，我注意到你对童年一带而过，很快就谈到了离家之后的事情。听起来，你和凯莉·安一样，家庭里也存在一些相当棘手的问题，而且你也和凯莉·安一样，尽快地逃离了这些问题。现在，在这里和我聊天，你又尽可能快地逃避了对过去的思考。”

He looked curious but said nothing, so I continued. ‘Do you mind if we go back to your childhood, just for a bit? I feel I’ve only got a glimpse. How did your parents get on, for instance?’

他看起来很好奇，但什么也没说，所以我继续说道：“你介意我们稍微聊聊你的童年吗？我觉得我对你的童年了解甚少。比如说，你的父母相处得怎么样？”

‘Oh Jesus,’ he laughed. ‘They hated each other. They couldn’t even stand to be in the same room. They shouldn’t have stayed together but, you know, they were really into the Church, so …’ He shrugged, lifting his shoulders in resignation. ‘My sister spent all her time with Dad and Mum was always with Douglas, my brother. Me? I stayed out of it. No one bothered me if I stayed out of the way.’

“哦，我的天哪，”他笑着说。“他们互相憎恨，甚至连待在同一个房间里都受不了。他们本不该住在一起，但你知道，他们都非常虔诚，所以……”他耸了耸肩，无奈地抬起肩膀。“我姐姐整天和爸爸在一起，妈妈则总是和我弟弟道格拉斯在一起。至于我？我置身事外。只要我不插手，就没人会来烦我。”

‘You talk as if it were a breeze, as if this situation was actually good for you. But I wonder if somewhere you felt then, and perhaps can still do at times, quite neglected, left out?’

“你说的好像一切都轻而易举，好像这种情况对你来说反而是好事。但我很好奇，你是否在当时，或许现在有时仍然会感到，自己被忽视、被冷落？”

‘Maybe …’ he said politely but I could see he wasn’t interested in delving deeper.

“也许吧……”他礼貌地说，但我看得出来他并不想深入探讨。

Despite that, I continued. ‘Do you think that this feeling of not getting enough attention is one you both share? From what I heard, it sounds like Kelly Anne might have found it quite difficult to suddenly have to share her mother with a new stepfather and new step-siblings. And you, Darryl, you sound like you never felt you came first. It makes me wonder if some of the arguments about Natalie are because the two of you are finding it hard to share each other. You’ve only been together a short while and straight away you have to make room in your relationship for Natalie and Cathy. Maybe, Kelly Anne, it feels a bit too early to share Darryl with his children?’

尽管如此，我还是继续说道：“你觉得你们俩都有这种感觉，觉得没有得到足够的关注吗？我听到的好像是，凯莉·安突然要和新继父以及新继兄弟姐妹分享母亲，这让她很难接受。而你，达里尔，听起来你好像从来没觉得自己是第一位的。这让我不禁怀疑，你们之间关于娜塔莉的争吵是不是因为你们难以接受彼此的存在。你们在一起的时间还不长，就得立刻在你们的关系中为娜塔莉和凯西腾出空间。凯莉·安，也许现在就让达里尔和他的孩子们分享他，还为时过早吧？”

They looked at each other and nodded and for a beat I thought we’d got somewhere, and this was a beginning. But a moment later, Darryl seemed to shake me off and said dismissively, ‘Oh, I don’t think either of us find sharing hard. We’re both big givers, you know!’ And he laughed and patted Kelly Anne’s hand, telling her it was time to go.

他们互相看了看，点了点头。那一刻，我以为我们终于有了进展，这或许是个好的开始。但片刻之后，达里尔似乎甩开了我，漫不经心地说：“哦，我觉得我们俩都不觉得分享难。我们俩都乐于付出，你知道的！”说完，他笑着拍了拍凯莉·安的手，示意她该走了。

After they left, I tried to put the pieces together. I could see that, on the surface, both had adopted a rather dismissive, ‘who gives a shit’ kind of persona. It was a brittle, hard shell around them and my attempts to get through it had been mostly without success. But both had described childhoods in which they’d been deprived of attention and I also thought that, perhaps, there was something darker lurking in Kelly Anne’s experience that she’d shied away from talking about.

他们走后，我试图把事情拼凑起来。我发现，表面上看，他们俩都摆出一副漠不关心、毫不在乎的样子。他们仿佛被一层坚硬的外壳包裹着，我试图走进去，但大多都以失败告终。不过，他们都提到过童年时期缺乏关爱，我也觉得，或许凯莉·安妮的经历中还隐藏着一些更黑暗的秘密，是她一直不愿提及的。

Could it be that closeness between fathers or father figures and daughters was stirring up something quite alarming for her? Was that why she was so hostile to the relationship between Darryl and his elder daughter? Was her concern about the way Natalie dressed also a clue? Something about Natalie’s emerging sexuality was clearly bothering her.

难道是父亲或父亲般的人物与女儿之间的亲密关系在她心中激起了某种不安？这是否就是她如此敌视达里尔和他大女儿关系的原因？她对娜塔莉穿着打扮的担忧是否也暗示着什么？娜塔莉逐渐萌发的性意识显然让她感到困扰。

I also wondered about his experience of always being left out in the family and how, now, that was exactly the experience that Kelly Anne was having with his daughters. Was he projecting his own competitive feelings into Kelly Anne? All the currents of their past lives, all their many fears and fantasies were driving the present difficulties between them. These unresolved issues had drawn this couple together and now these same things were driving them apart.

我也一直在想，他过去总是被家人冷落的经历，如今却恰恰成了凯莉·安与他女儿们相处时的感受。他是不是把自己的竞争心理投射到了凯莉·安身上？他们过往生活中的种种纠葛，他们各自的恐惧和幻想，都在加剧着他们之间的矛盾。正是这些未解的心结将他们紧紧联系在一起，而如今，正是这些矛盾将他们推向了分崩离析的边缘。

But I never got to find out if any of my speculations were, in any way, valid. They didn’t turn up the following week, and when I contacted them to find out why, Kelly Anne said they’d split up again. I wrote back, encouraging them to come and explore whether this was what they really wanted. I heard nothing for three weeks and then I got a brief text from Darryl saying they’d started divorce proceedings – so thank you, but no thanks.

但我始终没能验证我的任何猜测是否属实。他们下周没来，我联系他们询问原因，凯莉·安妮说他们又分手了。我回信鼓励他们过来好好谈谈，看看这是否真的是他们想要的。之后三个星期杳无音信，然后我收到达里尔的一条简短短信，说他们已经开始办理离婚手续了——所以，谢谢，但我还是算了。

I think Darryl and Kelly Anne’s difficulties probably ran quite deep but if they’d been able to stay the course, I think I might have helped them. Their marriage seemed to have been about an escape – from their previous relationships and from the pain of their pasts. They’d got together in a whirl, creating an illusion that everything could be left behind and nothing painful needed to be confronted and mourned.

我认为达里尔和凯莉·安的困境可能很深，但如果他们能坚持下去，或许我能帮到他们。他们的婚姻似乎是一种逃避——逃离之前的感情经历，逃离过去的痛苦。他们匆匆走到一起，营造出一种幻觉，仿佛一切都可以抛诸脑后，无需面对和哀悼任何痛苦。

Making changes and facing the ghosts that haunt and shape our lives is hard to do and most of us find ways not to look too deep. It seems we prefer to swipe right, get a new lover, have a drink, buy a new dress or simply turn a blind eye. Our society encourages us to move fast because moving slow costs money. Even our NHS mental health services love a quick CBT ‘fix’ despite its abject failure to ‘fix’ many people at all. Instead, patients go round and round and round the system, seeking desperately for something that short-term therapy can’t provide.

做出改变，直面那些萦绕在我们心头、塑造我们生活的阴影，并非易事，大多数人都会想方设法逃避深入探究。我们似乎更倾向于在交友软件上右滑、寻找新的恋人、小酌一杯、买件新衣服，或者干脆视而不见。我们的社会鼓励我们快速行动，因为行动缓慢需要付出代价。即使是英国国民医疗服务体系（NHS）的心理健康服务，也热衷于提供快速的认知行为疗法（CBT）“解决方案”，尽管这种疗法对许多人根本无效。相反，患者们在医疗系统中兜兜转转，苦苦寻求短期疗法无法提供的东西。

From childhood, Kelly Anne and Darryl had found a way to deal with their hurt and pain: they simply moved on. And now they were doing it again, moving on from each other and from me. And, without a backward glance, that was that.

从孩提时代起，凯莉·安妮和达里尔就找到了应对伤痛的方法：他们只是继续生活。而现在，他们又一次这样做了，他们要离开彼此，也要离开我。头也不回，一切就此结束。
